title: ATS vendor
content:
# ATS vendor

The platform the funnel runs inside. Writes no policy and decides no hire, yet its defaults decide what a great many people ever see.
summary: The platform the funnel runs inside. Writes no policy and decides no hire, yet its defaults decide what a great many people ever see.
controls: What the parser can extract, and what it silently drops
Which knockout rules a customer can configure, and which are on by default
What the ranking model reads as a feature
When an unreviewed application expires, and what it emails when it does
blind_to: Whether a rule its customer configured is lawful, reasonable or even intended
What happened to a candidate outside the platform
Whether the profile it scored 12/100 was unreadable rather than unqualified
incentives: Throughput and customer-visible efficiency, which are what the buyer evaluates
Feature parity with competitors, including features with known disparate effects
Defaults that reduce customer support load, not candidate confusion

specimens.label: A default nobody chose

lines.text: Setting: auto_expire_unreviewed · Default: enabled · Threshold: 60 days
Setting: employment_gap_penalty · Default: enabled
Both ship on. Turning them off is a customer action nobody is prompted to take.

specimens.reading: Two lines of default configuration account for several mechanisms in this registry and one of its three reinforcing loops.

recommendations.title: Remove employment continuity from the ranking feature set
recommendations.rationale: The feature set of the ranking model is written by the vendor, not configured per customer, so continuity is one of the few inputs here that no buyer has to agree to remove. While it stays in the set, a break in employment lowers the rank, a lower rank returns fewer interviews, and the next application carries a longer break.
recommendations.costs: Every threshold customers tuned against the old score distribution shifts, and the field stays on competitors' feature lists after it leaves this one.

recommendations.title: Stop scoring files the parser could not read
recommendations.rationale: A file whose work history was lost in extraction and a file with no relevant work history reach the ranker as the same low number, and nothing downstream separates them. The extraction score is already computed, so routing anything below its threshold into a hold state rather than into the ranking is a change inside the pipeline the vendor owns.
recommendations.costs: The hold state is work that lands on customers with nobody assigned to it, and the share of applications the platform disposes of without a person — a number the buyer is shown — falls.

recommendations.title: Show the applicant the record the parser stored
recommendations.rationale: The parsed record, not the uploaded file, is the version of the candidate every later stage reads, and it lives inside the platform rather than on the customer's careers page. Putting it into the submission confirmation with a way to correct it is the one point where the person who can tell that half the work history is missing is still able to say so.
recommendations.costs: It creates a candidate-facing surface the vendor maintains and receives corrections through, used by people who are not the customer that bought the platform.

recommendations.title: Hold the unreviewed queue instead of declining it
recommendations.rationale: When the inactivity timeout fires, what it does and what it emails are the vendor's, and the same batch job can hold the applications and raise the requisition to the customer as having had no interview activity since a stated date. Whether the listing then comes down is a decision about funding, which is not visible from inside the platform. Holding rather than declining leaves that decision with the party who can make it, and leaves the applicants a state rather than a verdict.
recommendations.costs: Every held queue becomes a customer decision the current default takes off their desk, and support load is exactly what these defaults are tuned to keep down.

recommendations.title: Show what a knockout rule removes before saving
recommendations.rationale: Which knockout rules can be expressed, and what the configuration screen shows while one is being written, are both the vendor's. Whether a rule is reasonable is not visible from here; what it would have done to the applications already stored is, and running the draft against them puts that in front of the person who does hold the judgement.
recommendations.costs: The dry run reads the customer's stored applications on the configuration path, and the screen now states a number the vendor stands behind — including when a draft rule would have ended the entire stored pool.

recommendations.title: Name the rule and threshold in automated declines
recommendations.rationale: The message an automated rule sends is the vendor's template, and the rule that fired, its threshold and the value it read are already in the log line behind it. Carrying those three items into the message is what separates a decline that names a criterion from one that arrives as a verdict on the person.
recommendations.costs: The customer's configuration becomes quotable by everyone it is applied to, and a threshold stated in writing draws replies the current template does not.

title: Candidate
content:
# Candidate

The person applying. The only party in the funnel who sees the whole of their own process and almost none of anyone else's.
summary: The person applying. The only party in the funnel who sees the whole of their own process and almost none of anyone else's.
controls: What is submitted, and in what machine-readable shape
Which processes to enter and when to withdraw
Which questions to ask, and when to ask them
What is recorded: dates, wording, who said it
blind_to: Whether a requisition is funded, frozen or already promised internally
The band, the level, and the rubric being scored against
How many others are in the pipeline and where they came from
Whether a rejection was written by a person or emitted by a rule
incentives: Reach a decision quickly enough to keep options open
Avoid spending unpaid hours on processes that were never live
Preserve the ability to reapply without having burned the relationship

specimens.label: What the candidate can and cannot see

lines.text: Visible: every message received, every date, every stated reason, every hour spent.
Invisible: the requisition status, the approved band, the rubric, the queue depth, and whether a human read anything.
Most of the pain of a hiring process is an attempt to infer the second list from the first.

specimens.reading: This asymmetry is the reason the registry exists. It does not remove it — it makes the boundary between the two lists explicit.

recommendations.title: Check what the parser extracted before you submit
recommendations.rationale: The shape of the file is on the candidate's side of the line; what a reader decides after it is not. A layout a person reads without difficulty can arrive in the record as zero work-history entries, and the score that follows is arithmetic on what was extracted. Running the file through a parser first turns an invisible failure into an edit.
recommendations.costs: A single-column text export gives up the layout, and every later edit to the document has to be checked again.

recommendations.title: Ask what the conversation is attached to
recommendations.rationale: Whether an approved requisition sits behind the outreach, and whether an internal candidacy is already running, are not in any field the candidate can see. Asking at the first exchange is the only route to either, and the answer arrives before the unpaid hours do.
recommendations.costs: A logistics question in the first reply comes before any discussion of the work, and the answer cannot be checked against anything.

recommendations.title: Ask for the band before any assessment is scheduled
recommendations.rationale: The band, the level and the rubric are the second of the candidate's two lists, and the compensation bind runs on the candidate naming a number first. Asking for the band before an assessment is booked puts the mismatch at the screen rather than at week four, when the hours are already spent.
recommendations.costs: The question can end a process at the screen, and stating an expectation early fixes a number before the level is fixed.

recommendations.title: Keep a dated record of every message
recommendations.rationale: Dates, wording and who said it are the one part of the process the candidate holds in full. Kept as they arrive, they separate what a process established from what it did not: a rejection timed minutes after submission, a requisition back on the board, two rounds whose feedback disagrees.
recommendations.costs: It is unpaid administrative time in the period when time is scarcest, and a complete record of a process that ends in silence is still a record of silence.

recommendations.title: Submit at the stated timebox and name the cuts
recommendations.rationale: The hours a work sample takes come out of the same budget as the search itself, and the minutes it is read for are set on the other side of the gate. Stopping at the stated timebox and writing down what was cut to fit it keeps the exercise inside the scope that was agreed and leaves the trade-offs on the page.
recommendations.costs: A submission that stops at the timebox is read next to submissions that did not stop, and the reviewer's minutes are not something the candidate sets.

recommendations.title: Set a date when a silent process closes
recommendations.rationale: Silence after submission covers a listing nobody took down, a batch expiry job and a queue that was never reached, and none of the three is visible from outside. Choosing the closing date in advance turns an open question into a finished one and returns the hours to the searches that answered.
recommendations.costs: An answer that arrives after the chosen date is treated as no answer, and the time already spent is written off rather than waited out.

title: Client
content:
# Client

The party paying for the seat when the company is not its own customer. Signs the contract the requisition depends on, and often holds a gate the candidate never sees named.
summary: The party paying for the seat when the company is not its own customer. Signs the contract the requisition depends on, and often holds a gate the candidate never sees named.
controls: Whether the contract that funds the seat is signed, extended or cancelled
The rate the seat bills at, which the band is derived from
Approval of the profiles submitted against the contract, where the contract gives them that right
Their own interview round, after the employer's loop has already said yes
How many seats the engagement needs, and by when
blind_to: What the employer's own funnel did to reach the profiles they are shown
What the candidate was told about who is deciding, and when
The margin between the rate they pay and the salary the candidate is offered
What declining a profile without a reason costs the person behind it
incentives: Fill the seats the engagement needs without carrying employment obligations
Keep the option to end the engagement without ending anyone's employment — that is what the vendor is for
Pay for delivery, not for the search that produced it

specimens.label: Where the client sits in someone else's funnel

lines.text: The employer's loop finishes: screen, technical, panel, level. The candidate is told the process went well.
The profile then goes to the client for approval, and sometimes to a client interview the posting never mentioned.
A decline at this desk arrives to the candidate as a generic rejection from the employer, because the employer cannot state a reason it was never given.

specimens.reading: The candidate is waiting on a party that is not their prospective employer and that no message has named. Nothing in what they can see distinguishes this wait from an internal one.

recommendations.title: Let your round be named in the process the candidate is told
recommendations.rationale: Where the contract gives the client a profile approval or an interview, the candidate ends up waiting on a party no message has named. Allowing the vendor to state that stage — one client review, expected turnaround — costs no confidentiality and converts an unexplained silence into a stated step.
recommendations.costs: A named stage invites questions when it overruns; an unnamed one never has to answer for itself.

recommendations.title: State in the brief whether the seat is funded or bid-conditional
recommendations.rationale: A search run against an unsigned bid is a real search for a conditional seat. The vendor's recruiters can only disclose what the brief states, so the one sentence that makes outreach honest — this role opens when the contract signs — has to originate here.
recommendations.costs: A bid the market can see is a bid competitors can see; some clients treat the existence of the search as confidential.

recommendations.title: Return profile decisions on a stated clock, with a category
recommendations.rationale: The employer cannot tell the candidate what it was never told. A decline that arrives as one of three categories — profile, rate, timing — on a stated turnaround lets the vendor close records with a reason instead of a template, without exposing anything commercially sensitive.
recommendations.costs: A category is a commitment; 'no' with no category can no longer be sent.

title: Employer policy
content:
# Employer policy

Finance, leadership and the people function: the layer that authorises headcount, fixes bands and writes the rules the funnel executes. Never meets a candidate.
summary: Finance, leadership and the people function: the layer that authorises headcount, fixes bands and writes the rules the funnel executes. Never meets a candidate.
controls: Whether a requisition is funded, and whether it stays funded
The band and the levelling grid
Whether postings must be published externally regardless of internal candidates
What may be disclosed, and what must not be
blind_to: What a freeze looks like from the far end of a five-round process
How a compliance posting reads to someone who spent six weeks on it
The cumulative candidate hours a policy consumes
incentives: Optionality: an approved requisition that can be paused costs less than one that cannot
Consistency and legal defensibility across every hire
Cost control, on a cycle measured in quarters rather than in conversations

specimens.label: Where the decisions actually sit

lines.text: Requisition funded: finance · Band: compensation · Level: levelling committee
External posting required regardless of an internal candidate: policy
Interviews conducted: the team. Rejection sent: the recruiter.
The candidate only ever meets the last two rows.

specimens.reading: Several observations in this registry are the visible end of a decision taken in a row the candidate never sees.

recommendations.title: Publish the band on the posting itself
recommendations.rationale: The band and the levelling grid are set in this layer, and nothing downstream can disclose a number this layer has not released. Publishing it turns the reconciliation at bar.compensation_levelling_reconciliation into arithmetic rather than a conversation that happens for the first time after the panel.
recommendations.costs: The published number becomes a commitment the band cannot be quietly revised against mid-search, and it is legible to everyone already employed at that level.

recommendations.title: Sign the headcount before the role is published
recommendations.rationale: This layer decides whether a requisition is funded, and bar.headcount_executive_budget_approval is the only gate that stops a process after every person the candidate met has said yes. Moving the finance signature ahead of publication makes the later approval a countersignature, so a published role is one whose headcount already exists.
recommendations.costs: Budget is committed at publication rather than at the offer, and a requisition funded in advance is harder to pause than one approved at the end.

recommendations.title: Expire the listing when its authorisation lapses
recommendations.rationale: Whether a requisition stays funded is decided here, and that fact reaches no configuration screen on its own. A rule that withdraws the listing when authorisation lapses, and notifies everyone still inside the process, closes the gap between the decision and what the page shows.
recommendations.costs: A paused search cannot be kept warm: reopening means another trip through the approval chain and a posting that restarts from zero applicants, which is a direct charge on this layer's optionality.

recommendations.title: State on the posting that an internal candidacy exists
recommendations.rationale: The rule that a role is published externally regardless of an internal candidate sits in this layer, and so does what the posting may say. One line stating that an internal candidacy is in process gives an external applicant, at the point of applying, the fact the panel already has.
recommendations.costs: The external pool for those postings shrinks, which weakens the same posting as evidence of an open search, and an internal candidacy goes in writing before the search has concluded.

recommendations.title: Narrow the checks and show the candidate any discrepancy
recommendations.rationale: Which checks a role requires, and whether a third-party record is put to the candidate before it decides anything, are both settled in this layer. At bar.reference_background_verification a mismatch between a vendor record and an application holds the offer, and only a policy rule makes the candidate's account part of the file before the hold becomes a decision.
recommendations.costs: Every discrepancy adds a round trip before countersignature, and the single standard check pack has to be split by role instead of running identically on every hire.

title: Hiring manager
content:
# Hiring manager

The person the role reports to, and the panel they convene. Sets the bar, owns the outcome, and is doing this alongside the work the role exists to absorb.
summary: The person the role reports to, and the panel they convene. Sets the bar, owns the outcome, and is doing this alongside the work the role exists to absorb.
controls: The requirements as written, and the ones only they know about
Who interviews and what they ask
The level a candidate is assessed at
Whether a split panel becomes a hire
blind_to: What the same candidate showed in rounds they did not attend
How the requirements read to someone outside the team
What the search is costing the people covering the gap
incentives: Avoid a bad hire, which is visible and attributed, more than a missed hire, which is neither
Fill the gap without the ramp-up cost of someone who needs teaching
Keep the team's own delivery on track while running the loop

specimens.label: The asymmetry that sets the bar

lines.text: A bad hire is visible for a year and attributed to the person who made it.
A missed hire is invisible and attributed to nobody.
Both are costly. Only one has a name on it.

specimens.reading: This is not a bias to be scolded out of anyone; it is an incentive with a shape. Several conservative-default mechanisms follow from it directly.

recommendations.title: Write the requirement list from last quarter's work
recommendations.rationale: The requirements as written belong to this actor, and the list is what the keyword filter and the recruiter's screen are both built from. Checking each line against what the team delivered last quarter separates what the job uses from what a previous strong candidate happened to have. A year count larger than the age of the technology is checkable before the posting goes up.
recommendations.costs: A shorter list brings more applications into a funnel this actor's own team staffs, and it gives up the requirement page as the argument for a higher level and a wider band.

recommendations.title: Put the house preferences into the interview brief
recommendations.rationale: This actor sets what each interviewer asks, and holds the requirements only they know about. A preference about architecture or about vertical experience that is not in the brief is still scored in the room, and the candidate cannot design against a criterion they were not given.
recommendations.costs: A preference in writing is open to challenge from the panel and from the recruiter, and one that cannot be put into a sentence does not make it into the brief.

recommendations.title: Cap the take-home and floor the review time
recommendations.rationale: The exercise and who reviews it are both this actor's to set. Work built over hours and read in minutes is scored on whatever the reader happened to open, and the note that comes out of it describes the review rather than the submission. Capping the candidate's hours without a floor under the reviewer's minutes moves the asymmetry rather than closing it.
recommendations.costs: A three-hour sample carries less to go on, so more of the decision falls to the panel, and twenty minutes from each of two reviewers comes out of a sprint the team is already behind on.

recommendations.title: Agree the decision rule before the first conversation
recommendations.rationale: Whether a split panel becomes a hire is this actor's decision, and a unanimity requirement settles it in advance: one dissent and three produce the same outcome. Writing the rule down before the loop starts, including who breaks a tie, keeps an even split from being written up as a finding about the candidate.
recommendations.costs: Naming the tiebreaker means this actor signs a hire the panel did not agree on, and a hire that goes wrong is visible for a year and carries their name.

recommendations.title: Freeze the requirements once the loop opens
recommendations.rationale: The requirements as written are this actor's; whether a requisition closes is not. Assessments taken against one description do not carry over to another, so a change of stack or scope that arrives mid-loop belongs in the next posting rather than in the scoring of work already done. Everyone already inside is then measured against the description they were given.
recommendations.costs: The loop runs to the end against a profile the team has moved past, and the change the requirements needed waits for a search that starts again from the posting.

recommendations.title: Fix the assessed level before the loop opens
recommendations.rationale: The level a candidate is assessed at is this actor's to set, and it is set at the in-depth review whether or not it was written down first. Naming the level, and what evidence meets it, before the loop opens means experience above the band is measured against the requirements rather than against a forecast about how long someone stays.
recommendations.costs: A level fixed in advance removes the move of recovering a strong candidate at the level below, and where the level was set wrong the search runs again from the posting.

title: Public policy and industry standards
content:
# Public policy and industry standards

Regulators, labour law, and the conventions the market copies from itself. Sets the outer bounds and moves on a timescale no individual process can wait for.
summary: Regulators, labour law, and the conventions the market copies from itself. Sets the outer bounds and moves on a timescale no individual process can wait for.
controls: What must be disclosed — pay transparency rules being the clearest current example
What automated decision-making is permitted, and what must be explainable
Which employment relationships are possible in which jurisdiction
blind_to: How a rule is implemented once it reaches a configuration screen
Practices that are legal, ordinary, and still produce the effects catalogued here
incentives: Rules that are enforceable and measurable, which is a narrower set than rules that would help
Not disrupting labour markets faster than they can absorb the change

specimens.label: What a disclosure rule reaches, and what it does not

lines.text: Covered by pay transparency rules: the band must appear in the posting.
Not covered: at which level the candidate will actually be assessed.
Not covered: whether the requisition is funded, or already promised internally.

specimens.reading: The strongest external lever in this registry closes one branch of the compensation bind and leaves the levelling branch entirely open.

recommendations.title: Extend disclosure from the band to the level
recommendations.rationale: A disclosure rule that reaches the band leaves unstated the level the band attaches to, and the level decides where inside the band an offer lands. Requiring the posting to name the level being hired at, and the band for that level, closes the branch of the compensation bind that a band alone leaves open.
recommendations.costs: A band is a number on a page and a level is a claim about an internal grid, so each complaint needs records the regulator has to ask for separately. It also fixes at publication a level that is currently settled after the panel.

recommendations.title: Require postings to name where employment is possible
recommendations.rationale: Which employment relationships are possible in which jurisdiction is settled before anyone applies, and it is one of the few facts here that this actor defines rather than regulates at a distance. Requiring the posting to list the jurisdictions the role can actually be contracted in moves that fact to publication day instead of the screening call.
recommendations.costs: The rule binds a posting readable everywhere to contracts possible in a few places, and the body writing it reaches only its own territory — which one that is, this atlas does not state. The employer must publish an entity map it holds internally, and postings that read as open narrow visibly.

recommendations.title: Require postings to be dated and withdrawn on closure
recommendations.rationale: What a public posting is — an advertisement, or a statement that funded work exists — is a disclosure question, and that is the question this actor reaches. A rule that a posting carries its publication date and comes down when the search ends makes the difference between an open search and a talent pool observable from outside.
recommendations.costs: Two dates are cheap to check, but the fact that decides a breach — whether the search had ended — sits in records only the employer holds, so every complaint starts with disclosure. The rule also reaches sourcing that is legal and ordinary, which widens the perimeter it has to defend.

recommendations.title: Require every automated rejection to name its rule
recommendations.rationale: Where an application is ended by a threshold rather than by a reader, whether that decision must be explainable already sits inside this actor's bounds. Attaching the duty to the ending rather than to the message means a rule that closes an application — a missing term, an unmet threshold, an elapsed review window — produces a statement the applicant can check instead of nothing.
recommendations.costs: The duty is written for an employer and performed by a setting on a configuration screen the rule's author never sees, so the text has to fix responsibility somewhere between the party that buys the system and the party that ships it. Each stated reason is also a statement that can be disputed, and at the volume of ended applications that is a caseload before it is a remedy.

recommendations.title: Require continuity-based ranking features to be documented and justified
recommendations.rationale: A feature that scores the length of a break sits inside the automated decision-making whose bounds this actor sets, and it is the input that closes the gap-penalty loop. Requiring any ranking input derived from employment continuity to be documented and justified makes its presence checkable, which a prohibition on its own does not.
recommendations.costs: The rule can only be checked where the feature is named in a model card or a settings screen, so it rests on a documentation duty that lands on a supplier rather than on the employer being regulated. Naming one input leaves its proxies — recency of the last role, density of transitions — outside the text until they are named too.

recommendations.title: Publish a common schema for posting terms and outcomes
recommendations.rationale: The market copies conventions from itself faster than it absorbs rules, and this actor writes conventions as well as rules. A published schema — band, level, stages, jurisdictions, and a decline that names its stage and its criterion — gives the disclosure duties a shape that can be filled in once and read by machine.
recommendations.costs: A schema carries no obligation, so it is adopted where it is cheaper than what it replaces and nowhere else. The categories fixed in the first version become the ceiling on what is disclosed later, and the body that publishes it owns the revisions for as long as anyone uses it.

title: Recruiter
content:
# Recruiter

The function that moves people through the funnel. Holds the most information about the process and the least authority over its outcome.
summary: The function that moves people through the funnel. Holds the most information about the process and the least authority over its outcome.
controls: Which applications are read and in what order
What is disclosed at the screen, and when
The wording of the rejection
Whether a candidate is told a search has stalled
blind_to: What the panel actually scored, beyond the recommendation
Whether finance will approve the headcount this quarter
What the hiring manager privately requires but has not written down
incentives: Move the pipeline; time-to-fill is measured, time-to-clarity is not
Protect the relationship with the hiring manager, who is the internal client
Avoid saying anything that could be quoted back as a commitment

specimens.label: The week as the metrics see it

lines.text: Open requisitions: 11 · Applications received: 640 · Screening capacity: 40
Measured: time-to-fill, pipeline conversion, offer acceptance.
Not measured: time-to-clarity, or whether anyone who was rejected understood why.

specimens.reading: Several mechanisms in this registry are the shape of this table rather than of any decision anyone made.

recommendations.title: State the band before asking for a number
recommendations.rationale: The screen is where compensation first comes up, and the order of the two questions is the recruiter's to set. Saying the band that is on the requisition, before asking what the candidate expects, removes the asymmetry that both branches of the compensation bind run on. Where no band has been set, saying that is also an answer the candidate can act on.
recommendations.costs: It spends the flexibility of hearing the candidate's figure first, and it puts a number into the conversation that can be quoted back later as a commitment.

recommendations.title: Name the stage and the criterion that ended it
recommendations.rationale: The wording of the rejection belongs to this seat, and the same message can carry the stage the process ended at, the criterion that was named to the recruiter, and what the process never reached. Where the panel returned a recommendation without a criterion, the message records that no criterion was given, rather than a template sentence standing in its place. What can be written is bounded by what the recruiter was handed.
recommendations.costs: Each message is written rather than selected, against a clock measured as time-to-fill, and asking the panel for a criterion spends standing with the hiring manager, who is the internal client.

recommendations.title: Tell everyone still inside when a search stops moving
recommendations.rationale: Whether a candidate learns that a search has stalled is decided in this seat, and it can be decided from what is visible here: the date of the last scheduling activity on the requisition. The message states that date and no more, because whether the headcount returns this quarter is not visible from here. Silence at this point is read as a decision about the candidate.
recommendations.costs: Candidates who are told make other plans, and the message puts in writing that the internal client's search has stopped, against a seat measured on time-to-fill and on that relationship.

recommendations.title: Name every stage and its date at the screen
recommendations.rationale: What the process contains, how many conversations it has and when the first decision is due are disclosed at the screen or nowhere, and that disclosure sits in this seat. A candidate holding the list can tell a delay from an ending. When a round is added or a date moves, the same channel carries that within days to everyone already inside.
recommendations.costs: A stated date is a commitment held against interviewer calendars this seat does not control, so every slip becomes a message that has to be written.

recommendations.title: Say whether an approved requisition sits behind the call
recommendations.rationale: Outreach and the first conversation are where the recruiter states what the contact is for. Whether a requisition is open and approved, or whether this is a pool for headcount that does not exist yet, is a fact available at the moment of contact. Without it, the silence that follows such a conversation is read as a decision about the candidate.
recommendations.costs: It costs replies: outreach that states there is no open requisition gives less reason to answer, and reply volume is what the sourcing side of the pipeline is counted in.

recommendations.title: Set the reading order in advance and in writing
recommendations.rationale: Which applications are read and in what order is decided in this seat, and the order can be fixed before the week's queue exists: a stated share of screening capacity for inbound, order of arrival within each source, and no sort on how recently someone was last employed. The rule adds no screening capacity; it decides once where the capacity goes, instead of deciding it profile by profile against the length of the queue.
recommendations.costs: Reading without that sort covers fewer profiles per hour, and outbound candidates the hiring manager has asked about wait behind inbound ones.

title: An application inside the ATS
content:
# An application inside the ATS

The machine the candidate never sees: what happens to a submitted application between the form and a human being, and the four ways it can end without anyone reading it.
summary: The machine the candidate never sees: what happens to a submitted application between the form and a human being, and the four ways it can end without anyone reading it.
subject: one application record

states.title: Submitted
states.description: A form submission has been accepted. Fields are validated against the requisition schema; nothing has been interpreted.
states.visible_to_candidate: A confirmation page, sometimes an acknowledgement email.

states.title: Parsing
states.description: The document is converted to structured fields. Multi-column layouts, graphics and custom fonts routinely lose whole sections silently.
states.visible_to_candidate: Nothing.

states.title: Rule evaluation
states.description: Knockout rules, keyword coverage, years thresholds and ranking features run in sequence, short-circuiting on the first failure.
states.visible_to_candidate: Nothing, for a second or two.

states.title: Queued for human review
states.description: The record is above the threshold and waiting. Queue position depends on source: outbound lists are usually read first.
states.visible_to_candidate: Silence. This is where most of the waiting happens.

states.title: Read by a person
states.description: A recruiter opens the profile. The median attention available per profile is measured in seconds when the queue is deep.
states.visible_to_candidate: Nothing yet.

states.title: Advanced to the funnel
states.description: The record leaves this machine and enters proc.the_hiring_funnel_end_to_end at the recruiter screen.
states.visible_to_candidate: An invitation to talk.

states.title: Rejected by rule
states.description: A rule failed. The notification is often queued and sent minutes later, which is what produces a rejection at midnight.

title: Client account hiring funnel
content:
# Client account hiring funnel

From client demand and commercial contract to profile submission, client interview, and placement or unannounced closure.
summary: From client demand and commercial contract to profile submission, client interview, and placement or unannounced closure.
subject: a seat funded by a client contract and the candidate moving towards it

states.title: Client demand & contract scope
states.description: The end client identifies project headcount demand or issues a vendor tender. Budget exists if the contract is signed or is contingent on winning the bid.
states.visible_to_candidate: Nothing. The search is not visible publicly.

states.title: Vendor search opened
states.description: Vendor recruiting opens direct outreach or listings. Whether an executed contract or an unawarded bid sits behind it is not disclosed.
states.visible_to_candidate: Outreach messages or job postings without commercial contract context.

states.title: Vendor recruiter screen
states.description: Introductory conversation assessing experience and target compensation against the vendor target margin.
states.visible_to_candidate: A screening call where the rate band is presented as the vendor internal range.

states.title: Vendor technical evaluation
states.description: Technical interview or test task scored against the vendor assessment of the client technical threshold.
states.visible_to_candidate: A technical evaluation round with vendor engineering staff.

states.title: Submitted to client
states.description: The candidate CV is submitted to the client account team for profile review and interview selection.
states.visible_to_candidate: An extended waiting interval while the client reviews candidate batches.

states.title: Client interview round
states.description: Interview conducted directly by client engineering or project management leadership.
states.visible_to_candidate: An external interview round evaluating project and culture fit.

states.title: Offer formulation
states.description: Compensation package calculated from client billing rate minus required gross margin.
states.visible_to_candidate: An offer package structured around vendor compensation models.

states.title: Pre-placement verification
states.description: Client-mandated background checks, certifications, and compliance paperwork.
states.visible_to_candidate: Document requests and compliance background screening.

states.title: Contract signed & project start
states.description: Contract executed and candidate onboarded onto active client delivery.
states.visible_to_candidate: Confirmed start date and client team onboarding.

states.title: Vendor-level rejection
states.description: The search terminates at vendor screening or technical evaluation before client submission.
states.visible_to_candidate: Standard rejection message from the vendor recruitment team.

states.title: Declined by client
states.description: The client declines the CV submission or rejects the candidate after the client interview.
states.visible_to_candidate: A generic rejection relayed by the vendor without client feedback details.

states.title: Search closed unfunded / tender lost
states.description: The search closes because the client tender was lost, project budget was cancelled, or the commercial contract was paused.
states.visible_to_candidate: Unannounced silence or a notification that project requirements changed.

states.title: Requisition filled from internal bench
states.description: The position is allocated to an existing internal specialist released from another account, closing the external process.
states.visible_to_candidate: A sudden search closure notification after advancing through interview rounds.

title: The hiring funnel, end to end
content:
# The hiring funnel, end to end

From the moment headcount is authorised to a signed contract or a closed search, with the actor who owns each step and what the candidate can see from where they stand.
summary: From the moment headcount is authorised to a signed contract or a closed search, with the actor who owns each step and what the candidate can see from where they stand.
subject: a requisition and the candidate moving through it

states.title: Requisition drafted
states.description: A manager writes the role. Level, band and requirements are decided here, usually by copying the last search for the same team.
states.visible_to_candidate: Nothing. The role does not exist publicly yet.

states.title: Headcount authorised
states.description: Finance and leadership commit budget against the requisition. Approval can lapse or be withdrawn later without the funnel noticing.
states.visible_to_candidate: Nothing.

states.title: Posting live
states.description: The role is public. It may also be refreshed automatically every thirty days, which looks identical to a new opening.
states.visible_to_candidate: The posting, and whatever it states.

states.title: Application received
states.description: A record exists and is linked to the requisition. Nothing has been read.
states.visible_to_candidate: A confirmation, or silence.

states.title: Automated screen
states.description: Parser extraction, keyword thresholds, knockout rules and ranking. Decided in under a second.
states.visible_to_candidate: Either nothing, or a rejection within minutes.

states.title: In the recruiter queue
states.description: Waiting to be read by a person, in an inbound queue that usually holds more profiles than the week has hours.
states.visible_to_candidate: Silence of indeterminate length.

states.title: Recruiter screen
states.description: A conversation about compensation, timeline, location and a two-minute version of the last project.
states.visible_to_candidate: The call itself, and whichever parameters the recruiter states.

states.title: Technical assessment
states.description: A live exercise, a take-home, or both, scored against a rubric the candidate does not see.
states.visible_to_candidate: The exercise, and sometimes structured feedback afterwards.

states.title: Manager and team panel
states.description: Depth, ownership and collaboration, assessed across several interviewers who may be measuring different things.
states.visible_to_candidate: The conversations. Rarely the scores.

states.title: Compensation and levelling
states.description: The level the panel assigned meets the band finance approved. First time the two are compared.
states.visible_to_candidate: A number, or a renegotiation.

states.title: Offer approval
states.description: Manager, director, finance and the talent committee sign off in sequence. Everyone the candidate met has already said yes.
states.visible_to_candidate: Silence, usually described as "final checks".

states.title: Offer issued
states.description: A written offer exists. The requisition is still open until the countersignature lands.
states.visible_to_candidate: The offer document.

states.title: Reference and background check
states.description: A third-party record is compared against what the candidate claimed.
states.visible_to_candidate: A request for documents, or nothing.

states.title: Hired
states.description: Contract executed both ways, start date set, onboarding triggered.
states.visible_to_candidate: A signed contract.

states.title: Rejected
states.description: A decision was made and communicated. What it says about the cause is a separate question entirely.
states.visible_to_candidate: A message, ranging from a rubric category to a template.

states.title: Search frozen or cancelled
states.description: Budget withdrawn or the requisition put on hold. Can happen at any point, including after an offer.
states.visible_to_candidate: If the candidate is lucky, an explanation. Often the posting simply disappears.

states.title: Lapsed without a decision
states.description: No one decided anything. The record aged past a threshold, or the posting was never taken down.
states.visible_to_candidate: Silence, then possibly a bulk rejection at two in the morning.

transitions.label: budget signed off
transitions.guard: Finance commits headcount against the requisition.

transitions.label: posting goes live
transitions.guard: An approved requisition with a written description is published.

transitions.label: application submitted
transitions.guard: The candidate applies, or answers outbound outreach.

transitions.label: rules evaluated
transitions.guard: The record is complete enough for the configured rules to run.

transitions.label: thresholds cleared
transitions.guard: Extraction score and every knockout rule pass.

transitions.label: filtered out
transitions.guard: Any knockout rule fails, or the ranking falls below the advance threshold.

transitions.label: short-listed
transitions.guard: A person reads the profile and puts it on the list.

transitions.label: aged out
transitions.guard: No review happened before the expiry threshold.

transitions.label: parameters align
transitions.guard: Expectations, timeline and location are compatible, and the profile is submitted to the team.

transitions.label: parameters do not align
transitions.guard: Compensation, level, location or availability rules the candidate out before any engineering is discussed.

transitions.label: assessment passed
transitions.guard: The score clears the rubric threshold.

transitions.label: assessment not passed
transitions.guard: The score falls short, or the review is too shallow to find what is there.

transitions.label: panel recommends hire
transitions.guard: Consensus reaches the hire threshold.

transitions.label: panel does not reach consensus
transitions.guard: A split panel under a unanimity rule defaults to no hire.

transitions.label: level and band reconcile
transitions.guard: The assigned level and the approved band overlap.

transitions.label: level and band do not reconcile
transitions.guard: Expectation sits outside the band and neither the level nor the number moves.

transitions.label: sign-off complete
transitions.guard: Every approver in the chain has cleared it.

transitions.label: headcount withdrawn
transitions.guard: Budget is pulled or a freeze is announced before the offer is issued.

transitions.label: offer accepted
transitions.guard: The candidate signs and the checks begin.

transitions.label: offer retracted
transitions.guard: A freeze reaches an outstanding offer before the countersignature.

transitions.label: checks clear
transitions.guard: No unresolved discrepancy in the third-party record.

transitions.label: discrepancy unresolved
transitions.guard: A record mismatch or an eligibility bar is not reconciled.

transitions.label: posting outlives the search
transitions.guard: Hiring stops but the listing is never withdrawn.

transitions.label: requisition reopened
transitions.guard: The search restarts, sometimes with a revised profile, sometimes as an automatic refresh.

title: The path as it is supposed to run
content:
# The path as it is supposed to run

This is the canonical path: one opening, from a real need to a decision the
candidate can act on. It is written as a machine because that is how the rest of
the registry is written, and because a commitment that cannot be expressed as a
state and a guard is usually not a commitment.

**It is a construct, not a description of anybody.** No employer runs exactly
this. It is assembled from the things employers already say they do — bands on
postings, rubrics agreed before interviews, decisions inside a stated window,
postings taken down when a search ends — and put in one order so that the rest
of the atlas has something to be measured against.

That is the whole point of it. A barrier is not simply a gate: a gate is normal
and this path has fourteen of them. A barrier is the point at which one of these
commitments stops being kept. `deviations` on each state names which ones, which
is why every barrier in the registry appears on exactly one state of this path
and every mechanism on at least one.

Two things this path deliberately does **not** treat as deviations. A decline is
not a deviation — most candidates are declined, and a path that could only end
in a hire would be a fantasy rather than a standard. A closed search is not a
deviation either; needs change and budgets go. What makes both of them part of
the path rather than departures from it is that they arrive, they say what
happened, and they arrive in time to be useful.
summary: One opening, from a real need to a decision the candidate can act on, with each step written as the commitment it is supposed to keep. Every barrier in the registry is a place where one of these commitments stops being kept.
subject: one opening, and one candidate moving through it

states.title: A real opening, described honestly
states.description: The requisition describes work that exists now, at a level the team actually needs, inside a band the budget already covers. Nothing here is aspirational: the list of requirements is what the job uses, not what the last four candidates happened to have.
states.visible_to_candidate: Nothing yet. Everything downstream inherits whatever is decided here.

states.title: Published with its terms on the page
states.description: The posting states the compensation band, the location rules, the stages the process has and roughly how long each takes. It comes down when the search ends.
states.visible_to_candidate: The role, the band, the stages, and a date by which the first answer should arrive.

states.title: Applied, and told so
states.description: The application is submitted and acknowledged. The record holds what the candidate actually wrote, and the candidate can tell that it arrived.
states.visible_to_candidate: A confirmation that names the role and says what happens next.

states.title: Machine work stays mechanical
states.description: Automation deduplicates, extracts and orders. It does not decide. Where a rule does end an application, the rule is stated and it is one a person would defend out loud.
states.visible_to_candidate: If a rule ends it here, which rule.

states.title: Read by a person, inside the stated window
states.description: Every application that clears the mechanical stage is read by someone, and read before the window the posting promised runs out.
states.visible_to_candidate: Either a next step or a decision, by the date the posting gave.

states.title: Terms compared before anyone spends time
states.description: Band, level, location, notice period and start date are put side by side in the first conversation, before any assessment is scheduled. Either side can stop here at no cost to the other.
states.visible_to_candidate: The numbers and the constraints, from both sides, in the first call.

states.title: Assessed on the work, against a rubric that is shared
states.description: One timeboxed exercise that resembles the job. The candidate is given the criteria before starting, the timebox is enforced against the evaluator as well, and the same rubric scores everyone.
states.visible_to_candidate: The exercise, the timebox and the criteria — before starting, not after.

states.title: One panel, one question each, one decision rule
states.description: Every interviewer knows what they are measuring and that nobody else is measuring it. The rule that turns their scores into a decision is agreed before the first conversation, and no round is added after the process has started.
states.visible_to_candidate: Who they will meet, what each conversation is for, and how many there are.

states.title: The level meets the band that was published
states.description: The level follows from the evidence the panel gathered, and the band was public from the first day. Reconciling them is arithmetic, not a negotiation about whether the band exists.
states.visible_to_candidate: The same band the posting stated, and which point in it the offer sits at.

states.title: Approval already exists
states.description: Headcount was signed before the role was published, so this step is a countersignature rather than a second decision. If the budget goes, the search closes and everyone inside it is told.
states.visible_to_candidate: A date for the offer, rather than an indefinite period described as final checks.

states.title: A written offer with everything in it
states.description: Salary, level, title, location terms, start date and anything conditional, in writing, with a decision window the candidate agreed to. Nothing in it changes after acceptance.
states.visible_to_candidate: The complete offer document, and how long they have to answer.

states.title: Checks that are proportionate and answerable
states.description: Only the checks the role actually requires. Where a third-party record disagrees with what the candidate said, the discrepancy is put to the candidate before it decides anything.
states.visible_to_candidate: What is being checked, and any discrepancy, before it is acted on.

states.title: Hired on the terms that were published
states.description: Contract executed both ways on the terms that were on the page from the beginning, with a start date both sides chose.
states.visible_to_candidate: A signed contract that matches the posting.

states.title: Declined, with a reason that can be acted on
states.description: Not every candidate is hired, and a decline is not a deviation. What makes it part of this path is that it arrives, it names the stage it happened at and the criterion that decided it, and it says whether applying again is worth anything.
states.visible_to_candidate: Which stage, which criterion, and whether to apply again.

states.title: Search closed, and everyone told
states.description: A search can legitimately stop: the need changes, the budget goes, someone internal turns out to be right for it. What this path requires is that the posting comes down and every candidate still inside the process is told within days.
states.visible_to_candidate: A message saying the search ended, and when.

transitions.label: posted with its terms
transitions.guard: An approved requisition, a band and a described process go live together.

transitions.label: application submitted
transitions.guard: The candidate applies against terms they could read beforehand.

transitions.label: record processed
transitions.guard: The submission is parsed and acknowledged.

transitions.label: passed to a person
transitions.guard: No automated rule ended it, so a person now has it.

transitions.label: worth a conversation
transitions.guard: A person read the profile and wants to talk.

transitions.label: terms are compatible
transitions.guard: Band, level, location and timing work for both sides, said out loud.

transitions.label: work meets the rubric
transitions.guard: The exercise was scored against the criteria the candidate was given.

transitions.label: panel decides by its rule
transitions.guard: The agreed decision rule returns a hire.

transitions.label: level lands inside the band
transitions.guard: The evidence-assigned level maps to a point in the published band.

transitions.label: countersigned
transitions.guard: The approval that existed before publication is confirmed.

transitions.label: offer accepted
transitions.guard: The candidate accepts a complete written offer inside the agreed window.

transitions.label: checks clear
transitions.guard: Nothing proportionate to the role is unresolved.

transitions.label: declined after reading
transitions.guard: A person decided no, and said at which stage and on what criterion.

transitions.label: terms are incompatible
transitions.guard: The gap is named in the same conversation, before any assessment is booked.

transitions.label: work did not meet the rubric
transitions.guard: The score is below the shared criteria, and the criterion is named.

transitions.label: decision rule returns no hire
transitions.guard: The rule agreed beforehand returns no hire, and which dimension decided it is stated.

transitions.label: level and expectation do not meet
transitions.guard: The published band and the candidate's stated expectation do not overlap, which both sides already knew.

transitions.label: discrepancy stands
transitions.guard: The candidate was shown the discrepancy and it remains unresolved.

transitions.label: need changed
transitions.guard: The work no longer exists, and the posting comes down the same week.

transitions.label: budget withdrawn
transitions.guard: Headcount is pulled, and every candidate in the process is told within days.

transitions.label: offer withdrawn and explained
transitions.guard: An outstanding offer cannot stand, and the candidate is told why, in writing, immediately.

title: Zero rates and a same-year deduction
content:
# Zero rates and a same-year deduction

Two policy facts, held for over a decade, set the price of a hire. Money cost
almost nothing to borrow, and a developer's salary reduced taxable income in the
year it was paid. Neither was about hiring, and both decided how hiring worked.

The consequence for a candidate was specific: an empty seat cost more than a
wrong hire, so employers absorbed the risk of training. Nothing in this era
required an employer to be generous for that to be true.
summary: For over a decade money cost nothing to borrow and engineering payroll reduced taxable income in the year it was paid. Both facts were policy, both were durable, and together they made an empty seat more expensive than a wrong hire.
capital: From 16 December 2008 the US policy rate sat at its floor for seven years, and the euro-area deposit rate was cut to zero in July 2012 and below zero in June 2014. Under section 174 as it then stood, research and experimental expenditures could be deducted in the year they were paid rather than charged to capital account. Borrowing to fund growth was close to free, and payroll spent building product reduced taxable income immediately.
hiring: Headcount was the standard use of raised capital. A salary was a current-year deduction and the return on a hire was measured in growth rather than in margin, so teams were sized to a funded plan and the plan came before the revenue. A listing route stayed open to companies without trailing profits throughout the period, which meant payroll could run ahead of earnings without closing off the exit.
entry: Demand for people who could do the work ran ahead of supply, so employers hired for potential and trained afterwards. A beginner's salary carried the same immediate deduction as a senior's, which made junior seats cheap to fund against the cost of leaving a seat empty. Self-teaching, a short conversion course and a first job with training attached were ordinary routes in.
ended_by: Not by a contraction. In March 2020 the same policy floor was reimposed and fund flows stepped up by a multiple, and hiring plans were sized to capital raised rather than to current revenue.

indicators.label: US federal funds target range, held at its floor
ECB deposit facility rate, at or below zero
Research and development payroll deductible in the year it was paid
US technology listings profitable on trailing earnings

title: The record funding years
content:
# The record funding years

The shortest era on this page, and the one that shaped what most people still
expect a hiring process to look like. Funding raised in a single year roughly
doubled the previous record, and headcount plans were written against that
capital rather than against revenue.

Two things followed that are worth stating plainly, because they are the
baseline everything after 2022 is measured against. Roles were opened before the
work that would fill them existed. And the constraint an employer optimised for
was time-to-fill — which is the only condition under which a process gets
shorter rather than longer.
summary: Two years in which the policy floor returned and venture funding roughly doubled its previous record. Headcount plans were set against committed capital rather than against bookings, and the terms of entry were set on the candidate's side.
capital: The policy rate returned to 0.00–0.25% on 16 March 2020 and stayed there for two years. US venture-backed companies raised $329.6 billion in 2021 against a previous record of $166.6 billion in 2020, and global venture investment reached $671 billion. The listing window stayed open to companies without earnings: of 121 US technology listings in 2021, 21% were profitable on trailing twelve-month earnings.
hiring: With several years of funding raised at once, headcount was planned against committed capital rather than against bookings, and roles were opened before the work that would fill them was specified. Time-to-fill became the operative constraint, so loops were shortened, offers raised and candidate pools widened across locations. Recruiting functions were themselves staffed to the expanded plan.
entry: Employers competed for candidates, so entry terms were set on the candidate's side: compressed interview loops, offers made on shorter evidence, and pay set by competing bids. Entry-level and career-change intake ran at volume, because the alternative was leaving funded seats empty. Holding a current job was not a precondition, and changing employer was the ordinary way to raise pay.
ended_by: Two dated changes. The target range left the floor on 17 March 2022, and for tax years beginning after 31 December 2021 any amount paid in connection with developing software had to be capitalised and amortised over five years — so a developer's salary stopped reducing taxable income in the year it was paid.

indicators.label: US venture-backed companies raised
Global venture capital invested
US policy rate, back at its floor
US technology listings profitable on trailing earnings

title: Rates up, payroll repriced
content:
# Rates up, payroll repriced

Four things moved at once and in the same direction: the cost of money, the
value of the equity, the availability of new funding, and the tax treatment of
the payroll itself. None of them was a judgement about anybody's work.

The change worth carrying forward is not the size of the reduction. It is what
happened to what a job posting *is*. When hiring narrows to replacing specific
departures, a posting stops describing a plan and starts describing a person who
recently left — and the evidence that satisfies it narrows to the same title, at
similar scale, in the same stack. That is a different document to apply to, and
most of the atlas is about what applying to it does.
summary: The policy rate reached its cycle peak, technology equities repriced, every stage of the private funding chain contracted at once, and software payroll became something to amortise rather than deduct. The correction ran through announced reductions rather than through attrition.
capital: The federal funds target range reached a cycle peak of 5.25–5.50% effective 27 July 2023 and was held there for about fourteen months, and the technology-weighted NASDAQ Composite fell 36.4% from its November 2021 close to its December 2022 low. Every stage of the private chain contracted together: US venture deal value fell from $348.0 billion in 2021 to $170.6 billion in 2023, exit value hit a decade low of $61.5 billion, and new fund commitments fell to a six-year low of $66.9 billion. From tax years beginning after 31 December 2021, software development costs were amortised over five years for domestic research and fifteen for foreign research instead of being deducted when paid.
hiring: Payroll was now both harder to refinance and slower to deduct, so plans were cut to the capital already in hand. Reductions were announced rather than absorbed through attrition: a tracker of publicly reported technology layoffs records 165,269 employees in 2022 and 265,660 in 2023, its highest year. Open requisitions were closed and filled positions eliminated, and the recruiting capacity built for the previous era was itself reduced.
entry: Hiring narrowed to the replacement of specific departures, which meant a posted role described work someone had recently been doing. The evidence employers would accept narrowed with it: recent experience in the same title, at similar scale, in the same stack. The routes that worked when employers hired for potential produced no offers, because the seats being filled were defined by an incumbent's job description rather than by a plan.
ended_by: The financial conditions reversed without the reduction reversing. The target range came off its peak on 18 September 2024 and the immediate domestic deduction was restored by statute in July 2025, but the headcount removed during the correction was not restored — so the reduced level carried forward as the baseline rather than as a trough.

NASDAQ Composite, record close to cycle low

US venture exit value, a decade low

Tracked technology layoffs, not a census

title: A fixed number of seats
content:
# A fixed number of seats

Two official series say most of it, and they say it together. Gross hires in the
US information sector fell 28.9% between 2022 and 2025. Layoffs and discharges
in the same official series barely moved over those years. The sector shrank
because people were not hired to replace the people who left, not because people
were removed at an accelerating rate — which is why a tracker of announced cuts
and the official separations series tell such different stories about the same
period.

That distinction is the whole point of this page. A separations problem gets
better when the announcements stop. A hiring problem does not: it gets better
when seats open. Seats open when incumbents leave, and the information-sector
quits rate is at 1.1%, roughly half what it was in June 2022.

So the arithmetic a candidate is inside: fewer openings, more applications per
opening, and the openings that exist described at senior level. That is
competition for a fixed and shrinking number of seats. It is not a statement
about anyone's ability, and it is not a claim that any employer behaved badly —
it is what happens to a queue when the queue stops moving.

The registry documents what that produces at each gate. This page exists so that
those entries are not mistaken for a description of the candidate.
summary: The conditions that made hiring expensive were reversed; the number of positions was not. The contraction now runs through the hiring channel rather than the separation channel, which is why it is competition for a fixed and shrinking number of seats rather than a shortage of qualified people.
capital: The tax treatment that penalised payroll was undone: section 174A, added on 4 July 2025, allows domestic research expenditure to be deducted when paid for tax years beginning after 31 December 2024, balances capitalised under the 2022–2024 rules may be recovered in one year or over two, and smaller taxpayers may elect back to 2022. Policy rates came off their cycle peak in September 2024. The inputs that made hiring expensive were reversed. The number of positions was not.
hiring: The contraction runs through the hiring channel, not the separation channel. Official gross hires in the US information sector fell from 1,270,000 in 2022 to 903,000 in 2025 — down 28.9% — while official layoffs and discharges in the same series were roughly flat at 451,000, 399,000, 395,000 and 447,000. Openings averaged 224,000 a month in 2022 and 121,000 in 2025, and stood at 90,000 in June 2026. Sector payrolls fell from 3,115,000 in November 2022 to 2,780,000 in July 2026.
entry: Incumbents vacate few seats: the information-sector quits rate was 1.1% in June 2026 against 1.9% in June 2022, and the total-private hires rate 3.7% against 4.7%. Applications per open role rose from 116 in 2022 to 244 in 2025 across one platform's benchmark. Software postings ran 69.3% senior and 4.5% entry-level in the first quarter of 2026, and payroll records show employment of developers aged 22–25 down close to 20% from its late-2022 peak while employment at older ages in the same occupation did not fall. Entry now means succeeding a specific incumbent rather than being trained into a funded seat.

Layoffs and discharges, US information sector — roughly flat

title: Communication mismatch or tone friction in panel
content:
# Communication mismatch or tone friction in panel

Noticeable divergence in communication style, pacing, or terminology during live panel discussions.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not prove the candidate lacks teamwork skills in general.
summary: Noticeable divergence in communication style, pacing, or terminology during live panel discussions.

probes.action: Ask the recruiter for explicit feedback on the collaborative dynamic.
probes.expected_signal: Clarifies whether the friction was taken as an attitude issue or as a difference in style.

outcomes.label: A reply arrives that adds nothing to the note: the summary line comes back as it was written — communication not calibrated to the audience — or the answer states that feedback beyond what was already sent is not given. No round, no minute and no exchange is attached to it.
outcomes.because: Inability to provide a single grounded communicative exchange points to non-calibrated impression scoring rather than an evidence-based panel.

outcomes.label: The recruiter names a specific exchange — which round, roughly when, what the question was about — and describes it as one moment rather than something that held across the session.
outcomes.because: A concrete communicative exchange demonstrates individualized panel recall, ruling out arbitrary non-specific impression bias.

outcomes.label: The answer moves from pacing to reception: the concern is put as how critique was taken, not as which level the answers sat at.
No reply arrives at all: the request sits unanswered on the thread, and the written note remains the whole record of the round.

specimens.label: Panel discussion, transcript fragment

lines.speaker: Interviewer A
lines.text: So when you say the write path is eventually consistent, what does the client see?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Depends on the read. If it goes through the cache it can be stale by up to the TTL; if it goes to the primary it is current.

lines.speaker: Interviewer A
lines.text: Sorry, I think we are talking past each other. I meant from the user perspective.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Ah — then: they may see their own write missing for a second or two.

lines.speaker: Interviewer A
lines.text: That is what I was after.

specimens.reading: The disagreement was about which layer the question lived in, not about the answer. The content was right at both levels.

specimens.label: Panel feedback
specimens.subject: Feedback — architecture round

lines.text: Technically solid throughout.
The panel felt communication was not always calibrated to the audience — answers went to implementation detail where a product-level framing was wanted.

specimens.reading: Read against the transcript, this is one exchange generalised into a trait. Both readings fit the same recording, which is exactly why the observation is not a verdict.

perspectives.sees: An exchange where the question and the answer sat at different levels, reconciled in the room within half a minute. Then written feedback that states the mismatch as a property of the answers.
perspectives.reads: One exchange and a generalisation of it both fit the same recording; which of the two the panel worked from is not in the note.
perspectives.does: Asks which moment the note refers to, and keeps the wording, since the note is the only version of the round that leaves the room.

perspectives.sees: Written impressions from each interviewer after the round. The recording is not what the panel reviews.
perspectives.reads: Wording that lines up across notes reads as a shared signal; a bad hire is visible for a year and has a name on it, a missed one has neither.
perspectives.does: Decides on the note as written, since it is the record of the round, and has no cheap way to test whether it describes one exchange or a pattern.

perspectives.sees: A summary line for the round: technically solid, communication not calibrated. What was said at minute twenty-two is not in the recruiter's view.
perspectives.reads: A reason to relay, at the level of detail it was given at.
perspectives.does: Passes the summary on, and when the candidate asks which moment it refers to, has the same sentence to answer with and nothing behind it.

non_inferences: Does not prove the candidate lacks teamwork skills in general.

title: Compensation band reduced or altered mid-process
content:
# Compensation band reduced or altered mid-process

The compensation band offered or discussed is revised downward from the range previously agreed or advertised.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not prove an intentional bait-and-switch unless evidence of company policy establishes one.
summary: The compensation band offered or discussed is revised downward from the range previously agreed or advertised.

probes.action: Ask whether the revised band follows from a lower levelling grade or from a company-wide budget adjustment.
probes.expected_signal: Separates the outcome of the levelling assessment from the company's financial constraints.

outcomes.label: The recruiter attributes the change to a revision of the band for the grade, names the date it was revised, and says the figure stated at the screen was the requisition's approved band until that date.
The recruiter says the change is to your assessed level: the panel placed you a grade below the one the role was posted at, and the lower band belongs to that grade.
A reply comes back that restates the new figure without saying whether it follows from the grade or from your assessment, and does not address the earlier band.
The question is not answered before the offer decision is due; the figure named on the call is the last statement of the band you have.

specimens.label: Recruiter message before the offer call

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Quick heads-up before we talk numbers tomorrow — where did we land on expectations?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Same as the range in the posting and what we agreed at the screen: 85–95k.

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Right. So finance has revised the band for this level since we opened the role. We are working with 72–78k now.

specimens.reading: The number moved after the process had already taken five weeks of the candidate's time. Note the date the original band was stated and by whom.

specimens.label: Offer call, transcript fragment

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Was the change specific to me, or to the level?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: To the level. Everyone coming in at this grade this quarter is on the new band.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: And the posting still shows the old range?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: It does. I will get that updated.

specimens.reading: An answer that generalises to the whole grade describes a policy. An answer that is specific to you would describe an assessment. They are different mechanisms.

perspectives.sees: A band stated in the posting and again at the screen, a lower band stated in week five, and the posting still showing the first figure.
perspectives.reads: An answer that applies to everyone at the grade describes a policy; an answer specific to this candidate would describe an assessment. The reply given was the first.
perspectives.does: Records the original band, the date it was stated and who stated it, and asks whether the revision is to the level or to this offer.

perspectives.sees: A revised grid for the level, arriving after the role opened, and a candidate holding the figure stated at the screen.
perspectives.reads: The number changed above the recruiter's position; the earlier figure is the one the candidate is holding going into the offer call.
perspectives.does: States the current band and where it came from, and files the posting correction as a request, because the band itself is set a level above this function.

perspectives.sees: A levelling grid and a band per grade, revised on the cycle at which compensation is reviewed.
perspectives.reads: A band set at the grade applies to everyone entering at that grade, which is what makes the hires consistent with one another.
perspectives.does: Revises the grid and applies it from the date of the revision. Processes already running against the previous figure are not rows in that decision.

perspectives.sees: Postings covered by a disclosure rule carry a range. A revision made mid-process reaches this layer only if the posting is checked against the offer.
perspectives.reads: The published range is a measurable object. The grade a candidate is assessed at, and the date a band was revised, are not covered by the same rule.
perspectives.does: Writes to what is enforceable: the presence of a range in the posting, and not the levelling decision that determines which range applies.

non_inferences: Does not prove an intentional bait-and-switch unless evidence of company policy establishes one.

title: Complete silence after submission
content:
# Complete silence after submission

After the application is submitted, nothing arrives: no automated receipt, no acknowledgement, no rejection, no message from a recruiter.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not prove the application was reviewed by a human.
- Does not prove the role was cancelled or already filled.
summary: After the application is submitted, nothing arrives: no automated receipt, no acknowledgement, no rejection, no message from a recruiter.

probes.action: Check the email spam folder and the security quarantine for an automated acknowledgement from the ATS.
probes.expected_signal: Shows whether the application was ingested and generated a confirmation ID.

outcomes.label: A dated automated acknowledgement carrying a confirmation ID is sitting in spam or in the security quarantine, filtered on the day of submission.
Neither folder holds anything from the employer or from its ATS domain; the only record of the submission is the confirmation screen the candidate saved.
Quarantine holds later automated mail against the same requisition — a status change, an expiry or a closure notice — but no acknowledgement from the day of submission.
The check cannot be completed: quarantine retention has already rolled over, or the quarantine is held by the mail administrator, so nothing from that period is visible.

specimens.label: ATS status history
specimens.context: exported by the candidate on day 41

lines.text: Application received — Senior Backend Engineer
Status: Under review
Status: Under review

specimens.reading: The record shows one state change and then nothing. Silence here is the absence of an event, not an event with a hidden meaning.

specimens.label: Follow-up message to the listed contact

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Hello — I applied for the Senior Backend Engineer role on the 3rd and wanted to check the application went through. Happy to send anything else that helps.
