lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Following up on the note above. If the search has been paused or filled, that is completely fine — I would just like to close the loop on my side.
— no reply —

specimens.reading: Two polite, dated attempts and no response. What is established is the absence of a reply, not a decision about the candidate.

perspectives.sees: One status line on day 0, the same status line on day 41, and no reply to two dated follow-ups sent to the listed contact.
perspectives.reads: The record establishes that no reply arrived. It does not carry a reading of the application, because no event after submission is in it.
perspectives.does: Records the confirmation ID and both follow-up dates, checks spam and quarantine for the receipt, and keeps other processes running to their own timelines.

perspectives.sees: The application sits in a queue whose depth exceeds the week's screening capacity. A follow-up sent to a listed address may not be attached to any requisition.
perspectives.reads: An unread application is a position in a queue, not a decision that has been taken and withheld.
perspectives.does: Works the requisitions closest to their fill date first, because time-to-fill is measured and time-to-clarity is not.

perspectives.sees: A record whose status has not changed since ingestion, and an expiry timer running against the threshold the customer's configuration sets.
perspectives.reads: An unreviewed record approaching its expiry threshold. Whether the profile was read, or was readable at all, is not a field the platform holds.
perspectives.does: Expires the record at the threshold and sends whatever the customer's notification settings specify, which may be nothing.

non_inferences: Does not prove the application was reviewed by a human.
Does not prove the role was cancelled or already filled.

title: Conflicting feedback across different interviewers
content:
# Conflicting feedback across different interviewers

Feedback from one round praises architectural depth while another round claims insufficient technical background.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not prove bad faith; it shows the rubric was not calibrated across the hiring committee.
summary: Feedback from one round praises architectural depth while another round claims insufficient technical background.

probes.action: Ask the talent partner for the consolidated rubric summary.
probes.expected_signal: Shows whether the two rounds were scoring against different criteria.

outcomes.label: A summary comes back naming what each round scored, and the two lines about depth turn out to be scores on two different exercises.
outcomes.because: Different criteria across distinct rounds establish separate evaluation dimensions rather than noisy evaluator disagreement.

outcomes.label: A summary comes back naming what each round scored, and both rounds scored the same criterion and recorded opposite results.
outcomes.because: Opposing scores on the identical criterion within the same interview loop demonstrate high inter-rater noise (mech.take_home_evaluation_fatigue_asymmetry) rather than an honest calibrated verdict.

outcomes.label: A reply arrives that adds nothing to the decision already sent: the two verdicts restated, or the scoring described as internal and not shared with candidates.
No reply arrives, and no summary is produced.

specimens.label: Two rounds, two verdicts
specimens.subject: Consolidated feedback

lines.text: Round 2 (systems): Strong architectural depth. Reasoned clearly about consistency trade-offs and failure modes. Recommend proceed.
Round 4 (technical): Insufficient depth for the level. Struggled to move past a first-pass solution. Recommend do not proceed.
Final decision: do not proceed.

specimens.reading: Both notes are about the same person in the same week. At least one of them is measuring something other than the candidate.

specimens.label: What the two rounds actually asked

lines.speaker: Interviewer B
lines.text: Round 2 — Walk me through how you would keep two regions in sync when the link between them drops.

lines.speaker: Interviewer D
lines.text: Round 4 — Here is a string parsing problem. You have twenty-five minutes.

specimens.reading: The rounds did not disagree about the candidate; they measured different things and reported both as depth.

perspectives.sees: Two verdicts from the same week: one round rating architectural depth highly, another finding depth insufficient for the level, and one negative decision under them.
perspectives.reads: The rounds asked different questions and both reported the answer as depth. Which of the two the decision rests on is not stated.
perspectives.does: Asks for the consolidated rubric summary, and records what each round actually asked alongside what each concluded.

perspectives.sees: Two written notes on the same candidate from rounds they did not sit in, each using the word depth for a different exercise.
perspectives.reads: Those notes are the whole of what is available about those rounds; nothing in them separates a disagreement about the candidate from a difference between the two exercises.
perspectives.does: Sets who interviews and what each round asks, and closes the split with a decision rather than a re-run. A hire made over a recorded negative note carries their name if it goes wrong.

perspectives.sees: Two recommendations pointing opposite ways and a decision line under them. The scores behind each recommendation are not in the recruiter's view.
perspectives.reads: One reason has to be written to the candidate out of two notes that do not agree. Anything said beyond the recorded decision can be quoted back later.
perspectives.does: Sends the outcome in wording that stays inside what was written down, and moves the requisition on. Reopening a recorded decision sits with the hiring manager, not the recruiter.

non_inferences: Does not prove bad faith; it shows the rubric was not calibrated across the hiring committee.

title: Explicit feedback citing skill-depth shortfall
content:
# Explicit feedback citing skill-depth shortfall

Interviewer or recruiter provides structured notes citing a specific deficit in algorithmic complexity, architecture, or tool mastery.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not imply general incompetence; it reflects the threshold for this specific role level.
summary: Interviewer or recruiter provides structured notes citing a specific deficit in algorithmic complexity, architecture, or tool mastery.

probes.action: Review the interview solution against the standard patterns for that problem and identify the edge cases it misses.
probes.expected_signal: Verifies whether the code actually lacked the optimisation or rigour the notes name.

outcomes.label: The solution has the property the feedback names, and the approach it expected is a standard pattern for that problem.
The solution has the property the feedback names, and the approach it expected is specific to one stack or house pattern rather than a general one.
The solution does not have the property the feedback names — the code already does what the notes say was missing.
Nothing was retained from the exercise — a shared editor closed, a whiteboard erased — so the claim cannot be checked against anything.

specimens.label: Structured feedback notes
specimens.subject: Feedback — technical panel

lines.text: The panel was positive on system decomposition and on how you reasoned about failure modes.

The gap was in the second exercise: the solution was correct but quadratic, and the panel was looking for the linear approach using a hash index. We would want to see that reached without prompting at this level.
We are not moving forward now, but this was close and we would welcome a re-application in six months.

specimens.reading: A named exercise, a named property, a named expectation. This is the rare rejection that is actually actionable.

specimens.label: The moment in the panel

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: This works. What is the complexity?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Quadratic — nested scan over the same list.

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: Right. Can you get it down?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Probably with an index of some kind. I would want to think about it.

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: That is fine, let us move on for time.

specimens.reading: The transcript and the written feedback agree. When they agree, the feedback is describing something that actually happened.

perspectives.sees: A rejection that names the exercise, the property of the solution and the expectation for the level, together with a stated window for re-application.
perspectives.reads: A threshold for this level in one named place, which is a claim that can be checked against what happened in the room.
perspectives.does: Checks the claim against their own record of the panel, and works from the two facts given: the named gap and the named window.

perspectives.sees: The panel's write-ups against the rubric, including the exercise where the step to the linear solution came after a prompt.
perspectives.reads: Evidence about the bar for the level rather than about the person; a decline can be revisited in six months and a hire cannot.
perspectives.does: Declines for now, keeps the exercise and the property in the notes, and leaves the re-application open.

perspectives.sees: A recommendation with a written reason attached to it, and none of the scoring that stands behind the reason.
perspectives.reads: A reason specific enough to send as written; the field it arrived in is free text, so what is in it is what the panel typed there.
perspectives.does: Sends the reason in the panel's own terms and adds the re-application window, and cannot expand on it if asked, because the scoring did not travel with it.

non_inferences: Does not imply general incompetence; it reflects the threshold for this specific role level.

title: Feedback naming as absent something the submitted work contains
content:
# Feedback naming as absent something the submitted work contains

The stated shortfall is the absence of work that is present in what the candidate submitted, at the path they gave.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not establish that the work was never opened, only that the claim and the submission disagree.
- Does not establish that the work would have met the bar had it been read.
summary: The stated shortfall is the absence of work that is present in what the candidate submitted, at the path they gave.

probes.action: Open the submitted path in a private window with no session, and note what the first screen shows before any navigation.
probes.expected_signal: Establishes what a reader with no context and no time actually lands on.

outcomes.label: The work named as absent is visible on the first screen, without navigating.
outcomes.because: Overlooking prominent first-screen evidence indicates superficial keyword/automated parsing or neglected review rather than an honest thorough evaluation.

outcomes.label: The work is there, but behind a non-default branch, a subdirectory, or an account other than the candidate's own.
The path does not resolve, or resolves to something private.
outcomes.because: An unreachable or private submission link confirms candidate omission rather than evaluator negligence or automated screening error.

outcomes.label: No path was submitted; the claim rests on the profile text alone.

specimens.label: Feedback after screening
specimens.subject: Following your application

lines.text: The team was looking for evidence of distributed systems work, and we did not see any in your materials.
We would encourage you to apply again once you have that experience.
The submitted index named three services and the path to each.

specimens.reading: Two sentences that cannot both hold. Either the work is absent or it was not opened — and only the second is consistent with a submission that names it.

perspectives.sees: A shortfall named in terms of something missing, against a submission that contains it — at a path that was given, in a file that opens.
perspectives.reads: Absent and insufficient are different claims. A reader who opened the work and judged it thin would say thin; the word missing describes a surface, and the surface may not be the one the work is on.
perspectives.does: Checks what the given path actually resolves to for someone with no context: default branch, first screen, whether the work sits under another organisation's account.

perspectives.sees: A profile and a link. Opening the link leads to a listing whose relevance is not decidable without reading code.
perspectives.reads: The submission is a claim to be passed on, not one to be assessed here. What can be checked at this desk is whether the requirement's keywords appear.
perspectives.does: Records against the requirement using what the profile states, and forwards the link unopened to whoever can read it.

perspectives.sees: A repository opened for a few minutes between meetings, landing on whatever the default branch shows first.
perspectives.reads: What the first screen shows stands for the whole, because there is no time to establish that it does not. A layout that buries the work reads the same as an absence of it.
perspectives.does: Writes the note against what was seen, in the vocabulary of what was expected to be there.

non_inferences: Does not establish that the work was never opened, only that the claim and the submission disagree.
Does not establish that the work would have met the bar had it been read.

title: Feedback stating candidate is overqualified for the grade
content:
# Feedback stating candidate is overqualified for the grade

Candidate is rejected on the grounds that their experience, seniority, or previous scope sits above the band the role was opened at.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not imply the candidate is undesirable; what it names is a concern about retention and about a pay mismatch.
summary: Candidate is rejected on the grounds that their experience, seniority, or previous scope sits above the band the role was opened at.

probes.action: Ask whether the organisation has requisitions open at a higher band or at staff level, where the wider scope is part of the role.
probes.expected_signal: Shows whether anything is open above this band.

outcomes.label: A reply names an open requisition at a higher level and gives a next step for it: a link, an introduction, or a referral.
outcomes.because: Active referral to an unblocked higher level band rules out structural down-levelling with a hard ceiling.

outcomes.label: A reply answers about level and names no requisition: nothing is open above this band, or the profile stays on file, or a pointer to the careers page — no requisition id, no date.
The reply answers about money rather than level: it names the approved ceiling for the closed requisition, or says the stated expectation sat above it.
outcomes.because: Stating rigid departmental budget ceilings rather than technical qualification gaps confirms pay band constraints rather than skill deficiencies.

outcomes.label: No reply arrives, and the thread ends on the rejection already received.

specimens.label: Rejection email
specimens.subject: Your application — Senior Backend Engineer

lines.text: Thank you for the time you gave us over the past two weeks. The team enjoyed the conversation and rated your systems background highly.

After discussion we have decided not to move forward. Your experience sits above the band we scoped for this role, and we were concerned the day-to-day would not stay interesting for you for very long.
We would be glad to keep your profile on file and reach out when something at the right level opens up.

specimens.reading: The stated ground is fit with a band, not the quality of the work — and the risk named is retention, not capability.

specimens.label: Recruiter screen, transcript fragment

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Your last role was a team lead position, is that right?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Formally, yes. In practice about two thirds of my week was hands-on.

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Got it. I will be honest with you — my worry is that this role is a step down, and six months in you would be looking again.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Right now I am optimising for depth rather than scope.

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Understood. I will pass that on either way.

specimens.reading: The concern is raised before any technical assessment: the level question is being settled ahead of the skill question.

perspectives.sees: A rejection naming experience above the band scoped for the role, and a retention concern raised at the screen, before any technical round.
perspectives.reads: The stated ground is fit with a band rather than the work shown. The message does not say whether a requisition at another level exists.
perspectives.does: Asks whether anything is open at a higher level, and records the stated reason and the date it was given.

perspectives.sees: A profile whose last title sits above the role, against a requisition opened at one band that the screen cannot move.
perspectives.reads: The level question is answerable now, and the same mismatch found at offer stage costs the search weeks. What the hiring manager will accept at this level is not written down anywhere the recruiter can read it.
perspectives.does: Raises the concern on the call and passes the answer on. Changing the band is not theirs to do; the wording of the rejection is.

perspectives.sees: A candidate who has previously held a wider scope than the role carries, assessed at the level the requisition was opened at.
perspectives.reads: A hire who leaves early is visible and attributed to the person who made it; a candidate declined on level leaves no record anyone reads later.
perspectives.does: Declines at this band, or asks for the level to be reconsidered, which means a different requisition funded elsewhere.

perspectives.sees: One requisition approved at one band, and a levelling grid that defines what sits above it. Individual candidates do not reach this layer.
perspectives.reads: One band per requisition is what keeps offers consistent and defensible across every hire. A person declined at the edge of the grid is not an event this layer records.
perspectives.does: Holds the requisition at the approved band. Opening one at a higher level is a separate funding decision on a quarterly cycle.

non_inferences: Does not imply the candidate is undesirable; what it names is a concern about retention and about a pay mismatch.

title: Generic "closer alignment" rejection template
content:
# Generic "closer alignment" rejection template

A standard automated email saying that the team has decided to proceed with candidates whose profiles match the requirements of the role more closely.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not establish which specific skill was deemed insufficient.
- Does not establish whether a human reviewer read the full resume.
summary: A standard automated email saying that the team has decided to proceed with candidates whose profiles match the requirements of the role more closely.

probes.action: Compare the wording of the CV with the exact requirement phrases in the published job description.
probes.expected_signal: Reveals a possible vocabulary mismatch between the candidate's wording and the ATS rubric.

outcomes.label: Every phrase the posting names — the acronyms, the named tools, the certifications, the years figure — appears in the CV as sent, in the posting's own wording, and the dated history covers the years figure.
One or more required phrases appear nowhere in the CV, while the work behind them is described there in different vocabulary — another tool name, a job title, a project description.
A requirement the posting states as a number or a named credential is not covered by the CV: fewer years in the dated history than the figure, or a certification the CV does not hold.
There is nothing to compare against: the posting has been taken down, or the text now on the page differs from the version applied to and no copy of that version was kept.

specimens.label: Rejection email
specimens.subject: Update on your application

lines.text: Thank you for your interest in our company and for the time you invested in the process.
After careful consideration we have decided to move forward with candidates whose profiles more closely align with the requirements of the role.
We wish you the best in your search and encourage you to apply for future openings.

specimens.reading: Nothing in the text is specific to this candidate, this conversation or this role. The message is a routing decision rendered as prose.

specimens.label: Request for specifics, and the reply

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Thanks for letting me know. If it is possible, I would value one line on which requirement was the gap — it would genuinely help me aim better.

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Unfortunately we are not able to share individual feedback. It was a very competitive process.

specimens.reading: The follow-up returns the same shape of answer. A template that survives a direct question is a policy, not an opinion about you.

perspectives.sees: A message sent at 03:14 with no sentence specific to this candidate, this role or this conversation, and a follow-up that returns the same wording.
perspectives.reads: The text is the standard wording for this outcome. Which requirement was the gap is not stated in it, and asking returned the template again.
perspectives.does: Records the date and the exact wording, and compares the wording of the CV against the requirements as they were published, since the message names no gap to work from.

perspectives.sees: A rejection step in the queue and, afterwards, a request for one line of specifics.
perspectives.reads: The wording is the one approved for this outcome; what the panel scored beyond a recommendation is not in the recruiter's record either.
perspectives.does: Sends the approved wording and answers within it, because anything more specific is quoted back afterwards as a stated reason.

perspectives.sees: One approved wording covering every rejection at every stage, and the disclosure rule that sets what may be given as a reason.
perspectives.reads: Identical wording across all outcomes is what makes each of them consistent and defensible if any one is challenged.
perspectives.does: Sets the template once for the whole funnel; the hours a candidate spends inferring a reason from it are not a figure this layer holds.

non_inferences: Does not establish which specific skill was deemed insufficient.
Does not establish whether a human reviewer read the full resume.

title: Materially similar role reposted shortly after rejection
content:
# Materially similar role reposted shortly after rejection

The same listing, or a near-identical one, is reposted or refreshed on the job boards within 1–8 weeks of the rejection.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not establish that the role was a "fake" or "ghost" posting.
- Does not establish that the prior interview feedback was fraudulent.
summary: The same listing, or a near-identical one, is reposted or refreshed on the job boards within 1–8 weeks of the rejection.

probes.action: Check the requisition ID on the listing, or ask the recruiter whether the posting is an automated ATS refresh or a separate headcount opening.
probes.expected_signal: Distinguishes an automated refresh on the job board from a genuinely recurring hiring need.

outcomes.label: The listing carries the requisition number you applied against, and the recruiter says the board re-posts it on a fixed interval; the record itself has not changed.
The listing carries a requisition number that did not exist when you applied, and the recruiter describes it as a separately approved opening on the same team.
The recruiter answers that the team stopped hiring for this and the listing should not still be up; it comes down within days.
The board shows no requisition number and the question goes unanswered; the two posted dates and the identical body text are all you hold.

specimens.label: The two postings, side by side
specimens.context: rejection on 14 March, repost seen on 2 April

lines.text: 14 Mar — Senior Backend Engineer · Payments · Remote (EU) · 5+ years · Go, PostgreSQL, Kafka · req #4471
2 Apr — Senior Backend Engineer · Payments · Remote (EU) · 5+ years · Go, PostgreSQL, Kafka · req #4471
Body text identical except for the posted date. Same requisition number, same team, same band.

specimens.reading: The requisition number is the thing to record. A refreshed listing and a genuinely new headcount look identical on the board and are different facts underneath.

specimens.label: Asking the recruiter directly

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: I saw req #4471 posted again this week. Is this a second opening on the team, or the same one refreshed?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Good catch — the board auto-refreshes listings after 30 days so they stay visible. Same requisition, still open.

specimens.reading: One question separated an automated refresh from a real second opening. This is the cheapest probe in the whole registry.

perspectives.sees: The same requisition number, team and band on a listing whose posted date has moved, with the body text otherwise unchanged.
perspectives.reads: A refreshed listing and a second opening look the same on the board. The requisition number is what separates them, and one question resolved which it was.
perspectives.does: Records both dates and the requisition number, and asks the recruiter directly, which costs one message.

perspectives.sees: One requisition record and a syndication schedule that re-posts a listing when it passes the configured interval.
perspectives.reads: Whether a listing stays in the visible window on a board is a distribution setting. Nothing about who was rejected enters that path.
perspectives.does: Refreshes the posted date on the interval the customer's configuration sets, and the board shows the listing as new.

perspectives.sees: The same requisition open on their own board with an unchanged number, and a question about it in the inbox.
perspectives.reads: The repost is the board's refresh cycle rather than a decision anyone took after the rejection.
perspectives.does: Answers it, since the requisition number and the refresh interval are facts that cannot be quoted back as a commitment.

non_inferences: Does not establish that the role was a "fake" or "ghost" posting.
Does not establish that the prior interview feedback was fraudulent.

title: Multiple interview reschedulings or interviewer no-show
content:
# Multiple interview reschedulings or interviewer no-show

Interviews are postponed repeatedly or moved at short notice, or the interviewer does not join the call at the scheduled time.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not imply candidate rejection; frequently reflects interviewer calendar congestion or emergency incidents.
summary: Interviews are postponed repeatedly or moved at short notice, or the interviewer does not join the call at the scheduled time.

probes.action: Offer a set of concrete times you are free, and confirm the contact details 2 hours before the call.
probes.expected_signal: Minimises scheduling friction and shows how quickly the recruiter answers.

outcomes.label: One of the offered times is confirmed, the two-hour check is answered, and the interview runs at that time.
A time is confirmed and then withdrawn by the organiser again, with a replacement date offered in the same message.
The time stands, the two-hour check goes unanswered, and no one joins the call at that time.
The availability message goes unanswered and no new date arrives.

specimens.label: Scheduling thread

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Tuesday 14:00 works for the panel — sending the invite now.

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Apologies, the interviewer has a conflict. Can we move to Thursday same time?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Sorry to do this again — Thursday is out. Would Monday work?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Something urgent came up on the team. I will come back to you with new slots.

specimens.reading: Four moves, no interview. Record the dates: a pattern of postponement is evidence about the process, not about the candidate.

specimens.label: Calendar record

lines.text: Invite sent — Technical panel
Cancelled by organiser
Invite sent — Technical panel
Cancelled by organiser · no replacement issued

specimens.reading: Every cancellation came from the same side. That asymmetry is the observable part.

perspectives.sees: Four dates for one interview, invitations withdrawn by the organiser each time, and a fourth message with no replacement slot in it.
perspectives.reads: Something on the other side is moving, and which thing it is — a calendar, a panel, a requisition — is not in any message received.
perspectives.does: Records the dates and the wording, keeps other processes open, and asks for a date rather than for a reason.

perspectives.sees: Declines coming back from the panel's calendar, and no instruction about whether the search itself has changed.
perspectives.reads: A slot to reissue. Whether the requisition is still funded is not visible from the scheduling view.
perspectives.does: Sends new times and keeps the candidate in the pipeline; no cause arrives with the decline, so none travels onward.

perspectives.sees: One conflict on one morning, resolved by moving one invitation. The series exists in the candidate's inbox, not in the panel's calendar.
perspectives.reads: A week in which delivery and the loop need the same hours, and the loop is the part that can be moved.
perspectives.does: Releases the slot to the work the role exists to absorb and asks for a new time, each move decided on its own.

non_inferences: Does not imply candidate rejection; frequently reflects interviewer calendar congestion or emergency incidents.

title: Offer accepted followed by delayed start date or post-signing revocation
content:
# Offer accepted followed by delayed start date or post-signing revocation

A signed offer is met with repeated start-date delays, pre-day-one communication freezes, or sudden revocation during early onboarding.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not establish that the candidate's performance or background check caused the delay.
- Does not establish that the role was fraudulent when the offer was originally issued.
summary: A signed offer is met with repeated start-date delays, pre-day-one communication freezes, or sudden revocation during early onboarding.

probes.action: Request written confirmation of the revised start date alongside written clarification of whether hardware shipment and payroll registration remain active.
probes.expected_signal: Separates an administrative IT delay from a structural hiring freeze or pre-start headcount cancellation.

outcomes.label: The employer confirms the date with tracking details for onboarding equipment.
outcomes.because: Active equipment dispatch and confirmed start date rule out pre-start headcount freeze and offer revocation.

outcomes.label: The employer provides vague holding notices without committing to a fixed onboarding date.
outcomes.because: Evasive holding notices without confirmed dates contradict an honest post-offer onboarding path.

outcomes.label: The employer confirms headcount revocation or indefinite pause prior to start date.
outcomes.because: Confirmed headcount cancellation prior to day one directly contradicts an honest hire.

specimens.label: Post-acceptance start date slippage
specimens.subject: Update on your upcoming start date

lines.text: We are excited to welcome you next Monday!
Due to internal team restructuring, we need to push your start date by three weeks.
We are still finalizing leadership approvals for the revised onboarding date.

specimens.reading: The delay occurs after the candidate has resigned from previous employment, shifting contractual risk entirely onto the worker.

perspectives.sees: A confirmed start date deferred after notice was given to a prior employer, leaving their career runway exposed.
perspectives.reads: Start-date slippage signals unbudgeted headcount risk or an unannounced internal hiring pause.
perspectives.does: Requests clear written documentation of employment status and assesses legal and search alternatives.

perspectives.sees: An onboarding ticket blocked by finance or department leadership pending quarterly budget reconciliation.
perspectives.reads: The offer was extended under previous headcount assumptions that changed before start day.
perspectives.does: Relays holding messages while awaiting confirmation on whether the placement can proceed.

perspectives.sees: Quarterly headcount adjustments or project scope revisions occurring between offer acceptance and payroll commencement.
perspectives.reads: Pushing start dates preserves budget flexibility before formal employment liability attaches.
perspectives.does: Enforces hiring pauses across pending pipeline offers where commercial conditions shift.

non_inferences: Does not establish that the candidate's performance or background check caused the delay.
Does not establish that the role was fraudulent when the offer was originally issued.

title: Offer rescinded or delayed due to internal freeze
content:
# Offer rescinded or delayed due to internal freeze

Candidate is offered a role verbally or in writing, and the offer is then delayed or withdrawn before the start date.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not mean the candidate failed a reference check, unless the message says so.
summary: Candidate is offered a role verbally or in writing, and the offer is then delayed or withdrawn before the start date.

probes.action: Ask for written notice of whether the requisition is cancelled outright or deferred to the next fiscal quarter.
probes.expected_signal: Establishes whether there is a date to wait for.

outcomes.label: A written reply states that the requisition is paused rather than closed, names the quarter or the date on which the freeze is reviewed, and says the offer is revisited if headcount returns.
outcomes.because: A formal written pause date confirms a genuine headcount freeze (mech.headcount_freeze_or_budget_cancellation) rather than an honest hire or an evergreen ghost posting.

outcomes.label: A written reply states that the requisition is closed and the headcount withdrawn, and names no date to return to.
outcomes.because: Definitive written headcount cancellation after offer issuance directly confirms retraction.

outcomes.label: A written reply confirms the freeze and its scope — every open requisition, other offers in the same position — and states that whether the role is cancelled or deferred is not known from inside the hiring process.
outcomes.because: Company-wide freeze confirmation confirms systemic budget suspension.

outcomes.label: Nothing further arrives in writing: the answer is given verbally, or the thread stops, and the two dated documents already held remain the whole record.

specimens.label: The offer, then the retraction
specimens.subject: Offer — Senior Backend Engineer

lines.text: Day 0 — Delighted to confirm the offer we discussed. Start date 1 June, contract attached for signature.
Day 9 — I am very sorry to write this. A company-wide hiring freeze was announced this morning and all outstanding offers are suspended, including yours.
Day 9 — I understand you may have given notice. Please tell me if there is anything I can do, and I will be honest with you about what I can and cannot influence.

specimens.reading: Two dated documents about the same role. Whatever happens next, the fact that a written offer existed on day 0 is established, not remembered.

specimens.label: Establishing the scope of the freeze

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Is the freeze specific to the team, or company-wide?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Company-wide. Every open req is paused, and three other offers are in the same position as yours.

specimens.reading: The answer places the cause outside the hiring loop and outside the candidate. It also makes the claim checkable against public news.

perspectives.sees: A written offer with a start date, then a message before that date saying outstanding offers are suspended. Notice may already have been given at the current employer.
perspectives.reads: The stated cause sits above the hiring loop, and the message does not say whether the role is cancelled or deferred. Two dated documents about the same role now exist.
perspectives.does: Asks in writing whether the requisition is cancelled or deferred and to which quarter, keeps both messages, and reopens the processes that were paused.

perspectives.sees: An instruction that every open requisition is paused, arriving the same morning it arrives for everyone else, and a list of candidates to notify that includes one already holding a written offer.
perspectives.reads: The commitment that was conveyed rests on an authority the recruiter does not hold, and whether headcount returns this quarter is not visible from inside the funnel.
perspectives.does: Writes the message and chooses its wording. Can state the scope of the freeze and that other offers are in the same position; cannot give a start date.

perspectives.sees: A headcount decision applied to every open requisition at once. What reaches this layer is a count of paused requisitions and the spend it holds back.
perspectives.reads: A pause preserves optionality: an approved requisition that can be stopped costs less than one that cannot. Offers already extended are part of that count.
perspectives.does: Sets the scope of the freeze and the date it is reviewed. Resignations already handed in on the other side of those offers are not a figure this layer holds.

non_inferences: Does not mean the candidate failed a reference check, unless the message says so.

title: Position closed after final interview without hire
content:
# Position closed after final interview without hire

The candidate completes every interview round and then learns that the requisition has been cancelled, frozen, or closed.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not prove that the candidate failed the technical or behavioural evaluations.
- Does not prove that the company misstated its intention in opening the role.
summary: The candidate completes every interview round and then learns that the requisition has been cancelled, frozen, or closed.

probes.action: Ask the recruiter whether the role was closed by a budget restructuring or by a reallocation of the work inside the team.
probes.expected_signal: Clarifies whether the barrier was specific to this candidate or budgetary.

outcomes.label: The recruiter answers and names a funding decision and its scope in writing: the requisition unfunded for the quarter, or a hold covering more than this one role.
The recruiter answers that the work was reallocated — taken on by the existing team or covered by someone already inside — and that no external hire is being made.
The recruiter answers that the search did not stop: the requisition has been re-scoped or re-levelled and is now being worked against a different profile.
No reply arrives, or the reply repeats the wording of the closing email and adds nothing that separates a budget decision from a team one.

specimens.label: Final round, closing minutes
specimens.context: minute 47 of 50, four days before the email below

lines.speaker: Hiring manager
lines.text: That is everything from our side. Any questions for us?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Only about timing — what happens next?

lines.speaker: Hiring manager
lines.text: We are wrapping up the loop this week. You are the last of three finalists, so expect to hear back by Friday at the latest.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Understood. Thank you for the time.

specimens.reading: The process was described as live and near a decision. Whatever happened next happened after this point, not before it.

specimens.label: Rejection email
specimens.subject: Regarding the Senior Backend Engineer search

lines.text: Thank you again for the conversations over the past six weeks — the panel was consistently positive about your work.
I am writing with disappointing news: the requisition has been put on hold as part of a wider planning review, and we will not be filling the role this quarter.
This is not a reflection on your interviews. If the role reopens I would like to come back to you first.

specimens.reading: The stated cause sits above the hiring loop entirely. A candidate cannot pass or fail a budget review.

perspectives.sees: A final round described in its closing minutes as one week from a decision, and an email four days later naming a planning review as the cause.
perspectives.reads: The stated cause sits above the interview loop. What the panel concluded did not determine the outcome, and the six weeks are already spent.
perspectives.does: Records the dates, the panel's own stated position and the wording of the close, and asks whether the requisition was frozen or cancelled.

perspectives.sees: A loop they ran to its end, a panel recommendation they can act on, and a requisition removed from the plan by a decision taken elsewhere.
perspectives.reads: The outcome of the loop no longer decides anything. The gap the role exists to absorb is still open and still covered by the team.
perspectives.does: Keeps the shortlist and returns to the same names if the requisition comes back, because funding it is not something this role controls.

perspectives.sees: Open requisitions as funded line items in a planning review held on a quarterly cycle.
perspectives.reads: An approved requisition that can be paused costs less than one that cannot; pausing is the instrument the approval was written to allow.
perspectives.does: Puts the requisition on hold. The stage each candidate had reached is not a field the review carries.

non_inferences: Does not prove that the candidate failed the technical or behavioural evaluations.
Does not prove that the company misstated its intention in opening the role.

title: Rejection after the application sat pending for months
content:
# Rejection after the application sat pending for months

A rejection arrives six weeks or more after submission, with no contact in the interval and no stage ever entered.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not mean the application was read at any point during the interval.
- Does not mean a decision on the merits was taken at the end of it.
summary: A rejection arrives six weeks or more after submission, with no contact in the interval and no stage ever entered.

probes.action: Compare the date the posting came down with the date the rejection arrived, using the portal's own listing history or a saved copy of the posting.
probes.expected_signal: Establishes whether the message followed the close of the search or an interval counted from submission.

outcomes.label: The posting came down first, and the message followed within days of it.
The message arrived a round number of days after submission — thirty, forty-five, sixty — and the posting's state did not change around it.
outcomes.because: A rejection arriving on a round calendar interval (e.g. 30/60 days) demonstrates an automated ATS queue expiry rule (mech.employment_gap_downranking_bias) rather than an active reviewer decision.

outcomes.label: The posting was still accepting applications when the rejection arrived.
outcomes.because: A rejection arriving while the role remains active and seeking candidates indicates an automated knockout filter or ghost listing (mech.stale_or_orphaned_job_requisition/mech.automated_keyword_qualification_filter).

outcomes.label: The posting's history cannot be recovered and no copy was kept.

specimens.label: Application timeline

lines.text: Application submitted
Status: Under review
Status: Not selected
Notification email queued

specimens.reading: Sixty days between the two status lines, and nothing recorded in between. The record's history shows one transition, not a review.

specimens.label: Rejection email
specimens.subject: Update on your application

lines.text: Thank you for your interest. We have decided not to move forward with your application at this time.
We encourage you to apply for future openings that match your background.
No stage is named, and none was entered.

specimens.reading: The message is written to close a record, not to report a decision about one. Nothing in it distinguishes the sixtieth day from the first.

perspectives.sees: A submission in one month and a rejection in another, with nothing between them: no acknowledgement beyond the automatic one, no question, no stage.
perspectives.reads: The interval bounds nothing on its own. A long wait is equally consistent with a queue that never reached the record and with a threshold that closed it on a date.
perspectives.does: Checks whether the posting stayed live through the interval and whether the portal shows a status that changed before the message arrived, because those are the two things the interval can be compared against.

perspectives.sees: A requisition that has been closed for weeks and a disposition list that still has to be cleared before the quarter's reporting.
perspectives.reads: Records that never entered the queue are not decisions deferred; they are decisions the queue never had capacity to reach.
perspectives.does: Clears the outstanding dispositions in one operation, because the alternative is leaving them open against a requisition that no longer exists.

perspectives.sees: A retention rule firing against every record still in a pending state past the configured interval, and one notification queued per record.
perspectives.reads: The configuration ran on schedule. Whether any of those records was ever opened is not a condition the rule tests.
perspectives.does: Transitions the records, queues the notifications, and reports the cleared backlog as pipeline hygiene.

non_inferences: Does not mean the application was read at any point during the interval.
Does not mean a decision on the merits was taken at the end of it.

title: Rejection naming a jurisdiction or work-eligibility ground
content:
# Rejection naming a jurisdiction or work-eligibility ground

The stated reason is where the candidate lives, the hours they can cover, or the right to be employed there — not anything about the work.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not establish that no route to employment existed, only that none was used here.
- Does not establish that the constraint was the first ground on which the application was set aside.
summary: The stated reason is where the candidate lives, the hours they can cover, or the right to be employed there — not anything about the work.

probes.action: Compare the ground named in the message against the copy of the posting as it stood on the day of application.
probes.expected_signal: Establishes whether the ground was stated up front or introduced afterwards.

outcomes.label: The posting stated the same constraint, in the same terms, before the application was made.
outcomes.because: An upfront explicit location constraint rules out post-hoc constraint injection and location bait-and-switch.

outcomes.label: The posting said nothing about the constraint, or stated a wider one.
outcomes.because: Rejecting on an unstated location constraint contradicts an honest baseline evaluation against published terms.

outcomes.label: The posting now carries the constraint, and the saved copy shows it did not.
outcomes.because: Retroactively editing criteria after applications arrive contradicts honest process standards.

outcomes.label: No copy of the posting as applied to was kept, and the listing has changed or gone.

specimens.label: Recruiter reply
specimens.subject: Re: your application

lines.text: Thanks for your time on the call earlier this week.
We are not able to employ in your country of residence for this role, so we cannot take this forward.
If that changes on your side, do let us know.

specimens.reading: The ground is checkable against a document, which almost no other stated reason is. That makes it worth checking — and checkable is not the same as operative.

perspectives.sees: A reason that can be checked against the posting: a country, a set of hours, a permit. Unlike most stated reasons, this one refers to a fact rather than a judgement.
perspectives.reads: The ground named is verifiable, which is unusual. Whether it was the operative ground, or the one that could be written down without commenting on the candidate, is not settled by the message.
perspectives.does: Compares the ground against what the posting stated when it was applied to, using a saved copy, because a posting can be edited after the fact.

perspectives.sees: A candidate the team would take and a hiring location list that does not include where they are.
perspectives.reads: This is the one closing reason that is fully outside the candidate and fully inside a document. It can be stated without hedging.
perspectives.does: Names the ground plainly, because doing so is both accurate and easier than a template that would invite a follow-up.

perspectives.sees: A list of jurisdictions in which a contract can be issued, set by which entities and payroll providers exist, and reviewed on a slower cycle than any single search.
perspectives.reads: The list is a constraint on the search, not an assessment within it. Roles are published against it, and exceptions cost more than a single hire usually justifies.
perspectives.does: Holds the list, and grants exceptions through a route that runs on a different calendar from the requisition.

non_inferences: Does not establish that no route to employment existed, only that none was used here.
Does not establish that the constraint was the first ground on which the application was set aside.

title: Rejection naming a specific industry sector as required
content:
# Rejection naming a specific industry sector as required

The stated reason is the absence of experience in one named sector, rather than the depth or correctness of the work assessed.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not establish that the sector was irrelevant to the work.
- Does not establish that the assessed work fell short in any respect.
summary: The stated reason is the absence of experience in one named sector, rather than the depth or correctness of the work assessed.

probes.action: Compare the sector named in the message against the requirements section of the posting as it stood on the day of application.
probes.expected_signal: Establishes whether the sector was listed as required, listed as preferred, or absent.

outcomes.label: The posting named the sector among the requirements.
outcomes.because: An explicit mandatory requirement stated up front rules out covert post-hoc goalpost shifting.

outcomes.label: The posting named the sector, among preferences or nice-to-haves rather than requirements.
The posting did not mention the sector at all.
outcomes.because: Disqualifying a candidate over an unmentioned sector criterion contradicts an honest evaluation against published standards.

outcomes.label: No copy of the posting as applied to was kept.

specimens.label: Feedback after the technical round
specimens.subject: Following your technical session

lines.text: The exercise was solid and the reasoning about failure modes was strong.
The team decided to go with someone who has already worked in the payments domain.
We would be happy to talk again for a role where that is less central.

specimens.reading: The work is assessed positively and the ground for the decision is elsewhere. That combination is what makes the sector legible as the operative line — and leaves open how heavily it was weighed.

perspectives.sees: A reason that names an industry rather than a capability: payments, health, advertising, trading — a sector the candidate has not worked in, stated as the thing that was missing.
perspectives.reads: The sector is a real difference. Whether it is a difference in what the work requires, or a proxy standing in for that, the message does not distinguish — and the two look identical from outside.
perspectives.does: Compares the sector named against the requirements the posting listed, because a requirement that appears only in the closing message appeared somewhere between the two.

perspectives.sees: Two candidates who can both build the system, one of whom has already met the constraints this sector imposes and will not spend the first quarter discovering them.
perspectives.reads: Sector context is a real cost, paid in ramp-up time that the team carries. Weighing it is judgement, not a rule, and nothing in the process asks how much of it was weighed.
perspectives.does: States the difference plainly, because it is the most concrete thing that separated two people who both passed.

perspectives.sees: A requirement that was written into the search brief as a preference and is now being applied as a threshold.
perspectives.reads: Preferences and thresholds are recorded in the same field. Which one a line was is decided when it is used, not when it is written.
perspectives.does: Passes the reason on in the manager's words, because it is specific enough to send and not attributable to anything the recruiter assessed.

non_inferences: Does not establish that the sector was irrelevant to the work.
Does not establish that the assessed work fell short in any respect.

title: Rejection naming an internal hire as the outcome
content:
# Rejection naming an internal hire as the outcome

The closing message states the role went to someone already inside the organisation, after the candidate had completed the later rounds.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not establish that the internal candidate was identified before the search was published.
- Does not establish that the external rounds were run without a decision available to them.
summary: The closing message states the role went to someone already inside the organisation, after the candidate had completed the later rounds.

probes.action: Check whether the posting was withdrawn or remained live, and whether it was reposted with the same level and scope within the following weeks.
probes.expected_signal: Distinguishes a filled requisition from a search that continued after the message.

outcomes.label: The posting came down and no materially similar role appeared afterwards.
outcomes.because: Clean requisition withdrawal without reposting is incompatible with an evergreen ghost opening.

outcomes.label: A role with the same level and scope was published again within weeks.
outcomes.because: Immediate reposting of the identical role contradicts honest closure via internal transfer.

outcomes.label: The posting continued to accept applications after the message arrived.
outcomes.because: A requisition that continues accepting applications while claiming an internal hire contradicts honest closure.

outcomes.label: The posting's state after the message cannot be established.

specimens.label: Closing message
specimens.subject: Update following your final round

lines.text: Thank you for the time you gave this process, and for the work you prepared for the final session.
We have filled the role with a candidate from inside the company.
We would be glad to keep your details for future openings on the team.

specimens.reading: The one specific sentence in the message is about where the hire came from, not about the candidate. That specificity is what separates this from a template, and it is also the limit of what it reports.

perspectives.sees: A message that names where the hire came from, arriving after several rounds that were scheduled, attended and prepared for.
perspectives.reads: The sentence establishes where the role landed. It does not establish when that became likely, and the difference between those two is the whole of what the candidate wants to know.
perspectives.does: Notes what was asked in the later rounds — whether the questions were about the work or about the team's existing plans — because that is the only record of what the process was doing while it ran.

perspectives.sees: An internal transfer that resolves a headcount problem without a notice period, alongside an external shortlist that was assembled in case it did not.
perspectives.reads: Both routes were live. One closed first, and the requisition needed one person, not the better of two processes.
perspectives.does: Asks for the external rounds to be closed out, and writes a reason short enough to be sent unchanged to everyone still open.

perspectives.sees: A requisition marked filled with an internal disposition code, and a shortlist of external candidates who now need messages.
perspectives.reads: The disposition is accurate and unusually specific — most closing reasons are not this legible from outside.
perspectives.does: Sends the stated reason rather than the generic template, because the internal outcome is the one closing reason that can be given without commenting on any candidate.

non_inferences: Does not establish that the internal candidate was identified before the search was published.
Does not establish that the external rounds were run without a decision available to them.

title: Rejection within minutes of application submission
content:
# Rejection within minutes of application submission

Automated rejection email arrives within 2 to 30 minutes of form submission, outside business hours.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not mean a human engineer read the resume and judged it poor.
summary: Automated rejection email arrives within 2 to 30 minutes of form submission, outside business hours.

probes.action: Audit the application answers to the mandatory knock-out questions (work permit, country of residence, minimum years of experience).
probes.expected_signal: Identifies which boolean filter rule the ATS applied.

outcomes.label: The answers are as intended, and one of them falls outside a condition the posting states: a country outside the listed hiring locations, no permit where the posting requires one, or fewer years than the stated minimum.
The answers are as intended, and every mandatory one meets the conditions the posting states.
The stored application shows an answer other than the one intended — a field left blank, or a dropdown submitted at its default value.
The answers cannot be retrieved: the portal shows no submitted application and no confirmation copy was kept.

specimens.label: Rejection email
specimens.subject: Your application

lines.text: Thank you for applying. After reviewing your application we have decided not to proceed at this time.
Sent 23:58 — eleven minutes after submission, outside working hours in every timezone the company operates in.

specimens.reading: The interval is the evidence. Eleven minutes at midnight describes the throughput of a rule, not the attention of a reader.

specimens.label: Application timeline

lines.text: Application submitted
Screening rules evaluated
Status: Rejected — does not meet minimum criteria
Notification email queued

specimens.reading: Two seconds between submission and decision. The eleven-minute delay was the mail queue, not deliberation.

perspectives.sees: A submission at 23:47 and a rejection at 23:58, outside working hours in every timezone the employer operates in.
perspectives.reads: Eleven minutes bounds how much reading could have happened; whether a person or a rule closed the record is not in the message.
perspectives.does: Reviews the answers given to the mandatory questions — permit, country, years of experience — because that is the only part of the decision the candidate holds a copy of.

perspectives.sees: A weekly figure: applications received, applications screened. This application sits inside the difference between the two and never enters the review queue.
perspectives.reads: The pipeline is a count against a capacity limit; a record closed at ingestion is not part of the work the queue holds.
perspectives.does: Works the queue that capacity allows, and answers a follow-up, if one arrives, from the status field, which reads that the minimum criteria were not met.

perspectives.sees: A submission, a rules evaluation two seconds later, a status transition and a queued notification. All four are events, and none of them is a reading of the profile.
perspectives.reads: The configuration ran as configured. Whether the criterion it enforced is the one the customer meant is not a value the platform holds.
perspectives.does: Sends the templated notification, records the disposition, and reports the interval as throughput on the dashboard the buyer evaluates.

non_inferences: Does not mean a human engineer read the resume and judged it poor.

title: Republished job posting with refreshed date and identical requirement body
content:
# Republished job posting with refreshed date and identical requirement body

An opening is closed or reposted with an updated timestamp and identical requirement text, resetting applicant queues while preserving candidate pipeline collection.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not establish that previous applicants were rejected on qualification grounds.
- Does not establish that a confirmed budget line exists for immediate onboarding.
summary: An opening is closed or reposted with an updated timestamp and identical requirement text, resetting applicant queues while preserving candidate pipeline collection.

probes.action: Compare the requirement text hash against prior archive snapshots and ask the recruiter if active interviewing has commenced.
probes.expected_signal: Separates an active newly funded replacement hire from an evergreen talent pool or stale posting refresh.

outcomes.label: The recruiter confirms an active search with initial screening calls scheduled within the week.
outcomes.because: An active screening schedule is incompatible with a ghost requisition maintained without hiring intent.

outcomes.label: The recruiter confirms the listing is maintained continuously for future project demand.
outcomes.because: An evergreen pipeline posting is incompatible with an honest baseline search for an immediate single opening.

specimens.label: Job board repost notification

lines.text: Senior Systems Engineer · Posted 45 days ago · 120 applicants
Senior Systems Engineer · Posted 2 hours ago · 3 applicants
Job description, tech stack, and experience criteria: 100% identical

specimens.reading: The refreshed publication date simulates immediate demand while resetting algorithmic visibility and applicant counters.

perspectives.sees: A newly posted opening matching their skillset, suggesting an urgent active search.
perspectives.reads: The position has just opened and early applications will receive prompt review.
perspectives.does: Customizes resume and submits application within the initial 24-hour window.

perspectives.sees: An automated posting refresh scheduled in the ATS to keep the requisition at the top of candidate search feeds.
perspectives.reads: Refreshing the date restores organic applicant volume after the initial post decays.
perspectives.does: Monitors incoming CV volume while sorting matches into long-term talent communities.

perspectives.sees: Continuous talent brand presence and pipeline generation across core engineering disciplines.
perspectives.reads: Sustained posting visibility minimizes time-to-hire when client or departmental headcount unlocks.
perspectives.does: Authorizes ongoing job board listings across foundational roles.

non_inferences: Does not establish that previous applicants were rejected on qualification grounds.
Does not establish that a confirmed budget line exists for immediate onboarding.

title: Take-home assignment exceeding reasonable stated scope
content:
# Take-home assignment exceeding reasonable stated scope

The take-home assignment asks for production-grade features that take 20+ hours to build, against a stated budget of 2–4 hours.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not prove the company is harvesting free intellectual property for production use.
summary: The take-home assignment asks for production-grade features that take 20+ hours to build, against a stated budget of 2–4 hours.

probes.action: Write the boundaries and trade-offs into the submission's README, naming the assumptions made to fit the agreed timebox.
probes.expected_signal: Tests whether evaluators value scope management and communication over unbounded free work.

outcomes.label: Written feedback, or the next conversation, refers to the timebox note and the cuts you named, and treats them as part of what was submitted.
The reply lists the stubbed items as missing work, with no reference to the note that names them as deliberate.
A rejection in standard wording arrives with nothing in it specific to the submission.
No reply arrives at all; the brief and the submission date are the only dated records you keep.

specimens.label: The assignment brief, as received
specimens.subject: Take-home exercise — Senior Backend Engineer

lines.text: Build a service that ingests order events, deduplicates them, and exposes a query API over the resulting state.

Requirements: persistence with migrations, idempotent consumers, retry with backoff, structured logging, metrics endpoint, containerised local run, integration tests, and a short design document covering scaling and failure modes.
Please submit within one week. We estimate 2–4 hours.

specimens.reading: Count the deliverables against the stated budget. The mismatch is measurable, which makes it a fact rather than a feeling.

specimens.label: Asking about scope

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Happy to do this. To fit the 2–4 hours, which parts should I treat as the core and which can I stub with a note in the README?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Ideally all of it — we use it to see how you work end to end.

specimens.reading: A direct question does not reconcile the stated budget with the expected deliverable. That is the observation; the reason for it is not visible from here.

perspectives.sees: A brief with eight requirements listed against a stated budget of two to four hours, and an answer to the scoping question that leaves the list unchanged.
perspectives.reads: The stated time and the stated deliverables are two different sizes, and which of the two the submission will be scored against is not written anywhere the candidate can reach.
perspectives.does: Decides how many unpaid hours to commit, and submits with the timebox, the deliberate cuts and the assumptions written into the README, keeping the brief and the reply on record.

perspectives.sees: A candidate asking which parts are core, and a brief that is the only document the recruiter holds about this exercise.
perspectives.reads: A question about scope is a question about the rubric, and the rubric sits with the panel; the stage is measured by how quickly it clears.
perspectives.does: Answers from the brief, since that is what the recruiter has, and returns the thread to a submission date.

perspectives.sees: Finished submissions. How long any of them took is not a field in what reaches the panel.
perspectives.reads: Differences in completeness read as differences in level, because completeness is the variable the submissions expose.
perspectives.does: Compares the batch against itself rather than against the stated budget, and sets the bar from the fullest submission received.

non_inferences: Does not prove the company is harvesting free intellectual property for production use.

title: Unsolicited recruiter outreach followed by ghosting
content:
# Unsolicited recruiter outreach followed by ghosting

Recruiter opens direct outreach expressing strong interest, then stops replying once the candidate answers with availability.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not prove the profile was rejected; often it is what an automated batch sourcing campaign looks like.
summary: Recruiter opens direct outreach expressing strong interest, then stops replying once the candidate answers with availability.

probes.action: Send one polite follow-up after five business days, on the original outreach thread.
probes.expected_signal: Recovers a stalled conversation if the recruiter was away or over capacity.

outcomes.label: Neither the follow-up nor the earlier answer is replied to, and the thread stays as it was: an outreach message, a same-day answer, and silence.
outcomes.because: Complete recruiter silence following initial candidate reply indicates discarded pipeline sourcing or talent pooling (mech.pre_selected_internal_candidate/mech.bid_conditional_talent_pool).

outcomes.label: The only thing that arrives is automated: an absence notice with a return date, or a notice that the address is no longer monitored. Nothing follows it from a person.
A person replies and the conversation continues: a call is booked, or the role is described in more detail.
outcomes.because: Active conversational resumption and call scheduling rule out speculative ghost sourcing and bench pooling.

outcomes.label: A reply arrives with no next step in it: the search is paused, the role is already filled, or there is no open requisition behind the outreach yet.
outcomes.because: Outreach without an active requisition behind it contradicts an immediate honest search.

specimens.label: Inbound outreach, then silence

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Hi! I came across your profile — your work on payment infrastructure is exactly what our team needs. Would you be open to a chat this week?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Thanks for reaching out. Yes, happy to talk. I am free Tuesday or Thursday after 15:00, and here is a short summary of what I have been working on.
— no reply —

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Following up in case this got buried. Still interested.
— no reply —

specimens.reading: The enthusiasm and the disappearance came from the same side, and the candidate did nothing between them except answer.

specimens.label: What was and was not established

lines.text: Established: an outreach message was sent on day 0; the candidate replied the same day with availability; two follow-ups went unanswered over eleven days.
Not established: whether the role existed, whether it was filled, whether anyone read the reply, or what the recruiter thought of the profile.

specimens.reading: Writing the two lists separately is the whole method. Most of the pain of this signal comes from filling the second list with guesses.

perspectives.sees: An inbound message naming their specific work, a same-day reply with availability, and then no answer — not to the availability, and not to a follow-up.
perspectives.reads: The approach and the silence came from the same side. Nothing in the thread separates a search that closed from a message no one opened.
perspectives.does: Sends one follow-up on the original thread, then treats the role as not live, and keeps the thread as a dated record of who started it.

perspectives.sees: A reply in an inbox that carries sourcing for several searches at once, beside a screening queue larger than the week's capacity.
perspectives.reads: A sourced reply is not an application, so it holds no position in the pipeline of record. Time-to-fill is measured; a thread with no requisition attached to it is not.
perspectives.does: Works the searches that are open now. Nothing in the queue raises the thread again, and no status message exists for a conversation that never became an application.

perspectives.sees: A sourcing sequence with a message sent and a reply received. The contact holds no application against any requisition.
perspectives.reads: A reply is a sequence outcome, not a pipeline stage. Nothing in the record marks the contact as awaiting an answer.
perspectives.does: Marks the sequence replied and stops sending. The expiry rule and the rejection template both key on an application, so neither fires here.

non_inferences: Does not prove the profile was rejected; often it is what an automated batch sourcing campaign looks like.

title: Requisition Approval & Public Posting
content:
# Requisition Approval & Public Posting

The gate that exists before any candidate does: headcount is authorised, the job description is written, and the requisition is published (or kept open) on careers pages and job boards.

### Pass Condition
An approved requisition with a written job description is published against real, funded headcount.
description: The gate that exists before any candidate does: headcount is authorised, the job description is written, and the requisition is published (or kept open) on careers pages and job boards.
pass_condition: An approved requisition with a written job description is published against real, funded headcount.

specimens.label: What was approved before anyone applied

lines.text: Headcount: 1 · Funded from: platform budget, FY approved · Level: L4 · Band: 68–79k
Job description drafted by the hiring manager, edited by recruiting, published unchanged.
Requirements list carried over from the previous L5 search for the same team.

specimens.reading: This gate closes before the first candidate exists, and it fixes the level, the band and the requirements that everyone downstream will be measured against.

perspectives.sees: A headcount request, a budget line, a level and a band. No candidate exists at this gate, so none is in the file.
perspectives.reads: A funded requisition is an option rather than a spend: it can be published, paused or carried into the next quarter without a new approval.
perspectives.does: Fixes the band, the level and whether the role must be posted externally at all, and hands the requisition down as fields the rest of the funnel treats as given.

perspectives.sees: The requisition form: a title, a level the grid allows, and a requirements list that can be carried over from the last search for this team.
perspectives.reads: The description is the one step where the bar is set in advance; everything after it is judging arrivals against a list already published.
perspectives.does: Writes the requirements into the fields the form has; what the form has no field for stays unwritten.

perspectives.sees: A published posting with a date on it. Whether the headcount behind it is funded, and at what level the assessment will run, are not part of what is published.
perspectives.reads: A live posting reads as a live search, and the requirements list reads as the bar.
perspectives.does: Applies against the list as published, and calibrates the ask to a level that was fixed before the posting went up.

perspectives.sees: The published posting, which is the only artefact of this gate that exists outside the company.
perspectives.reads: The posting is the enforceable surface: what it must state is reachable by rule, what stands behind it is not.
perspectives.does: Requires the band in the posting where transparency rules apply, and leaves the approved level and the funding status outside what any disclosure rule reaches.

title: Outbound Sourcing & Talent Pool Contact
content:
# Outbound Sourcing & Talent Pool Contact

Recruiter-initiated outreach to passive candidates and talent-pool building, independent of any inbound application.

### Pass Condition
The candidate responds to outreach and is attached to an active, authorised requisition rather than a speculative pool.
description: Recruiter-initiated outreach to passive candidates and talent-pool building, independent of any inbound application.
pass_condition: The candidate responds to outreach and is attached to an active, authorised requisition rather than a speculative pool.

specimens.label: Outreach, and what it was attached to

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Your platform work looks like a strong match for a role we are opening. Open to a conversation?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Yes. Is there an approved requisition behind it?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Not yet approved — we expect sign-off next quarter and want to be ready.

specimens.reading: This gate passes only when outreach is attached to a real, funded requisition. Attached to a forecast, it is a pipeline entry with no gate behind it.

perspectives.sees: A profile that matches a role, and the role's current state: approved, or expected to be approved. Whether the second becomes the first is not in the recruiter's fields.
perspectives.reads: Contact made before approval is time not spent after it; the time-to-fill clock starts at the opening, not at the first message.
perspectives.does: Sends the outreach and attaches the reply to whichever record exists — an open requisition, or a pool with no gate behind it.

perspectives.sees: An approach that names their work and a role described as opening. The state of the requisition behind it is knowable only by asking.
perspectives.reads: Outreach reads as demand: the search found them, which places them ahead of the queue an application would have joined.
perspectives.does: Answers, and asks whether an approved requisition sits behind it — the question that separates a live process from an entry in a pool.

perspectives.sees: Headcount requests in the approval queue and forecasts for the next cycle. Outreach already sent against an unapproved forecast is a line in neither.
perspectives.reads: A warm pipeline before approval shortens the fill after it, at no cost on any budget line the approval cycle tracks.
perspectives.does: Sets the approval cycle that decides when a forecast becomes a requisition, and does not gate the contact that happens before it.

title: Application Ingestion
content:
# Application Ingestion

The initial ingestion gate where candidate CV and structured application fields enter the talent acquisition database / ATS.

### Pass Condition
The application record is received, validates against the minimum schema, and is linked to an active job requisition.
description: The initial ingestion gate where candidate CV and structured application fields enter the talent acquisition database / ATS.
pass_condition: The application record is received, validates against the minimum schema, and is linked to an active job requisition.

specimens.label: What the gate wrote

lines.text: POST /apply — 200 OK
Candidate record created · linked to req #4471
Required fields validated: 12 of 12
Status: Under review

specimens.reading: Passing this gate means a row exists and is attached to a live requisition. It says nothing about whether anyone will read it.

perspectives.sees: A confirmation that the form was accepted and a status that reads as under review. Nothing about which queue the record entered or who it is assigned to.
perspectives.reads: The application is in the process, and the word review implies a reader.
perspectives.does: Records the date and the wording, and keeps other processes running while the status stays unchanged.

perspectives.sees: A request that validated against the schema and a record linked to a live requisition. The CV arrives here as fields, not as a reading.
perspectives.reads: The transaction succeeded. This is throughput, which is what the buyer of the platform evaluates.
perspectives.does: Creates the record, applies the default status, and starts the expiry clock that ships enabled.
