perspectives.sees: A counter on a requisition rising against a screening capacity that does not rise with it.
perspectives.reads: Passing this gate carries no signal about the candidate. Until triage reaches the record, it is volume.
perspectives.does: Nothing at this gate. The queue is worked at the next one, in an order set there.

title: Automated Filter & Parser Threshold
content:
# Automated Filter & Parser Threshold

Algorithmic text extraction, keyword scoring, compliance screening (location/work authorisation), and knockout question evaluations.

### Pass Condition
The extraction score from CV parsing is at or above the threshold, and the candidate passes every mandatory algorithmic gating rule.
description: Algorithmic text extraction, keyword scoring, compliance screening (location/work authorisation), and knockout question evaluations.
pass_condition: The extraction score from CV parsing is at or above the threshold, and the candidate passes every mandatory algorithmic gating rule.

specimens.label: The scoring pass

lines.text: Parser extraction score: 84/100 — PASS
Work authorization question: answered — PASS
Knockout rule years_experience >= 5: candidate 6 — PASS
Keyword coverage: 7 of 9 required terms — PASS (threshold 6)
Advanced to recruiter queue

specimens.reading: Everything at this gate is a threshold on a number. A person who clears it and a person who misses by one term are separated by arithmetic, not by judgement.

perspectives.sees: A rejection with no reason attached, or a status that does not change. The extraction score, the thresholds and which rule ran are in none of it.
perspectives.reads: An outcome that cannot be told apart from never having been read.
perspectives.does: Rewrites the CV toward the wording of the posting, because the wording is the only visible part of the rule.

perspectives.sees: An extraction score and a set of rule evaluations on each record, against thresholds the customer configured.
perspectives.reads: A pass or a fail on every rule. A low extraction score is a number and does not separate an unreadable file from an unqualified candidate.
perspectives.does: Applies the rules in order and routes the record. A rule that is on by default is applied the same way as one a customer selected.

perspectives.sees: The queue that cleared the thresholds, and the count of what arrived in it.
perspectives.reads: What reaches the queue is the pipeline for this requisition. The records that missed a threshold are not a list anyone is shown.
perspectives.does: Works the queue that arrived. Changing a threshold would require knowing which one removed whom, and that is not in the fields the queue displays.

perspectives.sees: A shortlist, and the requirements as they were written down.
perspectives.reads: The bar is being applied. A requirement written as a minimum is executed as a minimum, on whatever the parser extracted.
perspectives.does: Adjusts the written requirement when the shortlist looks wrong, which is the only point at which the rule becomes visible from here.

title: Inbound Screening & Triage
content:
# Inbound Screening & Triage

Recruiter or sourcing coordinator manual review of parsed inbound applications vs active outbound talent pipelines.

### Pass Condition
The recruiter adds the application to the active short-list for a first conversation.
description: Recruiter or sourcing coordinator manual review of parsed inbound applications vs active outbound talent pipelines.
pass_condition: The recruiter adds the application to the active short-list for a first conversation.

specimens.label: Triage note, as recorded
specimens.context: one of 40 profiles reviewed that day

lines.text: Source: inbound. Queue position 211 of 640.
Skim: backend, payments, right seniority band. No red flags.
Action: short-list for screen. Note — we are also running an outbound list for this req and those go first.

specimens.reading: Inbound and outbound applications compete at this gate, and they do not arrive on equal footing. Position in the queue is part of the outcome.

perspectives.sees: A queue of inbound records, a screening capacity smaller than it, and an outbound list running against the same requisition.
perspectives.reads: Position and source are part of the outcome here. Time-to-fill is measured; time-to-clarity is not.
perspectives.does: Works the outbound list first and skims inbound in queue order. The records below where the day ends stay unreviewed.

perspectives.sees: The same status as on the day of applying, and a gap that lengthens.
perspectives.reads: Nothing here separates a record that has not been reached from one that was read and passed over.
perspectives.does: Sends a follow-up, then treats the process as closed while it remains formally open.

perspectives.sees: Requisition-level figures: applications received, time-to-fill, cost per hire. The queue and the hours held in it are not among them.
perspectives.reads: Volume received reads as reach. The figures show arrivals, not what happened to them.
perspectives.does: Keeps the external posting requirement and sets the recruiting headcount that fixes review capacity, on a cycle measured in quarters.

title: Recruiter Screening Call
content:
# Recruiter Screening Call

Initial conversational interview evaluating salary expectations, timeline, communication, English fluency, and high-level role alignment.

### Pass Condition
The recruiter and the candidate agree on the core parameters, and the recruiter submits the candidate to the hiring team.
description: Initial conversational interview evaluating salary expectations, timeline, communication, English fluency, and high-level role alignment.
pass_condition: The recruiter and the candidate agree on the core parameters, and the recruiter submits the candidate to the hiring team.

specimens.label: What this gate actually asks

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: What are your compensation expectations?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: What is your notice period and earliest start?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Where are you based, and are you authorised to work there?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Give me the two-minute version of your last project.

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Any other processes running that we should know about?

specimens.reading: Four of the five questions are logistics and one is technical. This gate mostly filters on parameters, which is why it can end a process before any engineering is discussed.

perspectives.sees: A thirty-minute call in which four questions are logistics and one is about the work.
perspectives.reads: The compensation question arrives before the level, the rubric or the band is stated, so a number has to be given against an unknown.
perspectives.does: Names a figure or a range, and answers the timeline and location questions that can end the process at this gate.

perspectives.sees: The parameters this gate is scored on: expectations, notice period, location and authorisation, and one account of recent work.
perspectives.reads: A figure outside the approved band ends the process here, whether or not the band is among the fields available at the call.
perspectives.does: Asks the parameter questions first and submits the candidates who align. What may be said about the band at this call is set elsewhere.

perspectives.sees: The band, the levelling grid, and the rule for what may be said about either. Not the call.
perspectives.reads: A conversation held inside the band produces a hire that stays consistent and defensible alongside every other hire.
perspectives.does: Fixes the band and the disclosure rule. Both reach the call as constraints on the recruiter rather than as information the candidate receives.

perspectives.sees: The posting and the text of the disclosure rule. The screening call is not a record that reaches it.
perspectives.reads: Where a band must be published, the question at this gate is asked against a number both sides can name.
perspectives.does: Requires the band in the posting and leaves the level a candidate is assessed at outside the rule, because rules are written where they can be measured and enforced.

title: Technical Screen / Live Assessment
content:
# Technical Screen / Live Assessment

Synchronous technical evaluation assessing core technical competencies, problem-solving speed, and system architecture fundamentals.

### Pass Condition
The candidate's total on the assessing engineer's rubric is at or above the threshold to advance.
description: Synchronous technical evaluation assessing core technical competencies, problem-solving speed, and system architecture fundamentals.
pass_condition: The candidate's total on the assessing engineer's rubric is at or above the threshold to advance.

specimens.label: The rubric the engineer scored against

lines.text: Correctness: 4/5 · Complexity reasoning: 3/5 · Communication: 4/5 · Testing instinct: 3/5
Threshold to advance: 14/20. Total: 14.
Recommendation: advance, weak yes.

specimens.reading: The gate is a sum against a line. A weak yes and a strong no differ by two points in one column, and the candidate never sees the columns.

perspectives.sees: An exercise, a conversation about it, and an outcome. Not the columns, not their weights, not the line the total is compared with.
perspectives.reads: The hour resolves into a single number that is never shown, so a miss by one point and a clear fail arrive in the same wording.
perspectives.does: Reconstructs the session from memory and guesses which part of it cost the points, with nothing in the outcome to check the guess against.

perspectives.sees: Four column scores, a total, and the assessing engineer's recommendation. Not what the same candidate showed in rounds they did not attend.
perspectives.reads: A total on the line is an advance with doubt attached. On the company's own account, a bad hire is visible for a year and carries a name while a missed hire carries none — which is why the threshold holds. On a client account the asymmetry can invert: an unfilled billable seat loses revenue every week, and the same market that runs this five-round loop also makes same-week offers.
perspectives.does: Holds the threshold where it is and passes the doubt into the next round rather than settling it here.

perspectives.sees: The recommendation and, at most, the total. The columns and what was said in the room are not part of what is handed over.
perspectives.reads: The outcome is settled, and the reason for it stays with the panel.
perspectives.does: Writes the message from the recommendation, which is the level of detail available to write from.

title: Take-Home / Work Sample Evaluation
content:
# Take-Home / Work Sample Evaluation

Asynchronous technical assignment or project artifact reviewed by engineering peers against quality benchmarks.

### Pass Condition
The submitted code meets the architecture, functionality, test coverage and documentation requirements.
description: Asynchronous technical assignment or project artifact reviewed by engineering peers against quality benchmarks.
pass_condition: The submitted code meets the architecture, functionality, test coverage and documentation requirements.

specimens.label: Review record

lines.text: Submission received: 41 files, 78 tests, README with design rationale.
Reviewer 1: 9 minutes. Reviewer 2: 4 minutes.
Scored on: architecture, test coverage, documentation, commit hygiene.
Outcome: advance.

specimens.reading: This gate compares hours of work against minutes of review. It can pass or fail on what a reader happened to open.

perspectives.sees: A repository and a scoring form, opened between the team's own delivery work. The hours the submission took are not a field on the form.
perspectives.reads: A score against the rubric reads as the work this candidate would produce on the team.
perspectives.does: Advances or declines on the returned scores. A second read is scheduled where the two reviewers disagree, and not otherwise.

perspectives.sees: A brief, a deadline, and a scope the candidate sets inside it. After submission, a verdict with no reference to any particular file.
perspectives.reads: The hours spent read as the unit this gate measures, and a decline reads as a judgement on the code.
perspectives.does: Builds to the upper bound of the brief, because the brief states a scope and not a review depth. What is left afterwards is the dates and the wording of the verdict.

perspectives.sees: The date the assignment went out, the date it came back, and a line of recommendation. The submission itself is not in the fields the recruiter works from.
perspectives.reads: The gate reads as an interval in the pipeline: days between dispatch and a decision that can be acted on.
perspectives.does: Follows up with the reviewers as the interval grows, and writes the outcome from the recommendation, since the notes behind it do not reach the recruiter.

title: Hiring Manager In-Depth Review
content:
# Hiring Manager In-Depth Review

Detailed evaluation of candidate seniority, project ownership history, trade-off reasoning, and team-specific mission fit.

### Pass Condition
The hiring manager confirms the required depth and approves the candidate for the final panel.
description: Detailed evaluation of candidate seniority, project ownership history, trade-off reasoning, and team-specific mission fit.
pass_condition: The hiring manager confirms the required depth and approves the candidate for the final panel.

specimens.label: The question this gate is built around

lines.speaker: Hiring manager
lines.text: Tell me about a decision on that project you would make differently now.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: We picked synchronous calls between two services because it was faster to ship. It cost us during incidents — a queue would have been the right call.

lines.speaker: Hiring manager
lines.text: What made you choose speed at the time?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: A launch date we had committed to externally.

specimens.reading: This gate is testing ownership and trade-off reasoning, not knowledge. It is also the gate where an undisclosed house preference does the most damage.

perspectives.sees: An hour with the candidate, plus what the earlier rounds recorded. The rounds they did not attend arrive as scores rather than as what was said.
perspectives.reads: An answer about a past trade-off reads as evidence of ownership at the level the role is scoped to.
perspectives.does: Assesses against the requirements as written and the ones that were never written down. A bad hire is attributed and a missed one is not, so an unresolved doubt closes the loop rather than extends it.

perspectives.sees: Questions about past decisions, and no statement of which answers are scored or at what level.
perspectives.reads: A conversational round reads as rapport rather than as an assessment against a written bar.
perspectives.does: Chooses which projects to describe and in what depth, without knowing the house preference the answer is compared against. The available lever is to ask what the level and the rubric are before answering.

perspectives.sees: A recommendation and a date. The reasoning behind it arrives as a summary line, not as the manager's notes.
perspectives.reads: An advance is a pipeline step cleared; a decline here is a rejection to be worded without the reasoning that produced it.
perspectives.does: Moves the candidate to the panel, or sends the decline in standard wording, since the requirement behind it is not in what reached them.

title: Team & Cross-Functional Panel
content:
# Team & Cross-Functional Panel

Multi-interviewer round assessing collaborative problem solving, code review etiquette, cross-functional communication, and cultural norms.

### Pass Condition
Consensus score among team panelists meets or exceeds hire recommendation threshold.
description: Multi-interviewer round assessing collaborative problem solving, code review etiquette, cross-functional communication, and cultural norms.
pass_condition: Consensus score among team panelists meets or exceeds hire recommendation threshold.

specimens.label: Panel tally, as submitted

lines.text: Panelist 1 — collaboration 4, communication 4: hire
Panelist 2 — collaboration 4, communication 3: hire
Panelist 3 — collaboration 3, communication 2: no hire
Consensus threshold: unanimous, or manager override.
Outcome: not aligned.

specimens.reading: The gate is not an average; it is a veto rule. One dissent and a unanimity requirement produce the same result as three dissents.

perspectives.sees: The panel's score sheets and, in the split case, one dissent with a comment. What that panelist saw arrives second-hand.
perspectives.reads: Under a unanimity threshold, one no-hire and three no-hires read the same. The dissent reads as a risk that would be carried alone.
perspectives.does: Overrides or closes. The override carries their signature, and so would the hire it produces.

perspectives.sees: A sequence of separate conversations, each with a person whose weight in the decision is not stated. Then one outcome.
perspectives.reads: The round reads as an average of impressions, and the wording of the decline does not distinguish a split panel from a unanimous one.
perspectives.does: Cannot tell which conversation the decision turned on, so records who was on the panel and what each of them asked — the only part of this gate still available afterwards.

perspectives.sees: The threshold as a configured rule, and the outcome it produced. The individual sheets stay with the team.
perspectives.reads: A unanimity requirement reads as consistency across hires and as a defensible record for each one.
perspectives.does: Keeps the threshold uniform across teams. The hours a re-run of the loop consumes are not a line in the cycle this layer reports on.

title: Compensation & Levelling Reconciliation
content:
# Compensation & Levelling Reconciliation

Internal alignment between candidate expected compensation/level and company pay bands / levelling grid.

### Pass Condition
Candidate expectations fit within approved salary band and equity guidelines for the target grade.
description: Internal alignment between candidate expected compensation/level and company pay bands / levelling grid.
pass_condition: Candidate expectations fit within approved salary band and equity guidelines for the target grade.

specimens.label: Levelling reconciliation sheet

lines.text: Candidate expectation: 90k · Approved band for L4: 68–79k · Approved band for L5: 84–98k
Panel levelled the candidate at L4.
Gap: 11k above the top of the approved band. Options: level up (needs VP approval), reduce expectation, or close.

specimens.reading: Two independent decisions — a level and a band — meet here for the first time. Neither was visible to the candidate while they were being made.

perspectives.sees: A number stated at the screen, and later a message that it does not fit. The level it was compared against is named afterwards, if at all.
perspectives.reads: It reads as a negotiation over the number they named, rather than as the meeting of two decisions taken separately.
perspectives.does: Can restate the number or withdraw. Whether restating it changes anything turns on which of the two produced the gap — the level or the band — and that is not in the message.

perspectives.sees: The level the panel assessed at, and the band that level carries. Their input to this gate closed when the level was set.
perspectives.reads: The gap reads as a levelling question: the same candidate one level up sits inside a band, and moving the level needs a signature above them.
perspectives.does: Requests the level up, or holds the level and lets the process close. The unfilled seat on the team stays with them either way.

perspectives.sees: A request to place a candidate outside an approved band, with the level and the number attached. The rounds behind that number are not in the request.
perspectives.reads: An exception at one level reads against everyone already placed inside that band.
perspectives.does: Approves the exception or holds the grid. The grid is what makes each existing placement defensible, and it is revised on a quarterly cycle rather than per candidate.

perspectives.sees: The posting, and whether the band is in it. What happens between a level and a band inside a company is not filed anywhere.
perspectives.reads: A published band reads as the disclosure the rule required.
perspectives.does: The rule reaches the band and stops. The level a candidate is assessed at is not a disclosable field, so the half of this gate that moves sits outside what the rule reaches.

title: Headcount & Executive Budget Approval
content:
# Headcount & Executive Budget Approval

Formal sign-off by department leadership, finance, and talent committee to commit budget for the written offer.

### Pass Condition
Active headcount requisition is formally certified and unblocked by financial leadership.
description: Formal sign-off by department leadership, finance, and talent committee to commit budget for the written offer.
pass_condition: Active headcount requisition is formally certified and unblocked by financial leadership.

specimens.label: Approval chain

lines.text: Hiring manager: approved
Director: approved
Finance: pending — quarterly review in progress
Talent committee: blocked on finance
Offer cannot be issued while any step is pending.

specimens.reading: Everyone the candidate met has already said yes. This gate is the reason a process can stop after a unanimous panel.

perspectives.sees: A requisition in a quarterly review, alongside every other one. The rounds already run against it are not a field in that review.
perspectives.reads: An approved requisition that can be held costs less than one that cannot, and pending is the state in which the option stays open.
perspectives.does: Issues the certification on the cycle rather than on the loop already running. Nothing in that cycle is timed to a candidate's calendar.

perspectives.sees: A panel that went well, then an interval with no scheduled next step, then either an offer or a note about the role's direction.
perspectives.reads: Silence after a round that went well reads as a verdict on the candidate, since the approval chain has never been shown to them.
perspectives.does: Keeps the other processes running and sets a date past which they stop waiting. That date is the only part of this gate they set.

perspectives.sees: The approval chain with one row pending, and no date on that row.
perspectives.reads: The pipeline is stopped at a step outside their authority, and whether finance clears it this quarter is not among the things that reach them.
perspectives.does: Cannot give a date, and is measured on time-to-fill rather than on time-to-clarity, so the candidate hears again when the row moves.

title: Reference & Background Verification
content:
# Reference & Background Verification

Third-party or internal verification of past employment records, academic degrees, and professional references.

### Pass Condition
All mandatory background checks clear with no unresolved factual discrepancies.
description: Third-party or internal verification of past employment records, academic degrees, and professional references.
pass_condition: All mandatory background checks clear with no unresolved factual discrepancies.

specimens.label: Verification report

lines.text: Employment record 1 of 3: dates confirmed
Employment record 2 of 3: vendor has Mar 2019–Jun 2021, application states Jan 2019–Aug 2021 — DISCREPANCY
Degree: confirmed · References: 2 of 2 returned, both positive
Offer held pending reconciliation.

specimens.reading: The gate checks a third-party record against a claim. A mismatch here is usually a document problem with a named remedy, not a finding about honesty.

perspectives.sees: The list of mandatory checks, which of them cleared, and which line came back unresolved. The report arrives as a status, not as a person.
perspectives.reads: An unresolved line is an open item on a record that has to be defensible: while the file disagrees with itself, the offer cannot complete.
perspectives.does: Holds the offer at the gate until the record reconciles, and sets in advance which checks are mandatory and what evidence closes each one.

perspectives.sees: A vendor report of cleared and uncleared lines, and an offer flagged as held. The records the vendor queried are not in the recruiter's view.
perspectives.reads: A date mismatch is an item to reconcile before the start date, and the time-to-fill clock is already running against it.
perspectives.does: Writes to the candidate naming the mismatch and the document that would close it, and keeps the start date provisional until it does.

perspectives.sees: An offer already accepted and now marked as held, plus whatever part of the finding is passed on: which record disagrees, and by how much.
perspectives.reads: The offer now turns on paperwork the candidate does not hold — a former employer's payroll dates against their own memory of the same months.
perspectives.does: Retrieves whatever documentation covers the disputed months, and postpones resigning or closing other processes while the hold stands.

perspectives.sees: Which categories of check are run, and in which jurisdiction. Nothing about the individual file.
perspectives.reads: Verification is the point where an eligibility rule — a licence, a right to work, a limit on what may be asked — becomes a pass or a fail.
perspectives.does: Bounds what may be checked and what an adverse finding obliges the employer to disclose; how a vendor mismatch is reconciled within those bounds is not set here.

title: Offer Closing & Contract Execution
content:
# Offer Closing & Contract Execution

Final mutual execution of the formal employment agreement and start-date confirmation.

### Pass Condition
Both parties sign offer contract and onboarding workflow is triggered.
description: Final mutual execution of the formal employment agreement and start-date confirmation.
pass_condition: Both parties sign offer contract and onboarding workflow is triggered.

specimens.label: Closing sequence

lines.text: Contract issued for signature
Candidate signed
Countersignature pending
Start date confirmed · onboarding workflow triggered

specimens.reading: A signature from one side is not the gate. Until the countersignature lands the requisition is still open, and an open requisition is what a late freeze can still reach.

perspectives.sees: A requisition still open, a contract issued, and one signature returned. The countersignature is a step in an approval queue alongside the quarter's other commitments.
perspectives.reads: Until the second signature lands, the headcount is a commitment that can still be paused; after it lands, it is a cost that cannot.
perspectives.does: Countersigns and releases the start date, or holds the file while the quarter's funding is reconfirmed.

perspectives.sees: The candidate's signature returned on day one and the countersignature line still empty. Whether the delay is a queue or a funding question is not in the recruiter's fields.
perspectives.reads: The requisition is not closed and the fill is not counted; days of silence here are indistinguishable from a signature waiting its turn.
perspectives.does: Chases the countersignature internally and calls the start date provisional in every message until the contract is executed by both sides.

perspectives.sees: A contract signed and sent back, an unconfirmed start date, and days passing with no countersignature.
perspectives.reads: From here the process reads as finished, though nothing takes effect until the second signature, and that step is not visible from outside.
perspectives.does: Holds off on resigning or closing other processes until the countersigned copy arrives, and records the dates and the wording of what was promised.

title: Client Profile Approval and Client Interview
content:
# Client Profile Approval and Client Interview

The candidate profile is submitted to the end client for review, followed by a client-side interview round.

### Pass Condition
The client approves the profile submission and signs off on the technical and culture match after the interview.
description: The candidate profile is submitted to the end client for review, followed by a client-side interview round.
pass_condition: The client approves the profile submission and signs off on the technical and culture match after the interview.

specimens.label: Client review status

lines.text: Vendor screen & tech assessment: passed
Profile submitted to client for approval
Client interview scheduled

specimens.reading: The candidate remains in an external waiting state where decision authority sits with a party not named on the requisition.

perspectives.sees: A curated batch of candidate profiles forwarded by vendors, evaluated against internal delivery timelines.
perspectives.reads: Profiles are supplier proposals; reviewing them carries no direct employment commitment.
perspectives.does: Selects preferred profiles for a client interview or rejects without detailed feedback.

perspectives.sees: A candidate who passed vendor screening, awaiting feedback from the client account manager.
perspectives.reads: Time-to-feedback is dictated by the client; the vendor cannot advance the candidate unilaterally.
perspectives.does: Follows up with the client contact while keeping the candidate warm with generic holding updates.

perspectives.sees: An extended delay after vendor interviews, followed by an additional external round.
perspectives.reads: The interview process includes an unannounced external decision gate.
perspectives.does: Prepares for a client interview whose evaluation criteria and contractual context are opaque.

perspectives.sees: Commercial margin targets dependent on placing candidate billable hours on the client contract.
perspectives.reads: Candidate placement directly realizes project revenue once client sign-off is secured.
perspectives.does: Monitors client approval rates and manages bench fallback options.

title: Probation Period & Post-Start Confirmation
content:
# Probation Period & Post-Start Confirmation

The post-hire evaluation interval (statutory or contractual probation) during which performance, delivery, and team alignment are formally confirmed.

### Pass Condition
The candidate completes the probationary period without termination notice and transitions into confirmed permanent employment.
description: The post-hire evaluation interval (statutory or contractual probation) during which performance, delivery, and team alignment are formally confirmed.
pass_condition: The candidate completes the probationary period without termination notice and transitions into confirmed permanent employment.

specimens.label: Probation review milestone

lines.text: Day 1–60: Objectives assigned, delivery metrics tracked
Day 90: Formal probation sign-off review by engineering manager
Status: Full permanent standing confirmed

specimens.reading: The transition from conditional probation to permanent standing requires explicit managerial evaluation or statutory lapse.

perspectives.sees: Direct on-the-job execution during the first three months, assessing delivery speed, architecture decisions, and team communication.
perspectives.reads: Probation provides a low-friction termination window if the hire demonstrates unexpected capability gaps.
perspectives.does: Conducts regular 1-on-1 reviews and files the final probation confirmation report.

perspectives.sees: Initial project onboarding, ramp-up expectations, and milestone checkpoints toward passing probation.
perspectives.reads: Employment remains contingent on early performance until the probation gate is officially cleared.
perspectives.does: Delivers against sprint goals and seeks written confirmation upon completion of the probation interval.

perspectives.sees: Legal compliance boundaries (statutory 3-month caps under the Ukrainian Labour Code, or contractual notice rules under the UK Employment Rights Act 1996).
perspectives.reads: Probation defines the boundary where statutory employment protections and standard dismissal standards take full effect.
perspectives.does: Enforces notice requirements and confirms payroll status transition upon probation completion.

title: ATS Parser Extraction Failure
content:
# ATS Parser Extraction Failure

Multi-column formatting, graphics, custom fonts, or unsupported document layouts cause ATS parser to corrupt or omit critical work history.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `system`
- **Nature:** `noise`
- **Removability:** `candidate`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `mech.automated_keyword_qualification_filter` — Automated Keyword / Qualification Filter

### Non-Inferences
- Does not imply human recruiter evaluated and disliked candidate experience.
summary: Multi-column formatting, graphics, custom fonts, or unsupported document layouts cause ATS parser to corrupt or omit critical work history.

specimens.label: Parsed profile, as the ATS stored it
specimens.context: the same CV that renders correctly in a PDF reader

lines.text: Name: parsed · Email: parsed · Phone: parsed
Work experience: 0 entries
Skills: 0 entries
Raw text captured: 340 characters of a 4,100-character document
Ranking score: 12/100 — insufficient experience

specimens.reading: The document was not read and rejected; it was not read. A two-column layout and a graphic header are enough to produce this.

perspectives.sees: A document that opens correctly in a reader, and either a rejection soon after submission or no reply at all.
perspectives.reads: The stored profile is not shown back, so this is inferable from the timing and from nothing else.
perspectives.does: Resubmits in a single-column form with a text layer, wherever a second application is accepted. This is the branch the candidate can act on without anyone's cooperation.

perspectives.sees: A queue ordered by score, longer than the number of screens that fit in the week.
perspectives.reads: A profile below the line reads as a profile that did not qualify. The document behind the score is not opened to check which it is.
perspectives.does: Works down the ranked list from the top. The list carries no marker separating unread from unqualified, so the positions below the line stay closed.

non_inferences: Does not imply human recruiter evaluated and disliked candidate experience.

title: Automated Application Expiration Timeout
content:
# Automated Application Expiration Timeout

The ATS is configured to reject in bulk every application still pending after 45 or 60 days.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `system`
- **Nature:** `rule`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Masks `mech.stale_or_orphaned_job_requisition` — Stale or Orphaned Job Requisition

### Non-Inferences
- A bulk timeout rejection carries no assessment of the profile at all.
summary: The ATS is configured to reject in bulk every application still pending after 45 or 60 days.

specimens.label: Bulk expiry, as logged

lines.text: Scheduled job: expire_stale_applications
Selecting applications with status=submitted and age>60d — 312 matched
Human review recorded on 0 of 312
Status set to Rejected — 312 notification emails queued

specimens.reading: The rejection email is real and the review it implies never happened. Timing is the tell: everyone in the batch is notified in the same minute.

perspectives.sees: A scheduled job, the records matching status and age, and a count of notifications queued. Review activity is a stored field, and the threshold does not consult it.
perspectives.reads: Records past the threshold are stale queue state. Nothing in the schema separates an application nobody opened from one that was assessed and declined.
perspectives.does: Runs the job at the customer's configured threshold and sends the configured template. The setting ships enabled, and switching it off is a customer action.

perspectives.sees: The queue depth on the requisition drops overnight, and applications the recruiter never opened now carry the status Rejected.
perspectives.reads: The backlog cleared at the threshold rather than through screening. The binding constraint was never a decision, but how many applications fit into the week.
perspectives.does: Works the current inbound, which is what time-to-fill is measured against. The expired batch is not itemised anywhere the recruiter is asked to account for it.

perspectives.sees: A rejection weeks after applying, in the same wording used for a rejection after an interview.
perspectives.reads: A decision about the application. Nothing in the message separates a person's decision from a scheduled status change, and nothing says whether the role was live.
perspectives.does: Records the date and stops following up. Whether to apply to this employer again is decided on a message that carries no reason.

perspectives.sees: The class of practice rather than the batch: an application status changed by rule, in jurisdictions where automated decision-making carries disclosure or explanation duties.
perspectives.reads: A scheduled expiry is a decision only where the framing counts it as one. Where the rule lives on a configuration screen with a default, no filing records that a decision was made.
perspectives.does: The available lever is a rule written for a class of systems — disclosure, explainability, a right to human review — and it arrives on a cycle longer than the threshold it would govern.

non_inferences: A bulk timeout rejection carries no assessment of the profile at all.

title: Automated Keyword / Qualification Filter
content:
# Automated Keyword / Qualification Filter

Deterministic filter rejecting applications missing exact acronyms, certifications, or specific years-of-experience thresholds.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `system`
- **Nature:** `rule`
- **Removability:** `candidate`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `mech.employment_gap_downranking_bias` — Employment Gap Downranking Bias
- Amplifies `mech.mid_process_role_requirement_redefinition` — Mid-Process Role Requirement Redefinition

### Non-Inferences
- Passing keyword filters does not guarantee interview invitation.
summary: Deterministic filter rejecting applications missing exact acronyms, certifications, or specific years-of-experience thresholds.

specimens.label: Screening rules, as they ran

lines.text: Rule 1: must_contain("Kubernetes") — PASS
Rule 2: must_contain("CKA") — candidate holds CKAD — FAIL
Rule 3: not evaluated (short-circuit)
Status: Rejected — does not meet minimum criteria

specimens.reading: An adjacent certification is not a near miss to a string match; it is a miss. The filter compares tokens, not competence.

perspectives.sees: The rule as the customer configured it and the string it tests for, evaluated against the parsed fields of one application. Whether an adjacent qualification sits in those fields is not something a string comparison can represent.
perspectives.reads: The rule ran to specification: the token is present or it is absent. A failed knockout is a determinate result, not a low score.
perspectives.does: Writes the rejection status in the same session and emits the notification the customer configured. The rule stays on until a customer turns it off.

perspectives.sees: The shortlist that reaches the review, and the requirements as they were written into the posting. What that wording removed before the shortlist is not in the view.
perspectives.reads: A thin pipeline reads as scarcity of the skill in the market rather than as the reach of the requirement as it was written.
perspectives.does: Holds the bar and asks for more sourcing, or rewrites the requirements once the search runs long.

perspectives.sees: A rejection that arrives minutes after submission, in template wording that names no field.
perspectives.reads: The interval is the only evidence about how the application was read, and the message does not distinguish a rule from a person.
perspectives.does: Records the interval between submission and reply, and carries the exact strings the posting names into the next application.

non_inferences: Passing keyword filters does not guarantee interview invitation.

title: Bench-Priority Fill
content:
# Bench-Priority Fill

An engineer already employed and between projects becomes available mid-search, and the seat the external candidate is interviewing for is filled from the bench.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `policy`
- **Nature:** `incentive`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Non-Inferences
- Does not establish that the internal candidate was earmarked before the search was published — that is mech.pre_selected_internal_candidate, and from the outside the two are the same.
- Does not mean the external assessment found the candidate short: the search can end for reasons that never reached the assessment.
summary: An engineer already employed and between projects becomes available mid-search, and the seat the external candidate is interviewing for is filled from the bench.

specimens.label: Requisition timeline

lines.text: Requisition opened — client seat, external search approved
External candidate at panel stage
Internal availability: engineer rolling off project end of month
Requisition closed — filled internally

specimens.reading: Nothing in the record was decided against the external candidate. A person the company already pays became free, and an employed engineer on the bench costs the margin every idle week. The search ended because its reason did.

perspectives.sees: A process that was moving, then a closure — sometimes naming an internal hire, sometimes just the search ending.
perspectives.reads: Indistinguishable from a role that was promised internally before it was posted. The difference — whether the internal person was available when the search began or became available during it — sits in a staffing record no message describes.
perspectives.does: Notes the interval between the last positive signal and the closure; a short one is the only outside trace of an availability that changed mid-search.

perspectives.sees: A bench that costs salary against no billing, and an open seat that fits someone on it.
perspectives.reads: Filling the seat from the bench converts an idle cost into billed work in one move; continuing an external search past that point pays twice for the same seat.
perspectives.does: Fills from the bench as soon as the dates line up, and closes the external search that the bench has made redundant.

perspectives.sees: A seat filled on schedule with a profile the vendor vouches for, often faster than an external start date could have landed.
perspectives.reads: Whether the person came from a search or from the bench is invisible in the deliverable, and the contract does not ask.
perspectives.does: Accepts the staffing, unaware an external process ended somewhere so that this one could close on time.

non_inferences: Does not establish that the internal candidate was earmarked before the search was published — that is mech.pre_selected_internal_candidate, and from the outside the two are the same.
Does not mean the external assessment found the candidate short: the search can end for reasons that never reached the assessment.

title: Bid-Conditional Talent Pool
content:
# Bid-Conditional Talent Pool

Recruiters run a real search for a real role whose funding depends on a contract that is not yet signed; if the bid is lost, the pool is closed without the role ever having existed.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `recruiter`
- **Nature:** `incentive`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Non-Inferences
- Does not mean the role was fake: it was real and conditional, which is a different structure from a posting nobody intends to fill.
- Does not establish that the recruiter was free to disclose the bid's existence.
summary: Recruiters run a real search for a real role whose funding depends on a contract that is not yet signed; if the bid is lost, the pool is closed without the role ever having existed.

specimens.label: Outreach against a bid

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: We are growing the team on a large fintech engagement and your profile is a strong match. Could we talk this week?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Happy to. Is this for an open role I can read somewhere?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: The details are under wraps for now — I can share more on the call.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Following up on our call — is there any update?

specimens.reading: Everything said is true. The engagement is real, the match may be real, and the role does not exist yet: it exists if a contract signs. The one fact that would let the candidate price the wait is the one fact the conversation is structured not to state.

perspectives.sees: A concrete-sounding approach about a role that cannot be found posted anywhere, then a call that goes well, then a silence with no stated end.
perspectives.reads: Nothing distinguishes this from an approach against a funded seat. The difference is a record — a signed contract — that no message references and no search of the postings can reveal.
perspectives.does: Asks what the conversation is attached to: an approved requisition, or a pipeline for something expected. The answer, or its absence, is the only observable this structure leaks.

perspectives.sees: A staffing plan owed against a proposal, with named profiles required in it, and a deadline set by the client's procurement, not by any funnel.
perspectives.reads: The bid cannot be won without the CVs, and the people behind the CVs cannot be promised anything until it is won. Both halves are true at once, and the brief usually forbids stating the second.
perspectives.does: Builds the pool the proposal needs, keeps the conversations warm for as long as the decision takes, and closes them without a verdict when the decision goes the other way — because there is no verdict to send about a role that never came to exist.

perspectives.sees: A vendor's proposal with named, available profiles in it — evidence the vendor can actually staff what it is bidding to deliver.
perspectives.reads: The profiles are part of the bid's credibility. Whether the people behind them know what stage the engagement is at is the vendor's affair, and nothing in procurement asks.
perspectives.does: Evaluates the bid on rate, profiles and risk, on procurement's calendar — unaware that the calendar is experienced, somewhere, as an unexplained silence.

non_inferences: Does not mean the role was fake: it was real and conditional, which is a different structure from a posting nobody intends to fill.
Does not establish that the recruiter was free to disclose the bid's existence.

title: Communication or Working Style Friction
content:
# Communication or Working Style Friction

During a collaborative interview exercise the candidate is abrasive in tone, defensive about critique, or not listening.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `candidate`
- **Nature:** `bias`
- **Removability:** `candidate`

### Non-Inferences
- Style friction in a high-pressure interview is not a permanent personality defect.
summary: During a collaborative interview exercise the candidate is abrasive in tone, defensive about critique, or not listening.

specimens.label: The exchange the note refers to

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: I think this loop is doing more work than it needs to.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: It is fine. The input is bounded.

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: Sure, but if it were not?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Then I would change it. But it is.

specimens.reading: The panel recorded this as resistance to critique. A short answer under time pressure and a defensive posture look identical in a transcript — which is why this belongs in the honest-baseline set and not in the excuses.

perspectives.sees: The exchange as it happened under time pressure, and a rejection that names fit or collaboration without pointing at a moment.
perspectives.reads: A short answer given while still working on the problem, and a note about it that cannot be read back. There is nothing to check the reading against.
perspectives.does: Reconstructs the session from memory and changes how disagreement is phrased in the next one.

perspectives.sees: The panel's written impressions of how a disagreement went, alongside the technical scores. No recording, and each interviewer saw a different half hour.
perspectives.reads: A signal about how the person takes review in a team that has to work with them daily. A bad hire on this axis is visible for a year and has a name on it.
perspectives.does: Weighs the impression against the technical notes, and where the panel is split resolves it toward the more conservative outcome.

perspectives.sees: A panel recommendation with the reason recorded as style or fit, and no transcript behind it.
perspectives.reads: A decision that is final and hard to put in writing to the candidate without it reading as a judgement about the person.
perspectives.does: Sends the standard closer-alignment wording, or relays the specific note if the panel has phrased it as something the candidate can act on.

non_inferences: Style friction in a high-pressure interview is not a permanent personality defect.

title: Domain Specificity Over-Weighting
content:
# Domain Specificity Over-Weighting

The interviewer holds experience in one exact vertical — adtech, crypto, a named payment processor — as a requirement, ahead of transferable systems depth.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `hiring-manager`
- **Nature:** `bias`
- **Removability:** `intermediary`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `mech.hidden_evaluation_rubric_or_undisclosed_priority` — Hidden Evaluation Rubric or Undisclosed Priority
- Masks `mech.genuine_technical_skill_shortfall` — Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall

### Non-Inferences
- Transferable general engineering skills are not disproven by lack of specific proprietary protocol knowledge.
summary: The interviewer holds experience in one exact vertical — adtech, crypto, a named payment processor — as a requirement, ahead of transferable systems depth.

specimens.label: Where the round turned

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: You have built settlement systems, but not in cards specifically?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Not cards. Same problem shape though — idempotency, reconciliation, chargeback-equivalent reversals.

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: We really need someone who has lived in card rails. The scheme rules are their own world.

specimens.reading: Transferable depth was heard and set aside for vertical familiarity. That is a legitimate preference and a narrow one; the rejection is about the filter, not the engineering.

perspectives.sees: A gap in the team's coverage of a specific set of rules or protocols, and a candidate whose depth is in an adjacent shape of the same problem.
perspectives.reads: Transferable depth plus a ramp-up the team pays for while it is already short-handed. A miss on the vertical is visible after the hire and has a name on it.
perspectives.does: Holds the vertical as a requirement rather than a preference, and the round turns on it whatever the rest of the panel recorded.

perspectives.sees: A technical conversation that goes well until a question about a specific vertical, then a rejection worded as closer alignment.
perspectives.reads: The engineering was heard and the vertical decided it, or the engineering was the reason and the vertical is the wording. The email carries both.
perspectives.does: Records where in the round the turn happened, and reads the next posting's domain nouns as requirements rather than as context.

perspectives.sees: A brief with a vertical named in it, and panels returning notes that cite the vertical rather than the technical rubric.
perspectives.reads: A requirement that narrows the pool while time-to-fill keeps counting, and one the hiring manager holds rather than the recruiter.
perspectives.does: Screens on the vertical, because a shortlist without it comes back from the hiring manager, and sends the standard wording to the rest.

perspectives.sees: A requirement entered as a domain term, and a ranking model for which that term is a feature like any other.
perspectives.reads: A configured preference, scored as specified. The platform has nothing that represents an adjacent domain solving the same problem.
perspectives.does: Ranks and filters on the term as entered, and profiles whose depth is described in other nouns fall below the review threshold.

non_inferences: Transferable general engineering skills are not disproven by lack of specific proprietary protocol knowledge.

title: Employment Gap Downranking Bias
content:
# Employment Gap Downranking Bias

Automated ranking algorithms or human screeners discount candidates with recent career breaks regardless of verified project history.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `system`
- **Nature:** `bias`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `mech.automated_keyword_qualification_filter` — Automated Keyword / Qualification Filter

### Non-Inferences
- An employment gap does not correlate with a decline in technical ability.
summary: Automated ranking algorithms or human screeners discount candidates with recent career breaks regardless of verified project history.

specimens.label: Ranking breakdown, as scored

lines.text: Skills match: 91/100
Domain match: 88/100
Continuity penalty: −22 (gap of 14 months detected)
Final rank: 57/100 — below advance threshold

specimens.reading: The penalty is applied to a date range, not to anything in the work. Nothing the candidate shipped during or after the gap is in the arithmetic.

perspectives.sees: The date ranges the parser extracts from the history, and the continuity feature that reads them. Work done inside a gap is not among the fields that feature reads.
perspectives.reads: The penalty is a weight in the arithmetic that produces one number. A rank below the advance threshold reads the same whether it came from the match or from the deduction.
perspectives.does: Returns the rank and places the profile below the threshold. The setting ships enabled and stays on until a customer changes it.

perspectives.sees: The list in the order the platform returns it. The arithmetic that produced the order is not displayed alongside it.
perspectives.reads: The order is where the reading starts, and capacity ends it partway down. A profile below that point leaves no record that it was skipped.
perspectives.does: Screens from the top of the order until the week's capacity is spent. What sits below that point is not read, and is not rejected either.

perspectives.sees: Their own history with the interval in it, and afterwards either silence or template wording.
perspectives.reads: The interval and the outcome coincide, and nothing in the message separates a deduction on a date range from a judgement of the work.
perspectives.does: Puts the interval and the work done inside it into the history itself. The date range is a fact of record, and it is what the ranking reads.

non_inferences: An employment gap does not correlate with a decline in technical ability.

title: Experience-Age Grading Mismatch
content:
# Experience-Age Grading Mismatch

A candidate with 10+ years applies for a role graded at mid or senior, and the screening note records forecasts about boredom, short tenure and salary expectation.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `recruiter`
- **Nature:** `bias`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `mech.unstated_compensation_band_discrepancy` — Unstated Compensation Band Discrepancy
- Masks `mech.genuine_technical_skill_shortfall` — Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall

### Non-Inferences
- Being rejected as "overqualified" is an organisational tier mismatch, not a candidate deficiency.
summary: A candidate with 10+ years applies for a role graded at mid or senior, and the screening note records forecasts about boredom, short tenure and salary expectation.

specimens.label: Screening note, internal

lines.text: 12 years experience against a role scoped at 4–6.
Concern: likely to be bored within two quarters; salary expectation probably above band; risk of using us as a bridge.
Recommend: pass, unless the manager wants to see them for the level above.

specimens.reading: Every line is a forecast about the future, none is an observation about the work. This is why the rejection can arrive before any technical signal exists.

perspectives.sees: A CV with years and scope above the level the requisition is graded and funded at, and a screening queue larger than the week's capacity.
perspectives.reads: A forecast about retention and salary expectation, formed before any technical signal exists. The band is fixed and the level is not the recruiter's to change.
perspectives.does: Passes at screening, or asks the hiring manager whether they want the profile at the level above — which is a different requisition.

perspectives.sees: A rejection naming seniority or overqualification, arriving before any technical stage, for a role whose posted band was acceptable.
perspectives.reads: A decision about a future they were not asked about. Nothing in it separates a levelling grid from a judgement about the work.
perspectives.does: Records the stage the rejection arrived at, and names a salary expectation at the screen of the next process rather than after it.

perspectives.sees: A levelling grid mapping years and scope to a band, and requisitions approved at one level at a time.
perspectives.reads: Consistency across every hire, which is what the grid exists for. The applications the grid excludes do not reach this layer.
perspectives.does: Holds the grid and the band, and any exception moves through the levelling committee on its own cycle rather than through the process in progress.

non_inferences: Being rejected as "overqualified" is an organisational tier mismatch, not a candidate deficiency.

title: Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall
content:
# Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall

The candidate’s verified technical execution or domain depth does not meet the established baseline for the role level.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `candidate`
- **Nature:** `rule`
- **Removability:** `candidate`

### Non-Inferences
- Rejection does not mean the candidate has no engineering ability, only that the requirement bar was unmet for this specific benchmark.
summary: The candidate’s verified technical execution or domain depth does not meet the established baseline for the role level.

specimens.label: Feedback naming the gap
specimens.subject: Feedback — technical round

lines.text: The panel was positive on communication and on how you structured the problem.
The gap was concrete: the concurrency exercise needed a bounded worker pool and the submitted solution spawned unbounded goroutines, which the panel would expect to be caught at this level.
We would genuinely welcome a re-application once that area has had some time.

specimens.reading: A named exercise and a named property. This is the shape of feedback that is about the work rather than about fit — rare, and worth keeping.

perspectives.sees: The panel's written notes against the bar set for this level, and the exercise the notes refer to.
perspectives.reads: A gap at this level is something the team carries while it closes. A bad hire is visible for a year and has a name on it; a missed one has neither.
perspectives.does: Declines at the level assessed. The panel's specifics stay inside the loop unless they are passed on in a form the recruiter can quote.

perspectives.sees: The panel's recommendation and whatever note comes with it, not the scores behind it.
perspectives.reads: A decline that has to be worded before the next screen. Whether the reason can be repeated to the candidate depends on the form in which it arrives.
perspectives.does: Writes the rejection. Time-to-fill is measured and time-to-clarity is not, so a specific reason reaches the message where a quotable note already exists.

perspectives.sees: Either a message naming the exercise and the property that was missed, or a template that names neither.
perspectives.reads: A named gap can be checked against the work. A template leaves the bar, the level and the rest of the cohort all unstated.
perspectives.does: Records the wording and the date, and can work on the named area. That is the one branch of this the candidate controls.

non_inferences: Rejection does not mean the candidate has no engineering ability, only that the requirement bar was unmet for this specific benchmark.

title: Headcount Freeze or Budget Cancellation
content:
# Headcount Freeze or Budget Cancellation

Executive leadership or finance halts all new hires across division due to macroeconomic factors or revenue shifts mid-interview process.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `policy`
- **Nature:** `rule`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `mech.stale_or_orphaned_job_requisition` — Stale or Orphaned Job Requisition
- Masks `mech.genuine_technical_skill_shortfall` — Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall
- Masks `mech.stronger_competing_candidate_in_final_cohort` — Stronger Competing Candidate in Final Cohort

### Non-Inferences
- Candidate performance in interview was not the causal trigger for process termination.
summary: Executive leadership or finance halts all new hires across division due to macroeconomic factors or revenue shifts mid-interview process.

specimens.label: The freeze, as announced downward

lines.text: I have to pause our process. A hiring freeze was announced across the division this morning, effective immediately.
Your final round was scheduled for Thursday. I am cancelling it rather than having you prepare for something I cannot honour.
I will tell you plainly when I know anything, including if the answer is that this will not reopen.

specimens.reading: The cause is above the hiring loop and dated. Whether it is checkable against public news is the probe worth running.

perspectives.sees: The register of open requisitions and the forecast the quarter is planned against. Which of those requisitions has a person standing in a final round is not a field in that view.
perspectives.reads: An approved requisition is an option that can be paused, and pausing costs less than carrying it. The decision is taken at the level of the division, not of a process.
perspectives.does: Suspends funding across the division from a stated date and passes the instruction downward. The processes already running are closed by the people holding them.

perspectives.sees: A date on which the requisition changes state in the system, and the instruction that arrives with it. The forecast behind it is not something the recruiter is shown.
perspectives.reads: The pipeline is intact and has nowhere to arrive. Time-to-fill on this requisition stops being a number anyone can move.
perspectives.does: Cancels the scheduled rounds and writes the message. The wording is the recruiter's; what may be disclosed is not.

perspectives.sees: The requisition is no longer funded, and the work it was opened to absorb stays with the team. The panel's recommendation now decides nothing.
perspectives.reads: The search has ended for a reason that is not in the loop and not in the candidates. The gap remains, and the date it reopens is not the manager's to set.
perspectives.does: Stops convening panels and redistributes the work across the team. Anyone already in the loop is handed to the recruiter to close.

perspectives.sees: A final round cancelled, or an offer that does not arrive, on a date, with whatever reason the message states.
perspectives.reads: The timing sits directly after the rounds already completed, so a cause above the process and a verdict on the process look the same from here.
perspectives.does: Records the date and the wording, asks whether the requisition is paused or closed, and keeps the other processes running.

non_inferences: Candidate performance in interview was not the causal trigger for process termination.

title: Hidden Evaluation Rubric or Undisclosed Priority
content:
# Hidden Evaluation Rubric or Undisclosed Priority

The panel grades the candidate against architectural preferences, internal frameworks and house conventions that were not stated in the posting or in the round.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `hiring-manager`
- **Nature:** `bias`
- **Removability:** `intermediary`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `mech.hiring_manager_consensus_impasse` — Hiring Manager Consensus Impasse
- Masks `mech.genuine_technical_skill_shortfall` — Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall

### Non-Inferences
- Not guessing an unstated preference is not a shortfall in core competence.
summary: The panel grades the candidate against architectural preferences, internal frameworks and house conventions that were not stated in the posting or in the round.

specimens.label: The rubric that was not in the brief

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: I would put a queue between them so the write path stays available if the consumer is down.

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: Mm. We do not use queues here.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Is that a constraint I should design within?

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: Just carry on.

specimens.reading: A house preference was applied as a grading criterion without being stated as one. The candidate could not have designed to a rule they were not given.

perspectives.sees: The panel's write-ups, in the vocabulary the team uses for its own systems. What the candidate was sent before the round is not in front of the panel.
perspectives.reads: A design that departs from the pattern the team runs on reads as a shortfall in depth, not as a mismatch with a preference. A criterion the team shares is not experienced as a criterion; it is the standard.
perspectives.does: Records the objection in the panel's own terms and sets the level from it. The brief for the next candidate is unchanged.

perspectives.sees: The questions as they were asked and the reaction in the room, and afterwards a reason stated in general terms.
perspectives.reads: The feedback names a shortfall that cannot be checked against the criterion applied, because that criterion was not stated in the round.
perspectives.does: Records the exchange and asks in the round whether a stated preference is a constraint to design within. There is no revision available against a rule that was not given.

non_inferences: Not guessing an unstated preference is not a shortfall in core competence.

title: Hiring Manager Consensus Impasse
content:
# Hiring Manager Consensus Impasse

The panel splits evenly, no one holds a tiebreaking vote, and the rule for the absence of consensus is no hire.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `hiring-manager`
- **Nature:** `bias`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Masks `mech.stronger_competing_candidate_in_final_cohort` — Stronger Competing Candidate in Final Cohort

### Non-Inferences
- A split panel reflects the absence of a calibrated internal bar, not a failure by the candidate.
summary: The panel splits evenly, no one holds a tiebreaking vote, and the rule for the absence of consensus is no hire.

specimens.label: Debrief tally

lines.text: Interviewer A: hire. Interviewer B: hire. Interviewer C: no hire. Interviewer D: no hire.
No tiebreaker present. Policy: absent consensus, default to no hire.
Outcome recorded as: not aligned with team needs.

specimens.reading: A 2–2 split became a rejection by rule, and the rule was then written up as a judgement about the candidate.

perspectives.sees: A debrief that does not resolve: two for, two against, with no calibration record that would weigh one interviewer's bar against another's.
perspectives.reads: Absent a reason to override, the split is the answer. A bad hire is visible for a year and has a name on it; a candidate not hired leaves nothing to be asked about.
perspectives.does: Applies the default and records the outcome in the fit wording the debrief form accepts, which is what the rest of the process then sees.

perspectives.sees: A debrief that closes without a recommendation, and an outcome field set to no hire with no single reason attached to it.
perspectives.reads: The requisition is open again and the pipeline restarts. What the panel actually scored is not visible from here.
perspectives.does: Sends the standard rejection, since there is no agreed reason to convey, and reopens sourcing against a bar written down no more clearly than before.

perspectives.sees: Feedback from one round naming architectural depth as a strength, another naming technical background as a gap, then a rejection citing fit.
perspectives.reads: Two assessments of the same performance that cannot both hold. From here they read as an assessment of the candidate rather than of a room that did not agree.
perspectives.does: Sets out to close a gap that half the panel did not record, and keeps both statements with their dates.

non_inferences: A split panel reflects the absence of a calibrated internal bar, not a failure by the candidate.

title: Inflated Requisition Requirements vs Actual Team Needs
content:
# Inflated Requisition Requirements vs Actual Team Needs

The posting lists 10+ named technologies and a Staff-level bar for a role whose actual work is feature delivery.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `hiring-manager`
- **Nature:** `incentive`
- **Removability:** `intermediary`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `mech.automated_keyword_qualification_filter` — Automated Keyword / Qualification Filter
- Amplifies `mech.unstated_compensation_band_discrepancy` — Unstated Compensation Band Discrepancy

### Non-Inferences
- Failing to meet an inflated "wishlist" does not establish anything about how the candidate would do the team's actual work.
summary: The posting lists 10+ named technologies and a Staff-level bar for a role whose actual work is feature delivery.

specimens.label: The posting against the first month of work

lines.text: Posting: 10+ years distributed systems, Kubernetes, Kafka, Rust, Go, Terraform, GraphQL, ML serving, on-call leadership, mentoring.
Same team, standup notes from the quarter: CRUD endpoints for the billing dashboard, a report export, two library upgrades.
Both descriptions are of the same role.

specimens.reading: The requirement list is a wish, an anchor and a filter at once. It describes the ceiling somebody imagined, not the work in the sprint.

perspectives.sees: An approval form with one requirement list to cover the whole of what the role might have to absorb, and a level that has to be justified against the grid.
perspectives.reads: The list is the only written statement of the ceiling. A requirement left off cannot be screened for later without going back through approval.
perspectives.does: Writes the superset — the whole stack, the seniority the level needs — and calibrates afterwards against real candidates, in the screen and on the panel.

perspectives.sees: The requirement list as written, and a pipeline that thins under it. What the manager requires but has not written down is not visible from here.
perspectives.reads: Until the manager says otherwise, the list is the screening standard, and the pool that clears it is small.
perspectives.does: Screens against the written list, then goes back to the manager to find which items are movable — while time-to-fill runs from the day the requisition opened.

perspectives.sees: The requirement list as configurable criteria: years, titles, named technologies, each one a feature the ranking model can read or a knockout rule the customer can switch on.
perspectives.reads: Every listed item is a requirement. Nothing in the record separates what the role needs from what someone hoped for.
perspectives.does: Applies the criteria as configured and ranks accordingly. A longer list yields a smaller qualified pool, and the pool size is what the customer sees.

perspectives.sees: A posting listing a stack of named technologies and a seniority level, and later the same role posted again.
perspectives.reads: The list is the bar. Which items are load-bearing is stated nowhere the candidate can reach, and neither is the level they would be assessed at.
perspectives.does: Either does not apply to a role whose actual work is within reach, or applies and spends the hours; when the role reappears, there is nothing available to tell an unmet bar from a list nobody clears.

non_inferences: Failing to meet an inflated "wishlist" does not establish anything about how the candidate would do the team's actual work.

title: Interview Resource & Scheduling Saturation
content:
# Interview Resource & Scheduling Saturation

Engineering interviewers carry sprint commitments alongside the panels they sit on, and rounds are moved, read cold, or dropped.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `hiring-manager`
- **Nature:** `noise`
- **Removability:** `intermediary`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `mech.take_home_evaluation_fatigue_asymmetry` — Take-Home Evaluation Fatigue & Asymmetry

### Non-Inferences
- Rescheduling is an operational fact and does not indicate a negative evaluation.
summary: Engineering interviewers carry sprint commitments alongside the panels they sit on, and rounds are moved, read cold, or dropped.

specimens.label: Inside the interviewer calendar

lines.speaker: Engineering manager
lines.text: Can you take the panel Thursday? Nobody else on the team is free.

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: I am on release duty and I have not read the take-home. I can do it but it will be a cold read.

lines.speaker: Engineering manager
lines.text: Take it. We are already two weeks over on this req.

specimens.reading: The evaluation was compromised before it began, and nothing in the candidate could have changed that. This trace lives on the other side of the table.

perspectives.sees: The same engineers' calendars carrying the sprint and the panel, and a requisition running past its target date. What the loop costs the people covering the open work is not in that view.
perspectives.reads: An interviewer who is free is the option that keeps the loop moving; the alternative is another week on the requisition. A cold read is still a round completed.
perspectives.does: Puts whoever has the slot on the panel and takes the write-up that comes back.

perspectives.sees: Rounds moved, gaps between them, and an interviewer opening the submitted work during the call.
perspectives.reads: The changes are visible only through their own calendar, where a scheduling constraint and a decline in interest look alike.
perspectives.does: Records each date and each change, asks what remains in the loop and by when, and keeps other processes live.

perspectives.sees: Panel slots that come back unfilled and dates that shift; the interviewers' other commitments sit on the calendars the recruiter is scheduling around.
perspectives.reads: A move is an operational fact with a date, and time-to-fill is measured on the total. There is nothing in it to report about the candidate's standing.
perspectives.does: Reissues the invitation with the new date and decides whether the candidate is told the loop has stalled.

non_inferences: Rescheduling is an operational fact and does not indicate a negative evaluation.

title: Location or Timezone Compliance Constraint
content:
# Location or Timezone Compliance Constraint

The company has no legal entity or provider that can issue an employment contract in the jurisdiction where the candidate resides.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `policy`
- **Nature:** `rule`
- **Removability:** `intermediary`

### Non-Inferences
- The jurisdictional barrier is entirely independent of the candidate's technical competence.
summary: The company has no legal entity or provider that can issue an employment contract in the jurisdiction where the candidate resides.

specimens.label: Where the constraint actually sits

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Everything is agreed on our side. One question — you are resident where exactly?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Same country as in my application, no change.

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Then I have bad news. We have no legal entity there and our provider does not cover it, so we cannot issue a contract regardless of the role.

specimens.reading: A hard constraint that is knowable on day one and was checked at the offer. Nothing about the candidate is being assessed here.

perspectives.sees: The list of jurisdictions where an entity or an employment provider can issue a contract, and a candidate record showing a country outside it.
perspectives.reads: A contract that cannot be signed, whatever the panel concluded. Adding a jurisdiction is a registration and tax decision, not a hiring one.
perspectives.does: Holds the coverage list as written, and leaves any exception to a separate approval running on its own quarterly cycle.

perspectives.sees: A residency answer that falls outside the approved country list — a check that can happen at the screen or at the offer paperwork.
perspectives.reads: This process ends here regardless of the panel's recommendation, and the requisition returns to sourcing while time-to-fill keeps counting.
perspectives.does: States the constraint at the screen, where the list is at hand, or delivers it at the offer stage in the wording available for it.

perspectives.sees: A posting marked remote, a process that runs normally, and a jurisdiction question arriving late — or a rejection minutes after submitting.
perspectives.reads: Either the location was disqualifying from the start, or something about the profile was. Nothing in the message separates the two.
perspectives.does: Records the stage at which the question was asked, and asks about entity coverage before the next remote process rather than after it.

perspectives.sees: Employment law and tax registration in each jurisdiction, and the conditions under which a cross-border employment relationship can exist at all.
perspectives.reads: A settled boundary, working as written. Nothing in it says at which point in a hiring process the boundary has to be disclosed.
perspectives.does: Sets the rule and the licensed intermediary arrangements that can carry an employment relationship across it, on a legislative cycle no single process can wait for.

non_inferences: The jurisdictional barrier is entirely independent of the candidate's technical competence.

title: Mid-Process Role Requirement Redefinition
content:
# Mid-Process Role Requirement Redefinition

The team changes the stack, the seniority level or the project scope while candidates are mid-process, and the assessments already taken no longer apply.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `hiring-manager`
- **Nature:** `noise`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `mech.unstated_compensation_band_discrepancy` — Unstated Compensation Band Discrepancy
- Amplifies `mech.inflated_requisition_requirements_vs_actual_team_needs` — Inflated Requisition Requirements vs Actual Team Needs
- Masks `mech.genuine_technical_skill_shortfall` — Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall

### Non-Inferences
- The rejection was driven by a shift in the team's mandate, not by the candidate's interview answers.
