summary: The team changes the stack, the seniority level or the project scope while candidates are mid-process, and the assessments already taken no longer apply.

specimens.label: The role that changed underneath

lines.text: Thank you for the four rounds — the panel notes were strong throughout.

Since we opened this req the team has moved the service to Rust and folded the on-call leadership into the role. Weighted against the new profile we are looking for someone with production Rust and formal lead experience.
I recognise you interviewed against the previous description. I am sorry about that.

specimens.reading: The assessments were not re-run; they were re-scored against a target that moved after they were taken.

perspectives.sees: The scope the role has to absorb has moved since the requisition was written, and the panel notes in front of them were taken against the earlier description.
perspectives.reads: Strong notes against a target that no longer exists. Re-running four rounds costs the team weeks it is already short of.
perspectives.does: Rewrites the requirements, re-scores the existing notes against them, and decides at which level, if any, the candidate is still a candidate.

perspectives.sees: A requisition whose description changes while candidates are mid-loop, and a hiring manager asking for a profile that was not in the original brief.
perspectives.reads: The pipeline built for the old brief no longer converts, and time-to-fill keeps counting from the date the requisition first opened.
perspectives.does: Restates the role to everyone still in process, or closes them out with the standard wording and sources again against the new description.

perspectives.sees: Four rounds of positive signal, then a rejection describing a role different from the one applied to, and a materially similar posting on the board afterwards.
perspectives.reads: The rounds were passed and the target moved, or the rounds were not passed and the changed description is the courteous version. Both readings fit the same email.
perspectives.does: Records the original description, the dates, and the wording of the change, and decides whether to ask which requirement is the new one.

perspectives.sees: An amended requisition arriving for re-approval at a different level or band, with the original still counted as open.
perspectives.reads: A level and band change on a requisition already approved, which is what the levelling grid exists to settle. Nothing in the amendment records the interview hours already spent against the old scope.
perspectives.does: Approves or refuses the new level and band, and the process resumes or stops at the reconciliation step.

non_inferences: The rejection was driven by a shift in the team's mandate, not by the candidate's interview answers.

title: Portfolio / Work Artifact Misinterpretation
content:
# Portfolio / Work Artifact Misinterpretation

The surface a screener opens does not show the candidate's architecture work, which sits in a non-standard repository layout or in contributions under another organisation.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `candidate`
- **Nature:** `noise`
- **Removability:** `candidate`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `mech.genuine_technical_skill_shortfall` — Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall

### Non-Inferences
- Misinterpreted architecture can be corrected through structured documentation.
summary: The surface a screener opens does not show the candidate's architecture work, which sits in a non-standard repository layout or in contributions under another organisation.

specimens.label: What the screener saw and what was there

lines.text: Screener note: mostly forks, little original work, no evidence of architecture ownership.
The account: 3 pinned forks, and 40 commits over two years to an upstream project under a different org — including the storage layer rewrite referenced in the CV.

specimens.reading: The work exists and the surface that was checked does not show it. This is a discovery failure, and it is one of the few the candidate can fix directly.

perspectives.sees: A rejection, or structured feedback naming a shortfall in an area the candidate has shipped work in.
perspectives.reads: The work exists. What is not visible from here is which surface was opened and what it showed.
perspectives.does: Restructures what is submitted: the relevant work pinned, the commits linked directly rather than the account, the ownership stated in the CV line rather than left to be discovered.

perspectives.sees: A link and the minutes available for it, against an inbound volume larger than the week's screening capacity.
perspectives.reads: The surface that opens is the profile. A page of forks reads as little original work, because what is not on it cannot be told apart from what does not exist.
perspectives.does: Records the note from what the page showed and moves to the next application. That note travels forward as the evidence about the candidate's work.

perspectives.sees: A shortlist and the screening notes attached to it, not the repositories themselves.
perspectives.reads: Architecture ownership was checked and not evidenced, which is what the note in front of them says.
perspectives.does: Spends the panel's time on the shortlist as delivered. Reopening a screened-out profile costs review hours the team is already short of.

non_inferences: Misinterpreted architecture can be corrected through structured documentation.

title: Pre-Selected Internal Candidate
content:
# Pre-Selected Internal Candidate

Requisition was publicly advertised to satisfy corporate policy or legal compliance while an internal employee was already earmarked for the role.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `policy`
- **Nature:** `incentive`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Masks `mech.stronger_competing_candidate_in_final_cohort` — Stronger Competing Candidate in Final Cohort

### Non-Inferences
- Cannot be asserted as fact without internal hiring log confirmation.
summary: Requisition was publicly advertised to satisfy corporate policy or legal compliance while an internal employee was already earmarked for the role.

specimens.label: Final round, an aside

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: How many people are you seeing for this?

lines.speaker: Hiring manager
lines.text: You are the third external. There is also someone internal who has been covering part of the scope since spring.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Understood. Is that a formal candidacy?

lines.speaker: Hiring manager
lines.text: It is. We post externally regardless — that is policy.

specimens.reading: Nothing improper is described. The posting is real, the process is real, and the odds were set before the first external application arrived.

perspectives.sees: A funded requisition, and a posting rule that applies to every requisition regardless of who already works inside the scope.
perspectives.reads: Consistency across hires is what makes a process defensible. A rule that holds for all requisitions cannot be switched off for one.
perspectives.does: Publishes externally as the rule requires. What happens to the external pipeline afterwards is not reported back to this layer.

perspectives.sees: Someone already covering part of the scope, and a slate of external candidates each assessed inside the hours the loop allows.
perspectives.reads: Work already observed and work inferred from an interview are not the same evidence. Only one person on the slate has been watched doing the work itself.
perspectives.does: Runs the external loop as posted and assesses each candidate against a bar the internal work already meets.

perspectives.sees: A live posting, scheduled rounds, and interviewers who prepare. The composition of the slate is not stated.
perspectives.reads: Nothing in the process distinguishes it from one that is open. Whether a requisition is already promised internally is not a field the candidate is shown.
perspectives.does: Can ask at the final round how many are being seen and whether any are internal. That answer is available on request and absent without one.

non_inferences: Cannot be asserted as fact without internal hiring log confirmation.

title: Probation Used as Extended De-Facto Interview
content:
# Probation Used as Extended De-Facto Interview

Managers lower late-stage interview thresholds, treating the statutory probation period as an extended live trial where underperformance results in immediate low-friction dismissal.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `hiring-manager`
- **Nature:** `incentive`
- **Removability:** `intermediary`

### Non-Inferences
- Does not establish that the employee committed gross misconduct.
summary: Managers lower late-stage interview thresholds, treating the statutory probation period as an extended live trial where underperformance results in immediate low-friction dismissal.

specimens.label: Probation exit note

lines.text: Candidate onboarding evaluated over 60 days.
Delivery pace did not ramp to senior independent output within month two.
Notice issued under the statutory probation clause of the Ukrainian Labour Code.

specimens.reading: The interview process was truncated under the assumption that probation serves as the true filtering phase.

perspectives.sees: Direct on-the-job output under real sprint pressure, treating probation as a higher-fidelity filter than multi-round panel interviews.
perspectives.reads: Hiring fast and pruning early during probation reduces upfront interview coordination costs.
perspectives.does: Replaces extensive technical testing with early probationary evaluation.

perspectives.sees: A full employment offer that operates in practice as a temporary contract with heightened termination exposure.
perspectives.reads: The real hiring threshold was shifted post-start without explicit pre-acceptance disclosure.
perspectives.does: Delivers aggressively during initial months while maintaining external professional networks.

perspectives.sees: Probation turnover rates and dismissal compliance documentation under the Ukrainian Labour Code's constraints.
perspectives.reads: High probation turnover increases team onboarding costs while preserving statutory compliance.
perspectives.does: Monitors probation pass rates and reviews termination justifications.

non_inferences: Does not establish that the employee committed gross misconduct.

title: Recruiter Volume & Quota Incentive Distortion
content:
# Recruiter Volume & Quota Incentive Distortion

Applicant volume (500+ per req) runs past the screening hours available; profiles are read at the speed of the queue and matched against the pattern the requisition was described with.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `recruiter`
- **Nature:** `incentive`
- **Removability:** `intermediary`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `mech.interview_resource_scheduling_saturation` — Interview Resource & Scheduling Saturation
- Masks `mech.automated_keyword_qualification_filter` — Automated Keyword / Qualification Filter

### Non-Inferences
- Does not mean the recruiter is individually negligent; the capacity mismatch is structural.
summary: Applicant volume (500+ per req) runs past the screening hours available; profiles are read at the speed of the queue and matched against the pattern the requisition was described with.

specimens.label: The queue the screen ran against

lines.text: Applications received: 640
Recruiter screening capacity this week: 40
Median time spent per profile: 7 seconds
Profiles advanced: 11

specimens.reading: Seven seconds is not a judgement of a career. It is what a queue of 640 does to attention, whoever is holding it.

perspectives.sees: The count of open requisitions, the inbound volume against them, and the screening hours available this week. The three numbers do not reconcile.
perspectives.reads: The time a profile receives is set by the length of the queue rather than by the profile. Throughput and conversion are measured; time-to-clarity is not a field in the report.
perspectives.does: Advances the profiles that match the pattern the requisition was described with, and the rest of the queue stays unopened. Nothing is sent about a profile that was never opened.

perspectives.sees: Nothing after submission, or an outreach that opens a conversation and then stops.
perspectives.reads: Silence has no field to read. An application that was never opened and one that was read and declined produce the same inbox.
perspectives.does: Records the submission date and the date of the last message, and keeps other processes running rather than waiting on the queue.

perspectives.sees: Records that are created and never opened, and the age of each one against an expiry threshold that ships enabled.
perspectives.reads: An unreviewed application at the threshold is a housekeeping state, not a decision. Whether the queue was longer than the hours available is not a value in the record.
perspectives.does: Closes the record at the configured age and sends whatever the customer's template sends at that event.

non_inferences: Does not mean the recruiter is individually negligent; the capacity mismatch is structural.

title: Reference Check Discrepancy or Regulatory Ineligibility
content:
# Reference Check Discrepancy or Regulatory Ineligibility

A third-party check returns employment dates it could not verify, a degree the registrar has not confirmed, or a prior engagement flagged as a conflict of interest.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `candidate`
- **Nature:** `rule`
- **Removability:** `candidate`

### Non-Inferences
- An administrative mismatch in dates is distinct from fraudulent misrepresentation on a CV.
summary: A third-party check returns employment dates it could not verify, a degree the registrar has not confirmed, or a prior engagement flagged as a conflict of interest.

specimens.label: Where the check disagreed with the record

lines.text: The background provider returned a mismatch on employment dates for one role: our vendor has March 2019 – June 2021, your application states January 2019 – August 2021.
We are required to pause the offer while this is reconciled. If you have a payslip or contract covering those months, that resolves it.

specimens.reading: A resolvable discrepancy in a third-party record, with a named document that closes it. This is one of the few mechanisms with a direct, evidenced remedy.

perspectives.sees: An offer placed on hold and a named field in dispute: dates on one role, a degree the registrar has not confirmed, a prior engagement flagged as a conflict.
perspectives.reads: A third-party record and their own record disagree. Which one is wrong is answerable, and the document that answers it is either in hand or obtainable.
perspectives.does: Produces the payslip, contract or transcript covering the disputed months, and from here on states dates as the payroll record holds them rather than as remembered.

perspectives.sees: A vendor result marked for review, naming the field and the two values. The underlying records sit with the provider, not in the ATS.
perspectives.reads: The start date is at risk until the file closes, and the result does not say which side of the mismatch is the error.
perspectives.does: Pauses onboarding, asks the candidate for the document that reconciles the field, and keeps the wording to what the check returned.

perspectives.sees: The check result against the standard this layer wrote: which findings a document can reconcile, and which end the process regardless of explanation.
perspectives.reads: One rule applied the same way to every hire is the defensible position. An exception made once is a precedent that has to be defended later.
perspectives.does: Holds the offer until the file closes, and fixes how much of the reason may be stated — which is what determines whether the candidate is told the field or told nothing.

non_inferences: An administrative mismatch in dates is distinct from fraudulent misrepresentation on a CV.

title: Speculative Sourcing / Talent Pooling Without Opening
content:
# Speculative Sourcing / Talent Pooling Without Opening

Recruiters open conversations and build candidate pools against headcount that has not been approved or funded.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `recruiter`
- **Nature:** `incentive`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `mech.recruiter_volume_quota_incentive_distortion` — Recruiter Volume & Quota Incentive Distortion

### Non-Inferences
- Ghosting after an outbound message indicates the absence of an immediate opening, not a rejection of the profile.
summary: Recruiters open conversations and build candidate pools against headcount that has not been approved or funded.

specimens.label: What the outreach was actually for

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Great talking today. To set expectations — is there an open requisition behind this?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Not yet. We are building a bench ahead of the Q3 planning round; if the headcount is approved you would be first in line.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Understood, thanks for saying so.

specimens.reading: A straight answer converts a mystery into a schedule. The same silence three months later means something entirely different once this line exists.

perspectives.sees: Planning signals about headcount that is not yet approved, and a market where the profiles worth contacting are contacted early.
perspectives.reads: A pipeline built now converts if the requisition lands; a pipeline built after approval starts from zero, and time-to-fill is measured either way.
perspectives.does: Opens conversations ahead of approval and holds them with no stage to move them into until the headcount is decided.

perspectives.sees: Direct outreach describing a specific role, then a conversation, then no reply — and no posting to check the role against.
perspectives.reads: Silence after a specific conversation reads as an assessment of the profile. Nothing in the exchange separates that from a requisition that was never opened.
perspectives.does: Asks whether a requisition exists and is funded before spending rounds on it, and treats the answer as the date the process actually starts.

perspectives.sees: Headcount requests arriving at planning with named candidates already attached to them.
perspectives.reads: A team ready to move quickly if the role is approved. The conversations that produced the names are not part of the approval record.
perspectives.does: Decides funding on the quarterly cycle, and an approval or a deferral closes conversations this layer never saw.

perspectives.sees: Contact records held in a talent pool with no requisition attached, and nurture sequences configured against them.
perspectives.reads: A supported workflow behaving normally. The platform does not require a requisition to exist before outreach is sent from it.
perspectives.does: Ships the pool, the sequences and the expiry defaults; whether a record is attached to an open requisition stays a field the customer fills or leaves blank.

non_inferences: Ghosting after an outbound message indicates the absence of an immediate opening, not a rejection of the profile.

title: Stale or Orphaned Job Requisition
content:
# Stale or Orphaned Job Requisition

Job posting remains active on careers page and aggregator portals despite the team having ceased active hiring or closed headcount.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `system`
- **Nature:** `void`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `mech.automated_application_expiration_timeout` — Automated Application Expiration Timeout

### Non-Inferences
- Application silence does not reflect candidate suitability.
summary: Job posting remains active on careers page and aggregator portals despite the team having ceased active hiring or closed headcount.

specimens.label: Asking whether the role is alive

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: I applied for this in January and again in March — is the posting current?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Let me check. That team stopped hiring in December; the listing should have come down. I will get it removed.

specimens.reading: The posting was not bait and it was not a decision. It was a record nobody owned, which is a different thing to be angry at.

perspectives.sees: A requisition moved to paused or unfunded in the budget ledger.
perspectives.reads: Pausing an approved requisition keeps the option to restart it, and the approval costs nothing while it sits.
perspectives.does: Records the change where budgets are recorded. Taking a public listing down is a separate action in a separate system, and the budget decision does not trigger it.

perspectives.sees: A posting record in an active state, and applications arriving against it.
perspectives.reads: The state of the record is a customer-owned field. Nothing distinguishes a running search from a record no one has closed.
perspectives.does: Keeps rendering and syndicating the posting and accepting applications, and closes the unreviewed ones when the default expiry period runs out.

perspectives.sees: The requisition list as the platform holds it, in which a listing no longer being worked looks like any other.
perspectives.reads: Whether a search is still running is a fact held by the team that stopped, not by the funnel.
perspectives.does: Answers directly and has the listing removed once the question arrives. A requisition with no search behind it does not enter time-to-fill, which is what is counted.

perspectives.sees: A posting visible on the careers page and on aggregators, and no reply after submission.
perspectives.reads: Silence is the same artifact whether a record was left open or an application was read and set aside.
perspectives.does: Asks directly whether the posting is current, which is the only channel that returns the state of the record, and keeps the date of each submission.

non_inferences: Application silence does not reflect candidate suitability.

title: Start-Date Slippage and Post-Acceptance Revocation
content:
# Start-Date Slippage and Post-Acceptance Revocation

Employers defer confirmed start dates or revoke accepted offers between signing and day one when budgeting priorities or project authorisations change.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `policy`
- **Nature:** `incentive`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Non-Inferences
- Does not establish that candidate credentials or references failed validation.
summary: Employers defer confirmed start dates or revoke accepted offers between signing and day one when budgeting priorities or project authorisations change.

specimens.label: Start-date deferral notice

lines.text: We are finalizing internal team allocations and will be confirming the revised start date shortly.
Please do not report to the office until the updated equipment schedule is issued.

specimens.reading: The delay manages company cash flow and headcount quotas by deferring payroll liability onto the candidate.

perspectives.sees: A hiring freeze or executive budget revision taking effect across pending hires before day-one employment commencement.
perspectives.reads: Deferring start dates avoids immediate payroll commitments during headcount transitions.
perspectives.does: Freezes onboarding queues and issues holding notifications.

perspectives.sees: A signed offer with an indefinite or pushed start date after resigning from previous employment.
perspectives.reads: Contractual commitment was asymmetrical: candidate resignation is irreversible while company start date is deferred.
perspectives.does: Assesses legal notice entitlements under the UK Employment Rights Act 1996 and evaluates reopening active job search.

perspectives.sees: A closed search reopened administratively because the approved start date cannot be scheduled.
perspectives.reads: Hiring quotas shifted after offer signature, leaving recruiter metrics and candidate stranded.
perspectives.does: Attempts to maintain contact while leadership resolves headcount funding.

non_inferences: Does not establish that candidate credentials or references failed validation.

title: Stronger Competing Candidate in Final Cohort
content:
# Stronger Competing Candidate in Final Cohort

Candidate cleared all passing bars, but another applicant in the same pipeline demonstrated superior domain overlap or lower onboarding overhead.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `candidate`
- **Nature:** `rule`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Masks `mech.genuine_technical_skill_shortfall` — Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall

### Non-Inferences
- Does not mean candidate had negative feedback; relative cohort ranking is outside candidate control.
summary: Candidate cleared all passing bars, but another applicant in the same pipeline demonstrated superior domain overlap or lower onboarding overhead.

specimens.label: Rejection naming the comparison

lines.text: This was a genuinely difficult decision — you cleared every bar we set.
We went with another finalist who has shipped the same payment rails we are migrating to, which shortens the ramp by a quarter or so.
If anything opens at this level again I would like to come back to you directly.

specimens.reading: Nothing here says the candidate fell short. A comparison decided it, and comparisons are not properties of either person.

perspectives.sees: A decline that arrives after every round has been cleared, with no account of who else was in the final group.
perspectives.reads: From outside, a bar unmet and a comparison lost arrive in the same envelope. The cohort is not a field the candidate can see.
perspectives.does: Goes back over their own rounds, because they are the only variable available: the ranking that decided it comes back in answer to no question.

perspectives.sees: Finalists who all clear the bar, and the difference in what each would need before they work unaided.
perspectives.reads: The decision is a ranking between acceptable people, not a fault found in either. Ramp-up is the difference that can be stated.
perspectives.does: Takes the shorter ramp and closes the requisition. A ranking produces no fault to send back, so there is nothing specific to hand to the recruiter.

perspectives.sees: One requisition, several finalists, and a decision that names a choice rather than a shortfall.
perspectives.reads: Nothing in the outcome reads as feedback, and what decided it is a fact about a person who is not the recipient.
perspectives.does: Sends the standard wording and keeps the file for a later requisition at the same level.

non_inferences: Does not mean candidate had negative feedback; relative cohort ranking is outside candidate control.

title: Take-Home Evaluation Fatigue & Asymmetry
content:
# Take-Home Evaluation Fatigue & Asymmetry

A 15-hour take-home is reviewed in minutes, and the structure and tests held outside the files that were opened do not reach the assessment.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `hiring-manager`
- **Nature:** `noise`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `mech.interview_resource_scheduling_saturation` — Interview Resource & Scheduling Saturation
- Masks `mech.genuine_technical_skill_shortfall` — Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall

### Non-Inferences
- A take-home rejection made under evaluation fatigue does not measure the engineering in the submission.
summary: A 15-hour take-home is reviewed in minutes, and the structure and tests held outside the files that were opened do not reach the assessment.

specimens.label: Review record for a 15-hour submission

lines.text: Submission: 41 files, 78 tests, migrations, README with design rationale.
Reviewer time logged: 6 minutes. Files opened: 3.
Note: no tests visible, structure unclear.

specimens.reading: The note is false about the submission and true about the review. The asymmetry between the two efforts is the mechanism.

perspectives.sees: A submission and a review slot wedged between the team's own delivery work. The rubric is a form with fields for structure, correctness and tests.
perspectives.reads: What the opened files show is what the submission shows. Anything held elsewhere in the repository is not part of the assessment being written.
perspectives.does: Fills the rubric from what was opened and carries that note into the debrief, where it stands as the account of the whole submission.

perspectives.sees: A completed rubric and a one-line verdict. The time logged against the review is not in the fields the recruiter reads.
perspectives.reads: The panel read the work and the verdict stands for the reading. Nothing in the record separates a thin submission from a thin reading of one.
perspectives.does: Sends the rejection in the template wording and closes the record. The review note stays inside the debrief; nothing obliges it to travel further.

perspectives.sees: The hours the assignment took, the date it was submitted, and a rejection in standard wording some days later.
perspectives.reads: The work was read and found insufficient — the only reading the message supports, since nothing in it separates a person's verdict from a rule's.
perspectives.does: There is no named defect to correct. The next assignment is approached the same way, or declined once the unpaid hours are weighed against a process whose state is unknown.

non_inferences: A take-home rejection made under evaluation fatigue does not measure the engineering in the submission.

title: Unstated Compensation Band Discrepancy
content:
# Unstated Compensation Band Discrepancy

Candidate market rate exceeds budgeted compensation for the requisition, but salary band was never published or clarified early.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `policy`
- **Nature:** `rule`
- **Removability:** `intermediary`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `mech.mid_process_role_requirement_redefinition` — Mid-Process Role Requirement Redefinition
- Masks `mech.genuine_technical_skill_shortfall` — Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall

### Non-Inferences
- Rejection does not mean candidate is overpriced for the market, only mismatched with this specific employer budget.
summary: Candidate market rate exceeds budgeted compensation for the requisition, but salary band was never published or clarified early.

specimens.label: The number nobody published

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Before the manager round — what were your expectations again?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: 85–95k, as I mentioned at the screen.

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Right. I should be straight with you: the approved budget for this req tops out at 74k. It was never in the posting.

specimens.reading: The mismatch existed on day one and surfaced in week four. Four rounds were spent on a gap that a published band would have shown immediately.

perspectives.sees: The approved maximum for the requisition, the levelling grid it sits on, and the disclosure rules that apply to the posting.
perspectives.reads: The band is a control on cost across every hire. Whether it is published is a separate question, answered by the rules of the jurisdiction.
perspectives.does: Sets the ceiling and what may be stated, on a cycle measured in quarters. The hours one process spends above that ceiling appear nowhere in that cycle.

perspectives.sees: The approved maximum in the requisition, and the candidate's stated expectation from the screen.
perspectives.reads: A gap here decides the outcome whatever the panel returns.
perspectives.does: Chooses when the number is stated, which is the point where this can still be closed early. Saying it early ends a pipeline on a metric that is measured, and saves rounds on one that is not.

perspectives.sees: A posting with no band, and a question about expectations asked before any number is offered.
perspectives.reads: The figure given can be checked against nothing. The band, the level and the grid are all outside what the candidate is shown.
perspectives.does: States a range and records when it was asked and what was said. Asking for the band at the screen is the one point where the gap can surface early.

perspectives.sees: Whether the posting falls inside a jurisdiction where a band must be stated, and whether a stated band appears.
perspectives.reads: A published band closes the branch a disclosure rule reaches. The level a candidate is assessed at, and the grid behind it, sit outside the text of the rule.
perspectives.does: Writes to what is enforceable and measurable, which is the presence of a number in a posting rather than the reconciliation that happens later.

non_inferences: Rejection does not mean candidate is overpriced for the market, only mismatched with this specific employer budget.

title: Closed-Then-Reposted Requisition Motif
content:
# Closed-Then-Reposted Requisition Motif

A candidate completes multiple late-stage interviews, is rejected with a generic message, and sees the identical role reposted weeks later.

### Trigger Rule
The role is closed and the candidate rejected, and a materially similar listing is publicly reopened within 60 days.

### What this Establishes
- The interviewed pool did not meet the requisition's requirements or target profile, or the search criteria changed mid-process.

### What this Does NOT Establish
- Does not establish that the original job listing was fake or a ghost job.
- Does not establish that the candidate was intentionally misled.
summary: A candidate completes multiple late-stage interviews, is rejected with a generic message, and sees the identical role reposted weeks later.
trigger_rule: The role is closed and the candidate rejected, and a materially similar listing is publicly reopened within 60 days.
establishes: The interviewed pool did not meet the requisition's requirements or target profile, or the search criteria changed mid-process.
non_inferences: Does not establish that the original job listing was fake or a ghost job.
Does not establish that the candidate was intentionally misled.

specimens.label: The sequence, as recorded

lines.text: Applied — req #4471
Recruiter screen — passed
Technical panel — passed
Final round with hiring manager — completed
Rejected — generic template, no specifics given
req #4471 visible on the careers page again, text unchanged

specimens.reading: Late-stage progress, a contentless rejection, and the same requisition number back on the board. The sequence is the observation; its cause is not in the sequence.

specimens.label: The question that splits the branches

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: I saw req #4471 listed again. Is this a new opening on the team, or the same one?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Same requisition. We restarted the search with a revised profile after the first round of interviews.

specimens.reading: A revised profile, an automated refresh and a genuinely new headcount are three different mechanisms with one appearance. This is the question that tells them apart.

perspectives.sees: A generic rejection after a final round, and the same requisition number back on the careers page weeks later with the text unchanged.
perspectives.reads: Either the profile was revised, or the platform refreshed the listing, or the headcount is new — and the sequence on its own does not separate them.
perspectives.does: Asks whether the listing is the same requisition, and records the dates and the answer before deciding whether to reapply.

perspectives.sees: The requisition record moving from closed back to open with a revised profile, and a rejection template that is the same for every candidate at that stage.
perspectives.reads: This is one continuous search that changed shape, not two openings.
perspectives.does: Sends the standard wording, since a specific reason given at the close of one round can be quoted back at the next, and states the restart when a candidate asks directly.

perspectives.sees: Two finalists at the end of a loop, and the work the role exists to absorb still uncovered.
perspectives.reads: A loop that ended without a hire is information about the profile, and the profile is the part of this the manager controls.
perspectives.does: Rewrites the requirements and restarts the search on the same requisition, because a new requisition would go back through funding.

perspectives.sees: A requisition whose status returned to open, and a scheduled refresh that pushes open listings back out to aggregators with a current date.
perspectives.reads: An open requisition is a listing to distribute; the refresh reads the status field and not the history behind it.
perspectives.does: Republishes under the original identifier and stamps the posting with today's date, which is the default behaviour for any open requisition.

title: Compensation Double Bind
content:
# Compensation Double Bind

The candidate has to name a compensation expectation first: a high number ends the process, and a low one lowers the level the candidate is assessed at.

### Trigger Rule
The candidate is asked for a compensation number before the band for the role is stated, and the band is not stated in return.

### What this Establishes
- An information asymmetry works as an uncalibrated filter before technical merit is assessed.

### What this Does NOT Establish
- Does not establish that the employer has an unlimited budget, or that any of this is malicious.
summary: The candidate has to name a compensation expectation first: a high number ends the process, and a low one lowers the level the candidate is assessed at.
trigger_rule: The candidate is asked for a compensation number before the band for the role is stated, and the band is not stated in return.
establishes: An information asymmetry works as an uncalibrated filter before technical merit is assessed.
non_inferences: Does not establish that the employer has an unlimited budget, or that any of this is malicious.

specimens.label: The asymmetry, in four messages

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Before we go further — what are your compensation expectations?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Happy to discuss. What is the band for the role?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: We prefer to hear the candidate number first so we can match it to the right level.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Understood. My expectation is in the range of 85–95k.

specimens.reading: The number is required from one side and withheld by the other, and it is collected before the level is fixed. Both outcomes below follow from that ordering.

specimens.label: The two branches
specimens.context: the same question, two candidates, one week

lines.text: Quoted 95k — We are not able to proceed; the expectation is outside the range we have for this role.
Quoted 70k — Good news, we would like to move ahead. Based on the conversation we are looking at this as a mid-level hire rather than senior.

specimens.reading: A high number ends the process and a low one moves the level. There is no answer that leaves both the process and the grade untouched — which is what makes it a bind rather than a negotiation.

perspectives.sees: A request for a compensation expectation at the screen, and a band that is not stated in return.
perspectives.reads: The number is collected before the level is fixed, so it is an input to the level rather than an answer to it.
perspectives.does: Names a range without the band, without the level, and without knowing how many others in the pipeline have already named one.

perspectives.sees: A screening form with an expectations field that has to be filled before the candidate moves to the panel, and disclosure rules for the band that are set elsewhere.
perspectives.reads: The number is the cheapest available check on whether the process is viable, before panel time is spent on it.
perspectives.does: Asks for the number first and records it in the field, and says about the band exactly what is permitted at this stage.

perspectives.sees: A band per level and a rule about what may be said about it, both reviewed on a cycle measured in quarters.
perspectives.reads: A stated expectation is the input that places a candidate on the grid; a band stated first becomes the floor of every negotiation that follows.
perspectives.does: Publishes the band where a disclosure rule requires it and not elsewhere, and keeps levelling a decision separate from the number.

perspectives.sees: Postings in covered jurisdictions, which either carry a band or do not.
perspectives.reads: A published band is measurable and enforceable; the level a candidate will be assessed at is neither.
perspectives.does: Requires the band in the posting, which closes one branch of the bind and leaves the levelling branch untouched.

title: Experience-Age Impossibility
content:
# Experience-Age Impossibility

A requisition requires more years of hands-on experience with a specific framework or tool than that technology has existed in the open-source ecosystem.

### Trigger Rule
Job description or automated screen requires X years of experience where X > technology_age.

### What this Establishes
- The job description was written without technical review, from a copied template whose thresholds run as automated gating rules.

### What this Does NOT Establish
- Does not establish that the technical team is incompetent, only that the HR screening pipeline has no technical review.
summary: A requisition requires more years of hands-on experience with a specific framework or tool than that technology has existed in the open-source ecosystem.
trigger_rule: Job description or automated screen requires X years of experience where X > technology_age.
establishes: The job description was written without technical review, from a copied template whose thresholds run as automated gating rules.
non_inferences: Does not establish that the technical team is incompetent, only that the HR screening pipeline has no technical review.

specimens.label: The requirement, as published
specimens.subject: Senior Platform Engineer — requirements

lines.text: 7+ years of production experience with Kubernetes.
5+ years with a framework first released three years ago.
Screening is automated: applications below the stated year counts are filtered before human review.

specimens.reading: This is checkable against a release date, which makes it one of the few claims in hiring that can simply be false rather than debatable.

specimens.label: What the filter did with it

lines.text: Application submitted
Rule: years_with_framework >= 5 — candidate value 3 — FAIL
Status: Rejected — does not meet minimum criteria

specimens.reading: No one decided anything about this candidate. An impossible threshold was copied into a rule and the rule ran.

perspectives.sees: A posting requiring more years with a framework than the framework has existed, and a rejection minutes after submitting, outside working hours.
perspectives.reads: The threshold is checkable against a release date, which makes this one of the few claims in a posting that can be false rather than arguable.
perspectives.does: Keeps the posting text and the time of the rejection, which can be set against the release date; the requirement itself reaches nobody who could rewrite it.

perspectives.sees: A draft posting assembled from the template of a previous requisition, reviewed for the part that describes the team's work.
perspectives.reads: Years of experience is a shorthand for depth, and in the draft that figure carries less weight than the description of the role.
perspectives.does: Approves the draft and returns to the delivery the requisition exists to cover; the number reaches a screening rule without passing a technical review.

perspectives.sees: A configured knockout rule comparing a parsed year count against a threshold the customer entered.
perspectives.reads: A value below the threshold is a fail; whether the threshold is reachable at all is not a property the rule can evaluate.
perspectives.does: Rejects at submission and emits the standard does-not-meet-minimum-criteria notice, in seconds, at whatever hour it arrives.

title: Seniority Double Bind
content:
# Seniority Double Bind

The same candidate is rejected as overqualified for junior and mid-level roles and as underqualified, or not specialised enough, for staff and leadership roles.

### Trigger Rule
The candidate is rejected as overqualified at level N and as short on depth at level N+1 within the same market cycle.

### What this Establishes
- The candidate falls into a gap between evaluation tiers, where the compensation and experience expected match neither tier.

### What this Does NOT Establish
- Does not establish that the candidate lacks market value.
- Does not establish malice or coordinated collusion between employers.
summary: The same candidate is rejected as overqualified for junior and mid-level roles and as underqualified, or not specialised enough, for staff and leadership roles.
trigger_rule: The candidate is rejected as overqualified at level N and as short on depth at level N+1 within the same market cycle.
establishes: The candidate falls into a gap between evaluation tiers, where the compensation and experience expected match neither tier.
non_inferences: Does not establish that the candidate lacks market value.
Does not establish malice or coordinated collusion between employers.

specimens.label: Two rejections, six weeks apart
specimens.context: same candidate, same market, adjacent levels

lines.text: 12 Feb — Senior Backend Engineer (level 4). Your experience sits above the band scoped for this role and we were concerned it would not hold your interest.
26 Mar — Staff Engineer (level 5). The panel felt the depth of platform ownership was not yet at staff scope; we would look for a broader track record of org-wide impact.
Both roles: same city, same domain, same six-week window.

specimens.reading: Neither message is unreasonable on its own. Put next to each other they describe a candidate who is above one level and below the next, with nothing in between open.

specimens.label: What the pair does and does not establish

lines.text: Established: two rejections, two stated grounds, two adjacent levels, one market cycle.

Not established: that either judgement was wrong, that the two employers coordinated, or that the candidate is unhireable. The motif is a property of the level grid, not of the person moving through it.

specimens.reading: The pattern is worth naming precisely because each half is defensible. The trap is structural, which is also why no single conversation can argue it away.

perspectives.sees: Two rejections inside one market cycle: one saying the experience sits above the band scoped for the role, one saying the depth is not yet at the next level's scope.
perspectives.reads: Together the two messages describe a person who is above one rung and below the next, with nothing open in between.
perspectives.does: Applies at both levels at once and shifts what the CV emphasises depending on which rung the posting names.

perspectives.sees: A profile whose years and previous scope sit above the band approved for the requisition being screened.
perspectives.reads: An expectation above the band reads as an offer that will not close, and the level of the requisition is fixed before the screen begins.
perspectives.does: Closes the application against this requisition and writes the rejection in terms of fit with the level it was opened at.

perspectives.sees: A candidate in a staff-level round, assessed against the scope the panel has agreed for that level: ownership across an organisation rather than a team.
perspectives.reads: A track record that has not yet run at that scope is a risk that lands on the person who makes the hire.
perspectives.does: Records a not-at-this-level decision and leaves the requisition open: a bad hire carries a name and a search still running does not.

perspectives.sees: A levelling grid in which every level has a band and the bands are contiguous, and requisitions that are each opened at a single level.
perspectives.reads: A candidate above one band and below the next is a mismatch between a person and a particular requisition, not a gap in the grid; the grid is what makes offers consistent across every hire.
perspectives.does: Holds the grid steady through the cycle and approves requisitions at one level, because the level is the unit finance funds.

title: Employment Gap Penalty Loop
content:
# Employment Gap Penalty Loop

An employment gap triggers automated downranking (mech.employment_gap_downranking_bias), which pushes the profile below keyword and qualification filters (mech.automated_keyword_qualification_filter); fewer interview invitations lengthen the gap, which in turn strengthens the downranking.

### Cycle Dynamics
This causal loop reinforces mechanisms across iterations:
- `mech.employment_gap_downranking_bias` amplifies `mech.automated_keyword_qualification_filter`
- `mech.automated_keyword_qualification_filter` amplifies `mech.employment_gap_downranking_bias`
summary: An employment gap triggers automated downranking (mech.employment_gap_downranking_bias), which pushes the profile below keyword and qualification filters (mech.automated_keyword_qualification_filter); fewer interview invitations lengthen the gap, which in turn strengthens the downranking.

specimens.label: The same profile, two cycles apart
specimens.context: same CV, same market, nine months between

lines.text: Cycle 1 — skills 91, domain 88, continuity penalty −22 (gap 14 months) → rank 57
Cycle 2 — skills 91, domain 88, continuity penalty −34 (gap 23 months) → rank 45
Advance threshold both times: 60.

specimens.reading: Nothing in the work changed between the two rows. The only variable that moved is the one the penalty reads, and it moves because the penalty worked the first time.

specimens.label: Why the loop closes

lines.text: Downranking pushes the profile below the filter threshold.
Below the threshold there are no interviews.
No interviews means no offer, so the gap continues to grow.
A longer gap increases the penalty on the next application.

specimens.reading: Each step is a reasonable rule on its own. Together they form a cycle whose input is its own output.

perspectives.sees: Applications that return no reply at all, or a generic rejection, with the same CV and the same market as the cycle before.
perspectives.reads: Something in the profile moved between cycles, and the only thing that did move is the length of the break itself.
perspectives.does: Keeps applying, since applications are the only input available, and each month without an interview adds to the break the next application carries.

perspectives.sees: A ranked queue of several hundred applications against capacity to read a few dozen, on a requisition where time-to-fill is measured.
perspectives.reads: The order is a triage of a list that cannot be read end to end, not a judgement about anyone in it.
perspectives.does: Reads from the top down until the week's capacity is used, which is where the ranking becomes the decision.

perspectives.sees: A continuity feature computed from the dates in the parsed work history, shipping enabled by default.
perspectives.reads: It is one input among several in a ranking the buyer evaluates on throughput; whether a low-scored profile was unreadable rather than unqualified is not something the score records.
perspectives.does: Applies the penalty on every scoring pass and offers it as a setting the customer can switch off, which nothing in the default configuration prompts anyone to do.

title: Inflated-Requirements Search Saturation Loop
content:
# Inflated-Requirements Search Saturation Loop

Teams write inflated requirements that filter out strong generalists; the search stays open for months, recruiters tire of it, and the role is redefined mid-process.

### Cycle Dynamics
This causal loop reinforces mechanisms across iterations:
- `mech.inflated_requisition_requirements_vs_actual_team_needs` amplifies `mech.automated_keyword_qualification_filter`
- `mech.automated_keyword_qualification_filter` amplifies `mech.mid_process_role_requirement_redefinition`
- `mech.mid_process_role_requirement_redefinition` amplifies `mech.inflated_requisition_requirements_vs_actual_team_needs`
summary: Teams write inflated requirements that filter out strong generalists; the search stays open for months, recruiters tire of it, and the role is redefined mid-process.

specimens.label: The same requisition, rewritten twice

lines.text: Month 0 — 8 required technologies, 7+ years, staff-level scope. Applications: 340. Advanced to onsite: 2. Hired: 0.
Month 3 — search still open. Requirements rewritten upward: 10 technologies, 9+ years, plus formal lead experience.
Month 6 — search still open. Recruiter reassigned; team now covering the work with overtime.

specimens.reading: The response to a failed search was a narrower filter. The filter was the reason the search failed, which is the turn that makes this a loop.

specimens.label: Where the requirement came from

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Do we really need nine years and Rust for this? The backlog is mostly billing endpoints.

lines.speaker: Hiring manager
lines.text: Nobody good has applied in three months. If we lower the bar we will get more of the same.

specimens.reading: The inference runs backwards: an empty pipeline is read as evidence that the bar is too low. That reading is what tightens the next iteration.

perspectives.sees: Three months of applications, two candidates reaching onsite, no hire, and the team covering the work with overtime.
perspectives.reads: The pipeline holds nobody the panel wanted, and a lower bar would add to the pool it has already turned down.
perspectives.does: Rewrites the requirements upward, adds the missing signal as a formal requirement, and reposts: a bad hire is recorded against them and an open search is not.

perspectives.sees: A requisition ageing past the time-to-fill it is measured on, and a requirements list that got longer at the rewrite.
perspectives.reads: The requirements belong to the hiring manager, who is the internal client for this search.
perspectives.does: Raises the question once, posts the revised text, and moves screening capacity to requisitions that can close.

perspectives.sees: A posting with ten required technologies, a nine-year threshold and a lead requirement, republished with a longer list than the version before it.
perspectives.reads: The list is either the bar or a wish, and the posting does not say which; the year thresholds are the part a filter can act on.
perspectives.does: Skips the posting or applies against a list they do not match, and never learns which of the requirements the screen enforced.

title: Take-Home Opportunity-Cost Saturation Loop
content:
# Take-Home Opportunity-Cost Saturation Loop

Candidates spend heavy hours on take-home assignments with no bounded scope, which leaves less time for applications, while reviewers work through the queue under evaluation fatigue.

### Cycle Dynamics
This causal loop reinforces mechanisms across iterations:
- `mech.interview_resource_scheduling_saturation` amplifies `mech.take_home_evaluation_fatigue_asymmetry`
- `mech.take_home_evaluation_fatigue_asymmetry` amplifies `mech.interview_resource_scheduling_saturation`
summary: Candidates spend heavy hours on take-home assignments with no bounded scope, which leaves less time for applications, while reviewers work through the queue under evaluation fatigue.

specimens.label: One month of a candidate calendar

lines.text: Take-home A: 14 hours. Take-home B: 11 hours. Take-home C: 16 hours.
Applications sent that month: 4 — down from 21 the month before.
Outcomes: two rejections after sub-ten-minute reviews, one no response, one still open.

specimens.reading: The hours are real and they come out of the same budget as the search itself. Fewer applications is not a change in motivation; it is arithmetic.

specimens.label: The same month from the reviewer side

lines.text: Submissions in the queue: 19 · Reviewer capacity: 2 hours per week
Median review time per submission: 6 minutes.
Reviewers report the assignments are too large to assess properly, and the scope is set by the same team.

specimens.reading: Both sides are short of the same thing. Larger assignments do not buy better signal — they buy shallower reads, which is what makes it a loop rather than a trade-off.

perspectives.sees: Assignments scoped at a few hours that take double-digit hours each, and rejections returned faster than the work can be read.
perspectives.reads: The hours come out of the same budget as the search itself, so each assignment is a bet placed against the applications not sent that week.
perspectives.does: Sends fewer applications and finishes the assignments already accepted, because the hours in them are already spent.

perspectives.sees: A queue of submissions and interviewer hours that are already committed to the sprint the role exists to relieve.
perspectives.reads: A larger assignment covers more of the job, and a full read of every submission is not available from the hours the team has.
perspectives.does: Keeps the scope, since a smaller assignment would decide less, and the reviews get the minutes left after the team's own delivery.

perspectives.sees: Candidates going quiet between the assignment being sent and the work coming back, and time-to-fill running on the requisition.
perspectives.reads: A stage where the pipeline stalls is a reason to put more people into it, not a reason to remove the stage.
perspectives.does: Sends reminders and reopens sourcing, which puts more submissions into the same review queue.

title: A named decider and a written rule for a split panel
content:
# A named decider and a written rule for a split panel

Before the panel sits, one member is named as holding the decision and the rule for an even split is written down; when the split happens, the candidate is told that it did and which way the rule ran.

### Expected Effects
- mech.hiring_manager_consensus_impasse keeps operating — panels will split — but stops resolving by default and unrecorded
- The candidate learns the outcome turned on a tie rule, not on a finding about them

### Measurements
- `tie_rule_declared_rate`
- `impasse_disclosure_rate`
summary: Before the panel sits, one member is named as holding the decision and the rule for an even split is written down; when the split happens, the candidate is told that it did and which way the rule ran.
expected_effects: mech.hiring_manager_consensus_impasse keeps operating — panels will split — but stops resolving by default and unrecorded
The candidate learns the outcome turned on a tie rule, not on a finding about them

specimens.label: The rule, written before the panel meets

lines.text: Decider for req #5120: the hiring manager. On an even split the decider decides and records one paragraph of reasons.
Panel 2–2 on system design depth. Decider: no hire. Reason recorded: the two dissenting scores rested on the same unasked follow-up.
To the candidate: the panel did not reach agreement; the decision fell to the named decider under the rule set before the round.

specimens.reading: Panels split, and no rule stops them splitting. What a written rule stops is the split being resolved by whoever is most tired, and then reported outward as a considered judgement about the candidate. The default nobody wrote down is almost always no hire — which means the absence of a rule is itself a rule, and an unstated one.

perspectives.sees: A line to fill in before the panel is scheduled: who decides, and what happens on a tie.
perspectives.reads: The tie rule was always there — it was just never written, and unwritten it defaulted to the outcome that requires nobody to be responsible for it.
perspectives.does: Names the decider, writes the tie rule, and records a paragraph of reasons when the rule is used.

perspectives.sees: A debrief that ends with a recorded decision rather than a second round of scheduling.
perspectives.reads: An impasse used to cost the candidate weeks and produce nothing to send; now it produces a sentence that is true and can be sent the same day.
perspectives.does: Sends the outcome with the fact of the split in it, rather than converting it into a fit narrative.

perspectives.sees: An outcome that says the panel disagreed and a named person decided under a rule fixed beforehand.
perspectives.reads: Being split on is not the same as being found wanting: half the room was on the other side, and what settled it was a rule about ties.
perspectives.does: Reads the result as a close call rather than a verdict, and reapplies where the registry says the same team reopens.

title: Auto-Close Stale Job Requisitions
content:
# Auto-Close Stale Job Requisitions

Implement automated ATS policy to expire public listings when headcount authorisation lapses or no interview activity occurs within 60 days.

### Expected Effects
- mech.stale_or_orphaned_job_requisition stops operating: a listing cannot outlive the authorisation that funded it
- Silence after applying acquires a bound — the record is closed and the closure is sent

### Measurements
- `stale_requisition_rate`
- `closure_latency_days`
summary: Implement automated ATS policy to expire public listings when headcount authorisation lapses or no interview activity occurs within 60 days.
expected_effects: mech.stale_or_orphaned_job_requisition stops operating: a listing cannot outlive the authorisation that funded it
Silence after applying acquires a bound — the record is closed and the closure is sent

specimens.label: The rule, and what it did

lines.text: Policy: expire_listing when headcount_authorisation lapses OR no interview activity for 45 days
req #4471 — last interview activity 47 days ago → listing withdrawn from careers page and aggregators
Candidates with applications in flight: 84 — each notified that the search has closed, with the date.

specimens.reading: The same batch job that produces silent bulk rejections can be pointed at the listing instead of the candidate. The cost is a configuration line.

perspectives.sees: A configuration line, and the count of open requisitions it would withdraw this quarter, on the same cycle where headcount is reviewed.
perspectives.reads: What is being spent is optionality: a listing that closes on a timer cannot be held open while funding is decided, and reopening it runs the approval chain again.
perspectives.does: Sets the interval and what counts as activity, and decides whether a lapsed authorisation withdraws the listing or only flags it for review.

perspectives.sees: Listings dropping off the careers page overnight, and the batch notification going to every application still in flight against them.
perspectives.reads: A requisition closed on a timer is counted as closed rather than filled, and the pipeline built against it is gone if the search restarts.
perspectives.does: Sends the closure notice with the date on it, and asks for the requisition to be reopened where the manager still intends to hire.

perspectives.sees: A message naming the requisition, the date the search closed, and the reason the listing came down.
perspectives.reads: The process ended for a reason that has nothing to do with the application; there is nothing further to wait for and nothing left to infer.
perspectives.does: Closes the file, stops holding capacity for a possible next round, and reapplies if the role is posted again.

perspectives.sees: A customer enabling an expiry rule pointed at the listing, on the same scheduler that already expires unreviewed applications.
perspectives.reads: This is an existing batch capability with a different target rather than new machinery; whether it runs is a customer setting.
perspectives.does: Ships the rule as a configurable option, and its default value decides how many customers ever run it.

title: Bench availability declared at each stage gate
content:
# Bench availability declared at each stage gate

At every advance the search states whether an already-employed engineer between projects could still take the seat, and an external candidate closed out by a bench fill is told so, with the date the availability appeared.

### Expected Effects
- mech.bench_priority_fill keeps operating — it cannot be removed — but stops being read as a verdict on the candidate
- External effort spent against an internally contestable seat becomes countable, and can be priced

### Measurements
- `bench_fill_closure_rate`
- `dated_closure_notice_rate`
summary: At every advance the search states whether an already-employed engineer between projects could still take the seat, and an external candidate closed out by a bench fill is told so, with the date the availability appeared.
expected_effects: mech.bench_priority_fill keeps operating — it cannot be removed — but stops being read as a verdict on the candidate
External effort spent against an internally contestable seat becomes countable, and can be priced

specimens.label: The notice that replaces the alignment letter

lines.text: Backend engineer, req #5120 — the search is closed and why
On 14 March an engineer already employed here came off a project that ended early and was assigned to this seat. The requisition is filled internally as of that date.
Your panel scored above the bar. Nothing in your assessment is the reason this ended, and the scores are held for 12 months against the next opening at this level.

specimens.reading: A company will always prefer an engineer it is already paying, and this does not ask it to stop. It asks the date to be named. The letter costs a paragraph and takes away the only thing the candidate would otherwise have to work with: an inference about their own performance drawn from an event that had nothing to do with it.

perspectives.sees: A field on the requisition recording whether an internal availability is live, and a closure code that distinguishes a bench fill from a hire and from a cancellation.
perspectives.reads: The distinction already exists in the staffing system; what is new is that it reaches the outside. A search that closes internally and is reported as a hire understates how often external effort is spent against a seat that was never contestable.
perspectives.does: Adds the closure code, and requires the date the availability appeared to be carried into the notice.

perspectives.sees: The staffing feed showing a bench engineer assigned to the requisition mid-search, and a pipeline that has to be closed out that day.
perspectives.reads: The close-out is not a judgement to be softened into alignment language — the reason is a date, and writing the date is faster than composing around it.
perspectives.does: Sends the dated notice to everyone still in flight, and records the assessment scores against the next opening rather than discarding them.

perspectives.sees: A dated reason: a seat filled from inside on a day that can be checked against the day the process went quiet.
perspectives.reads: The outcome was decided by an event in someone else's project schedule. There is no performance signal in it to act on, and no version of the interview that would have changed it.
perspectives.does: Stops re-reading the panel for a fault that was not there, and keeps the standing score rather than starting over.

title: Candidate ATS Parser Conformance Test Utility
content:
# Candidate ATS Parser Conformance Test Utility

Provide candidates with an open-source parsing validation tool to verify CV machine-readability before submission.

### Expected Effects
- The candidate can see the extraction before submitting, so an unreadable file is distinguishable from a thin one
- mech.ats_parser_extraction_failure moves from invisible to checkable on the candidate's side of the line

### Measurements
- `parser_extraction_error_rate`
- `ingestion_pass_rate`
summary: Provide candidates with an open-source parsing validation tool to verify CV machine-readability before submission.
expected_effects: The candidate can see the extraction before submitting, so an unreadable file is distinguishable from a thin one
mech.ats_parser_extraction_failure moves from invisible to checkable on the candidate's side of the line

specimens.label: Tool output, before submitting
specimens.subject: hoba-parse-check · cv.pdf

lines.text: Extraction score: 41/100
Work experience entries recovered: 0 of 5 — two-column layout detected
Skills recovered: 0 of 24 — rendered inside a graphic
Suggested: single-column export, text-based headings, skills as plain text.
Re-check after changes: extraction score 93/100, 5 of 5 entries, 24 of 24 skills.

specimens.reading: This is the one intervention on the candidate side of the line. Seeing what the parser sees turns an invisible failure into a fixable file.

perspectives.sees: An extraction report against their own file: how many work entries and skills a parser recovers, and which layout choice dropped them.
perspectives.reads: The failure was in the document rather than in the record, and it is fixable before submission rather than inferable afterwards.
perspectives.does: Re-exports single-column with text headings, re-checks, and submits the version that survives extraction.

perspectives.sees: A complete profile in the queue: work history in fields, skills in fields, orderable against the rest.
perspectives.reads: A profile with nothing in the experience field and a profile whose experience did not extract read identically from here; this removes one of the two before it arrives.
perspectives.does: Screens on the content, and in the applications that still arrive empty, an unreadable file and a thin record remain indistinguishable.

title: Candidate Work Index Submitted With the Application
content:
# Candidate Work Index Submitted With the Application

Submit a one-page index naming each work artefact, the part of it that is the candidate's and the direct path to it, and open that index in the first minutes of the live screen.

### Expected Effects
- mech.portfolio_work_artifact_misinterpretation loses its default: the surface opened is the one the candidate named, with the part that is theirs stated on it
- A contribution held under another organisation arrives as a commit range rather than as something to be discovered
- The index travels with the application, so bar.inbound_screening_triage and bar.technical_screen_live_assessment open the same named artefacts instead of whatever a profile page shows first

### Measurements
- `work_index_attachment_rate`
- `named_artifact_citation_rate`
- `technical_screen_advance_rate`
summary: Submit a one-page index naming each work artefact, the part of it that is the candidate's and the direct path to it, and open that index in the first minutes of the live screen.
expected_effects: mech.portfolio_work_artifact_misinterpretation loses its default: the surface opened is the one the candidate named, with the part that is theirs stated on it
A contribution held under another organisation arrives as a commit range rather than as something to be discovered
The index travels with the application, so bar.inbound_screening_triage and bar.technical_screen_live_assessment open the same named artefacts instead of whatever a profile page shows first

specimens.label: The one-page index, submitted with the application
specimens.subject: Work index — backend: storage and ingest

lines.text: Ingest library, upstream project under a different organisation. Mine: the storage layer rewrite — 40 commits, March to November. The link goes to the commit range, not to the account.
Internal service, not public. What can be shown: the design note with the employer's name removed, and a walkthrough on request.
Five-minute read path: the migration note in /docs, then the fourth commit in the range.
The CV line reads 'storage layer rewrite, upstream ingest library, contributor', so the claim and the path to it sit in one sentence.

specimens.reading: The surface a screener opens is a choice, and the default is a profile page in date order. The index makes that choice, and names which part of each artefact is the candidate's.

perspectives.sees: The surface an application opens on by default — a profile page, a list of repositories in date order — and their own work spread across it in a shape that page does not show.
perspectives.reads: Which surface is opened is decided by what the application carries, and the index is the part of that the candidate writes.
perspectives.does: Names each artefact, the part of it that is theirs and the direct path to it, and opens the index in the first minutes of the live screen instead of leaving the choice of surface to the hour.

perspectives.sees: An index in the application with named artefacts and direct links, alongside the profile link.
perspectives.reads: The minutes available per application go to something already located, and a line in the CV has a path attached that opens in one click.
perspectives.does: Records the note from the named artefact where the index points to one, and from the profile page where the application carries no index.

perspectives.sees: The index in the material the panel receives, with the ownership line and the read path in it.
perspectives.reads: The exercise hour and the evidence of past work stop competing for the same minutes: what to open is stated, so the round is spent on the exercise.
perspectives.does: Reads the named artefact before the session where it is short enough, and asks about that work in the round rather than about the profile.

title: Contractable jurisdictions listed in the posting
content:
# Contractable jurisdictions listed in the posting

The posting names the countries in which the employer can actually issue a contract — through an entity, an employer of record, or a contractor arrangement — so a constraint that no interview can change is known before the first call.

### Expected Effects
- mech.location_or_timezone_compliance_constraint stops being discovered at the offer stage
- A lawful contracting limit becomes distinguishable from a ground that is not one

### Measurements
- `jurisdiction_list_published_rate`
- `late_stage_jurisdiction_rejection_rate`
summary: The posting names the countries in which the employer can actually issue a contract — through an entity, an employer of record, or a contractor arrangement — so a constraint that no interview can change is known before the first call.
expected_effects: mech.location_or_timezone_compliance_constraint stops being discovered at the offer stage
A lawful contracting limit becomes distinguishable from a ground that is not one

specimens.label: The line that goes where "remote" used to be

lines.text: Remote. Contract can be issued in: PL, UA, PT, DE (own entity); ES, RO (employer of record). Nowhere else, including as a contractor.
Overlap required with CET 10:00–15:00. This is a scheduling requirement, not a residence one.
This list is a statement about where we can contract, not about who may work: it is reviewed quarterly and dated below.

specimens.reading: A jurisdiction the employer cannot contract in is a real and lawful constraint, and it is also the one most often discovered at the offer stage. Published, it costs a line. Withheld, it spends the candidate's whole process — and it is indistinguishable from the ground that is not lawful, which is exactly why it has to be stated as a contracting fact with a date on it rather than as a preference about people.

perspectives.sees: The list finance and legal already hold — entities, employer-of-record coverage, and where contracting was declined — rendered into the posting template.
perspectives.reads: Publishing it converts a constraint that currently surfaces as a late rejection into one the market routes around, and it separates a contracting fact from a ground that would not be lawful.
perspectives.does: Publishes the jurisdiction list with a review date, and keeps timezone overlap stated separately from residence.

perspectives.sees: A published list to screen against, instead of a question that has to be asked carefully on the first call.
perspectives.reads: The conversation that used to end a process at week six now does not start one, and the reason given is a fact about the employer rather than about the candidate.
perspectives.does: Points candidates outside the list at the roles that can contract where they live, and stops running processes that cannot end in a contract.

perspectives.sees: A named list of countries and a separate, stated overlap window.
perspectives.reads: Whether this role can exist for them is answered before any effort is spent, and a rejection on this ground later would now be checkable against a published statement.
perspectives.does: Applies where a contract is possible, and treats the overlap window as the negotiable part that it is.

title: Critique injected on script in the collaborative exercise
content:
# Critique injected on script in the collaborative exercise

The collaborative round carries a written script: the same objection is raised at the same point for every candidate, and the panel records what was said in response rather than how the room felt.

### Expected Effects
- mech.communication_or_working_style_friction is measured against a common prompt rather than inferred from an interviewer's chosen one
- Interviewer variance stops entering the verdict as if it were candidate behaviour

### Measurements
- `scripted_prompt_coverage`
- `panel_inter_rater_agreement`
summary: The collaborative round carries a written script: the same objection is raised at the same point for every candidate, and the panel records what was said in response rather than how the room felt.
expected_effects: mech.communication_or_working_style_friction is measured against a common prompt rather than inferred from an interviewer's chosen one
Interviewer variance stops entering the verdict as if it were candidate behaviour

specimens.label: The script, and the line it produces

lines.text: Scripted at minute 18, verbatim for every candidate: "I think this design is wrong — you have put the queue in the wrong place."
Recorded: asked which failure the objection was about; restated the trade-off; proposed moving it and named what that would cost.
Not recorded: tone, warmth, whether the room enjoyed it. The rubric has no column for it, so no column carries it.

specimens.reading: Friction in a collaborative exercise is a real signal, and this does not deny it — it makes it comparable. Unscripted, the objection arrives when an interviewer happens to feel like raising it, in words chosen for that candidate, and what comes back is scored against a memory of how other rounds went. Scripted, the same prompt produces answers that can be set side by side.

perspectives.sees: A one-page script with the objection, the minute it lands, and the three things the answer is scored on.
perspectives.reads: What the panel disagreed about was never the candidate — it was which objection each interviewer raised and how hard. Fixing the prompt leaves only the answer to disagree about.
perspectives.does: Writes the script once per role, and holds the panel to scoring the response rather than the room.

perspectives.sees: An objection that arrives as part of the exercise, and a rubric that names what the answer is being read for.
perspectives.reads: The pushback is the test, not a reaction to something already gone wrong — so it can be answered on the merits instead of managed.
